The person of the sage is the root of this Way; the classics of the sage are the traces of this Way. That whereby the Two Emperors…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以帝天下者此也三王之所以王天下者此
也其載諸經傳如典謨訓誥之文何莫非斯
道之所寓也肆惟我
太祖高皇帝
太宗文皇帝
宣宗章皇帝
聖聖相承繼天立極心帝王之心體帝王之道既
躬行以化導乎民必立言以垂教于世故於
萬幾之暇條成
===
大誥
綸爲善陰隲孝順事實五倫書頒示中外
嘉惠臣民
宸翰奎章輝暎天地玉軸瑤編昭回日月浩乎其
無涯際茫乎其無畔岸考其要歸無非欲人
明五倫以惇道化而已夫五倫一書其載古
今能盡人倫之道者星分胪列雖更僕未能
悉數姑以明問所及者言之君道莫大乎敬
天法祖也莫大乎節儉剛明也若堯之欽若
昊天敬授民時舜之在璇璣以齊七政盤庚
punctuated: 以帝天下者，此也；三王之所以王天下者，此也。其載諸經傳，如典、謨、訓、誥之文，何莫非斯道之所寓也？肆惟我太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝、宣宗章皇帝，聖聖相承，繼天立極，心帝王之心，體帝王之道，既躬行以化導乎民，必立言以垂教于世。故於萬幾之暇，條成《大誥》，綸《爲善陰隲》、《孝順事實》、《五倫書》，頒示中外，嘉惠臣民。宸翰奎章，輝暎天地；玉軸瑤編，昭回日月。浩乎其無涯際，茫乎其無畔岸，考其要歸，無非欲人明五倫以惇道化而已。夫《五倫》一書，其載古今能盡人倫之道者，星分胪列，雖更僕未能悉數。姑以明問所及者言之：君道莫大乎敬天法祖也，莫大乎節儉剛明也。若堯之欽若昊天，敬授民時；舜之在璇璣以齊七政；盤庚
translation_en: … ruled All under Heaven as Emperors was this; that by which the Three Kings ruled All under Heaven as Kings was this. As for what is recorded in the Classics and Commentaries, such as the texts of the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements, how could any of it not be where this Way resides? Thus our Grand Progenitor the High Emperor (Taizu Gao Huangdi), Grand Ancestor the Cultured Emperor (Taizong Wen Huangdi), and Proclaiming Ancestor the Resplendent Emperor (Xuanzong Zhang Huangdi), sage succeeding sage, carried on the work of Heaven and established the Supreme Standard. Making the minds of the former Emperors and Kings their own mind, and embodying the Way of the former Emperors and Kings, having personally practiced it to transform and guide the people, they inevitably established words to hand down teachings to the world. Therefore, in their leisure from the myriad affairs of state, they compiled by article the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao), and imperially composed [?] the Secret Blessings for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), the True Records of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), promulgating them within the court and throughout the realm to bestow favor upon officials and commoners. The imperial brush and starry compositions shine across heaven and earth; the jade rollers and precious compilations revolve brightly like the sun and moon. Vast and boundless, immense and shoreless—yet if we examine their essential aim, it is nothing other than wishing people to understand the five human relationships so as to thicken moral transformation. Now, in this single work, the Book of the Five Human Relationships, those from antiquity to the present recorded as having fulfilled the Way of human relationships are arrayed like stars; even if one were to change attendants from exhaustion, one could not recount them all. Let me speak provisionally of those touched upon in the brilliant question: in the Way of the Ruler, nothing is greater than revering Heaven and modeling oneself on the ancestors, and nothing is greater than frugality, firmness, and discernment. For instance, Yao’s reverently conforming to vast Heaven and respectfully bestowing the seasons upon the people; Shun’s examining the pearl-adorned turning sphere to put in order the Seven Directors; Pan Geng’s…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
行湯之政成王繼序不忘此其敬天法祖盜
與我
太祖之遇旱憂震徒步請禱
太宗之繼承天位恪遵成憲者同一道焉禹之
食惡衣周文之卑服即功武帝斥田蚡之
孝宣辨燕王之誣此其節儉剛明蓋與我
太祖之不作苑臺以費民財
太宗之辨民交通特釋其非者同一揆焉以臣道
言之莫先於守法持正也莫先於忠義廉介
===
也如犯蹕之止於罰金不肯順旨故入必正
以賍罪不徇私恩非張釋之蘇章之守法乎
龍闘淯淵力拒禳祟之請帝欲廢立廷爭而
不奉詔非子産周昌之持正乎至如我
朝來亥文為天策知事守將欲擅殺人而力爭
其不可卒蒙賚予之榮較諸張釋之蘇章之
輩何讓拒蘇峻之逆賊而父死於忠子死於
孝當祿山之不道而兄死於前弟死於後此
卞壼顏杲卿之忠義也以不貪為寶而不寳
punctuated: 行湯之政，成王繼序不忘，此其敬天法祖，盜與我太祖之遇旱憂震、徒步請禱，太宗之繼承天位、恪遵成憲者，同一道焉。禹之菲食惡衣，周文之卑服即功，武帝斥田蚡之請，孝宣辨燕王之誣，此其節儉剛明，蓋與我太祖之不作苑臺以費民財，太宗之辨民交通、特釋其非者，同一揆焉。以臣道言之，莫先於守法持正也，莫先於忠義廉介也。如犯蹕之止於罰金，不肯順旨故入；必正以賍罪，不徇私恩，非張釋之、蘇章之守法乎？龍闘淯淵，力拒禳祟之請；帝欲廢立，廷爭而不奉詔，非子産、周昌之持正乎？至如我朝來亥文為天策知事，守將欲擅殺人而力爭其不可，卒蒙賚予之榮，較諸張釋之、蘇章之輩何讓？拒蘇峻之逆賊，而父死於忠、子死於孝；當祿山之不道，而兄死於前、弟死於後，此卞壼、顏杲卿之忠義也。以不貪為寶而不寳
translation_en:
… practiced the governance of Tang, and King Cheng continued the royal line without forgetting. In their reverence for Heaven and emulation of ancestors, these indeed share the same Way as our Taizu, who, distressed and alarmed upon encountering drought, walked on foot to pray for rain, and Taizong, who succeeded to the heavenly throne and respectfully abided by the established institutions. Yu's eating simple food and wearing coarse clothes [note: text omits 菲 before 食], King Wen of Zhou's wearing humble garments and devoting himself to work, Emperor Wu's rejecting the request of Tian Fen [note: text omits 請], and Emperor Xiaoxuan's discerning the false accusation of the King of Yan—in their frugality, firmness, and perspicacity, these share the same principle as our Taizu, who refused to build parks and terraces that would waste the people's wealth, and Taizong, who investigated the people accused of illicit collusion and specially absolved them of wrongdoing.

Speaking of the Way of the minister, nothing comes before upholding the law and maintaining rectitude, and nothing comes before loyalty, righteousness, and incorruptible integrity. For instance, imposing only a fine of gold for violating the imperialprocession and refusing to bend to the imperial will to deliberately inflict a heavier penalty; or insisting on punishing the crime of bribery according to law without yielding to private favor—was this not the upholding of the law by Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 and Su Zhang 蘇章? When dragons fought in the Yu Abyss, forcefully rejecting the request to perform exorcistic sacrifices; or when the Emperor wished to depose and replace the Heir Apparent, arguing at court and refusing to carry out the edict—was this not the maintaining of rectitude by Zichan 子產 and Zhou Chang 周昌? As for our dynasty, when Zhu Wen 朱文 [transcribed as 來亥文(?)] served as Administrative Aide (zhishi) of the Tiance Guard, the garrison commander wanted to kill someone without authorization, and he forcefully argued that it was impermissible, ultimately receiving the honor of imperial rewards—how does he yield anything when compared to the likes of Zhang Shizhi and Su Zhang? Resisting the rebel bandit Su Jun 蘇峻 so that the father died in loyalty and the sons died in filial piety; or facing the wickedness of An Lushan 安祿山 so that the elder brother died first and the younger brother died after—this was the loyalty and righteousness of Bian Kun 卞壼 and Yan Gaoqing 顏杲卿. Taking non-covetousness as one's treasure rather than treasuring…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
金玉以清白遺子孫而不計產業此司城子
罕司徒楊震之廉介也至若我
朝孫炎為處州總制禁縣之徒欲脅以降而罵
賊以死終獲爵土之封較諸卞壼顏杲卿之
儔何亞古者百里負米之仲由名有家法之
公綽與今之母病不愈吮疽嘗糞之李英親
沒哀慟疏食廬墓之張翼同一父子之盡道
也可知古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺不忘糟
糠之宋弘與今之夫溺水而自投二屍並出
===
之袁氏夫死不嫁雙節並稱之俞氏同一夫
婦之盡道也可見若趙孝趙禮之爭死不懼
逆式張元之雖死不易以至不肯分財異居
隨所欲取之李貞非古今能盡兄弟朋友之
倫者乎然以五倫一書質之於
大誥孝順事實為善陰隲三書之旨則
大誥所載君臣同遊者非五倫書所謂盡君臣之
道者乎孝順事實所載武王之達孝非五倫
書所謂盡父子之倫者乎為善陰隲所載馮
punctuated:
金玉，以清白遺子孫而不計產業，此司城子罕、司徒楊震之廉介也。至若我朝孫炎為處州總制，禁縣之徒欲脅以降，而罵賊以死，終獲爵土之封，較諸卞壼、顏杲卿之儔何亞？古者百里負米之仲由、名有家法之公綽，與今之母病不愈吮疽嘗糞之李英、親沒哀慟疏食廬墓之張翼，同一父子之盡道也可知。古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺、不忘糟糠之宋弘，與今之夫溺水而自投二屍並出之袁氏、夫死不嫁雙節並稱之俞氏，同一夫婦之盡道也可見。若趙孝、趙禮之爭死不懼，逆式、張元之雖死不易，以至不肯分財異居、隨所欲取之李貞，非古今能盡兄弟、朋友之倫者乎？
然以《五倫》一書質之於《大誥》、《孝順事實》、《為善陰隲》三書之旨：則《大誥》所載「君臣同遊」者，非《五倫書》所謂盡君臣之道者乎？《孝順事實》所載「武王之達孝」，非《五倫書》所謂盡父子之倫者乎？《為善陰隲》所載馮
translation_en:
…gold and jade, and leaving spotless integrity to one's descendants without calculating family property—this was the incorruptible rectitude of Minister of Works Zihan 子罕 and Minister over the Masses Yang Zhen 楊震. As for our dynasty, when Sun Yan 孫炎 served as Regional Commander of Chuzhou 處州, the rebels He [transcription has 禁, error for 賀] Ren and his ilk [transcription has 縣之徒, for 賀仁德之徒?] [?] sought to coerce him into surrender, yet he cursed the bandits and died, ultimately receiving an enfeoffment of noble rank and territory; compared with the likes of Bian Kun 卞壼 and Yan Gaoqing 顏杲卿, how was he any inferior? That in antiquity Zhong You 仲由, who carried rice on his back from a hundred li away, and Liu Gongchuo 柳公綽, who was renowned for his family discipline, share with Li Ying 李英 of the present day—who sucked pus from an ulcer and tasted feces when his mother's illness did not heal—and Zhang Yi 張翼—who grieved bitterly when his parents died, ate coarse food, and dwelt in a hut by their grave—the same fulfillment of the Way of father and son can thus be known. That in antiquity Ji Que 冀缺, where husband and wife treated each other with the respect due a guest, and Song Hong 宋弘, who did not forget the wife who had shared his husks and mash, share with Lady Yuan 袁氏 of the present day—whose husband drowned and who threw herself into the water so that their two corpses emerged side by side—and the Ladies Yu 俞氏—who refused to remarry after their husbands died and were jointly praised for their double chastity—the same fulfillment of the Way of husband and wife can thus be seen. As for Zhao Xiao 趙孝 and Zhao Li 趙禮 contending with each other to die without fear, Fan Shi 范式 [transcription has 逆式] [?] and Zhang劭 (Zhang Yuanbo 張元伯) [transcription has 張元] not changing their word even in death, down to Li Zhen 李貞 of our time, who refused to divide the family property and live apart and let his brothers take whatever they wished—are these not men of ancient and modern times who were able to fulfill the moral relations of older and younger brother and of friends?

Yet if we examine this single book, the Book of the Five Moral Relations (Wulun shu 五倫書), against the purport of the three books—the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥), the True Cases of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實), and the Secret Blessings of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰隲): then is not "Ruler and Minister Roaming Together" recorded in the Grand Pronouncements what the Book of the Five Moral Relations calls fulfilling the Way of ruler and minister? Is not the "Far-Reaching Filial Piety of King Wu" recorded in the True Cases of Filial Piety what the Book of the Five Moral Relations calls fulfilling the moral relation of father and son? Are not the accounts recorded in the Secret Blessings of Doing Good of Feng…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
式娶督叔通娶啞不與五倫書所謂盡夫婦
之道者同一意歟是則五倫之理包天括地
而是書足以該之三書之旨殊塗異轍而是
書足以會之溥天率土不實爲號之弓而寶
此書四方萬國不藏曲阜之履而藏此書斯
世斯民得以盡彝倫惇道化熙熙然於光天
化日之下可以匹休唐虞三代之治者豈無
所自
第二問
===
楊廉
同考試官學正陳　批〔歎對詳明必熟於大學衍義者也策學如此場屋幾人〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔條答無遺且忠愛之意溢於言表蓋久學而有志者懋歆羨歆羨〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔答問詳悉非熟於衍義者不能〕
對甚矣天下不可一日無大學之書而衍義
一書亦不可以一日不講也脩己治人之道
於焉而存化民成俗之本於焉而在涵養君
punctuated:
式娶督、叔通娶啞，不與《五倫書》所謂盡夫婦之道者同一意歟？是則五倫之理，包天括地，而是書足以該之；三書之旨，殊塗異轍，而是書足以會之。溥天率土，不實爲號之弓而寶此書；四方萬國，不藏曲阜之履而藏此書。斯世斯民，得以盡彝倫、惇道化，熙熙然於光天化日之下，可以匹休唐虞三代之治者，豈無所自？

第二問
楊廉
同考試官學正陳　批〔歎對詳明，必熟於《大學衍義》者也。策學如此，場屋幾人！〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔條答無遺，且忠愛之意溢於言表，蓋久學而有志者懋。歆羨，歆羨！〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔答問詳悉，非熟於《衍義》者不能。〕

對：甚矣，天下不可一日無《大學》之書，而《衍義》一書亦不可以一日不講也！脩己治人之道於焉而存，化民成俗之本於焉而在，涵養君
translation_en:
…[Feng] Shi marrying a blind woman [? 督 for 瞽] and Shutong marrying a mute woman—do these not share the exact same meaning as what the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) calls fulfilling the way of husband and wife? Thus, the principles of the five human relationships encompass heaven and earth, and this book suffices to embrace them all; the purports of the three books follow different paths and tracks, yet this book suffices to unite them. Throughout the whole world, down to the borders of the land, people do not treasure the Wuhao bow [? 實爲號之弓 for 寶烏號之弓], but treasure this book; across the four quarters and the myriad states, people do not store away the shoes of Qufu, but store away this book. That this age and this people are able to fulfill the constant human relationships, strengthen moral transformation, and live in harmonious prosperity beneath a bright sky and transforming sun—matching the splendid rule of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—how could this be without a source?

Question 2
Yang Lian 楊廉
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Chen 陳, comments: [An admirable [? 歎 for 敷] response, detailed and clear; he must be someone thoroughly familiar with the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi). With policy learning like this, how many in the examination compound can match him!]
Examiner, District Instructor Wu 吾, comments: [He answers point by point without omission, and sentiments of loyalty and affection overflow beyond his words; truly the effort [? 懋] of one who has studied long and possesses high aspirations. Admirable, admirable!]
Examiner, District Instructor Zhao 趙, comments: [His answers to the questions are detailed and thorough; no one who is not thoroughly familiar with the Extended Meaning could achieve this.]

Reply: Indeed, the world cannot go a single day without the book of the Great Learning (Daxue), and the book Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning] (Yanyi) likewise cannot go a single day without being expounded! The way of cultivating oneself and governing others is preserved therein; the foundation of transforming the people and perfecting customs resides therein; and the nourishment of the ruler's…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
德緝熙聖學亦莫不於是而基學者一日不
由乎此則流於異端惑於邪說無以開發聰
明而措諸事業君天下者一日不由於此則
身有不脩化有不行而天下不得蒙至治之
澤此西山真文忠公衍義之所以作而執事
之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟愚雖不敏敢不
紬繹舊聞以答明問之萬一乎夫大學一書
其經出於孔氏其傳出於曾子二程爲之表
章朱子爲之章句綱領條目畢備無遺誠聖
===
賢進德之閫奥君天下者之律例格令後世
莫能尚已至宋真文忠公當理宗之朝圖致
治之道以爲治道莫大於大學於是首𠛬聖
賢性命道德之言旁采古今治亂安危之迹
推本帝王爲治之序探求帝王爲學之本詳
著格物致知誠意正心脩身齊家之要而及
其目以爲衍義一書其所以闡義理之淵微
發聖賢之未發爲帝王之監戒豈小補哉觀
其述帝堯克明峻德而致黎民於變皐謨身
punctuated: 德，緝熙聖學，亦莫不於是而基。學者一日不由乎此，則流於異端，惑於邪說，無以開發聰明而措諸事業；君天下者一日不由於此，則身有不脩，化有不行，而天下不得蒙至治之澤。此西山真文忠公《衍義》之所以作，而執事之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟？愚雖不敏，敢不紬繹舊聞，以答明問之萬一乎？夫《大學》一書，其經出於孔氏，其傳出於曾子，二程爲之表章，朱子爲之章句，綱領條目，畢備無遺，誠聖賢進德之閫奥，君天下者之律例格令，後世莫能尚已。至宋真文忠公，當理宗之朝，圖致治之道，以爲治道莫大於《大學》，於是首𠛬聖賢性命道德之言，旁采古今治亂安危之迹，推本帝王爲治之序，探求帝王爲學之本，詳著格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家之要，而及其目，以爲《衍義》一書。其所以闡義理之淵微，發聖賢之未發，爲帝王之監戒，豈小補哉？觀其述帝堯克明峻德而致黎民於變，《皐謨》「身…
translation_en:
…virtue and bringing radiant continuity to sagely learning likewise have their foundation nowhere if not here. If scholars do not follow this for even a single day, they drift into heterodoxy and are deluded by perverse doctrines, having no means to develop their intelligence or put it into practice in their endeavors. If one who rules the world does not follow this for even a single day, his person will go uncultivated, his transforming influence will not take effect, and the world will be unable to receive the blessings of supreme governance. Is this not why Zhen Wenzhonggong 真文忠公 [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] of Xishan 西山 composed the Extended Meaning (Yanyi 衍義), and why Your Excellency so earnestly questions us students about it? Though I am愚鈍 [slow-witted], how could I dare not draw out what I have previously learned in order to answer even a ten-thousandth part of your discerning inquiry?

Now as for the book of the Great Learning (Daxue 大學), its Classic (Jing 經) came from Confucius, and its Commentary (Zhuan 傳) came from Zengzi 曾子. The two Cheng 程 brothers brought it to prominence, and Master Zhu 朱子 [Zhu Xi 朱熹] divided it into chapters and phrases (Zhangju 章句). Its overarching principles and specific items are complete without omission; truly it is the inner sanctum for sages and worthies in advancing their virtue, and the statutes, precedents, and ordinances for one who rules the world, which later ages cannot surpass. When it came to Zhen Wenzhonggong of the Song dynasty, serving during the reign of Emperor Lizong 理宗, he planned out the way to bring about good governance. Believing that nothing in the way of governance is greater than the Great Learning, he thereupon placed at the head [?; 𠛬] the words of sages and worthies on human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue, and extensively gathered the traces of order and disorder, security and danger from antiquity to the present. He traced back the fundamental sequence by which emperors and kings govern, and sought out the root of how emperors and kings pursue learning. He set forth in detail the essentials of investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, and regulating the family, along with their subsidiary items, to make the book Extended Meaning. In elucidating the profound subtleties of moral principle, bringing to light what the sages and worthies had left unexpressed, and serving as a mirror and warning for emperors and kings, how could this be a mere minor supplement?

Observe how he recounts Emperor Yao's 堯 ability to make bright his lofty virtue and thereby bring the black-haired people to transformation, and the "Counsels of Gao Yao" (Gaomo 皐謨) on "cultivating the person…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩思永邇可遠在茲與夫四海雖遠致治
在心之語則帝王爲治之序可知矣述伊訓
太甲立愛惟親立敬惟長以終於四海詩美
文王刑于寡妻至于兄弟以御于家邦與夫
治天下有本身之謂也之言又豈不可見其
序哉其述堯舜禹湯文武或執中懋德或宅
心建極以至勉彊學問行道之辭則帝王爲
學之本可知矣述漢唐魏陳諸君或以王霸
雜治或以音律爲高以至或專文賦游宴之
===
樂夫豈得其本哉其格物致知之要曰明道
術其目則天理人心之正吾道源流之正異
端之差王霸之異也而審治體非在分德刑
先後別義利輕重乎曰辨人材其目則聖賢
觀人之法帝王知人之事姦雄之術憸邪之
情也而察民情非在生靈嚮背田里休戚乎
若夫誠意正心之要曰崇畏敬則崇脩已事
天之敬崇遇灾臨民之敬及夫操存省察之
功規警箴戒之助也曰戒逸欲則戒沈湎于
punctuated: 脩思永、邇可遠在茲，與夫「四海雖遠，致治在心」之語，則帝王爲治之序可知矣；述《伊訓》「太甲立愛惟親，立敬惟長，以終於四海」，《詩》美文王「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦」，與夫「治天下有本，身之謂也」之言，又豈不可見其序哉？其述堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，或執中懋德，或宅心建極，以至勉彊學問行道之辭，則帝王爲學之本可知矣；述漢、唐、魏、陳諸君，或以王霸雜治，或以音律爲高，以至或專文賦游宴之樂，夫豈得其本哉？其格物致知之要，曰「明道術」，其目則天理人心之正、吾道源流之正、異端之差、王霸之異也；而「審治體」，非在分德刑先後、別義利輕重乎？曰「辨人材」，其目則聖賢觀人之法、帝王知人之事、姦雄之術、憸邪之情也；而「察民情」，非在生靈嚮背、田里休戚乎？若夫誠意正心之要，曰「崇畏敬」，則崇脩已事天之敬、崇遇灾臨民之敬，及夫操存省察之功、規警箴戒之助也；曰「戒逸欲」，則戒沈湎于
translation_en: … cultivating the person with thoughts of perpetuity, whereby starting from the near one can reach the distant, along with his remark that "though the Four Seas are distant, bringing about good governance lies in the mind," then the proper sequence of governance for emperors and kings can be known. When he recounts the Instructions of Yi (Yi xun) on Tai Jia—"establishing love begins with kin, establishing respect begins with elders, and ends throughout the Four Seas"—and the Book of Odes (Shi) praising King Wen—"setting an example for his consort, extending to his brothers, and so governing his family and state"—along with the saying that "governing the world has a root: it is called the person," how could one not see this sequence? When he recounts Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—whether holding fast to the Mean and exerting themselves in virtue, or settling their minds and establishing the supreme standard, down to words on striving in study, inquiry, and practicing the Way—then the fundamental basis of learning for emperors and kings can be known. And when he recounts the various rulers of the Han, Tang, Wei, and Chen dynasties—some governing by mixing the Kingly Way with that of the Hegemon, some prizing musical pitch-pipes as lofty, and some devoting themselves solely to the pleasures of literary compositions, excursions, and banquets—how could they have grasped that fundamental basis? As for his essentials of investigating things and extending knowledge: one is called "clarifying the Way and its methods," whose specific items are the correctness of Heavenly Principle and the human mind, the orthodoxy of the origin and transmission of our Way, the errors of heterodoxies, and the distinction between the Kingly Way and the Way of the Hegemon; and as for "examining the substance of governance," does it not lie in distinguishing the priority of virtue and punishment, and differentiating the relative weight of righteousness and profit? Another is called "discerning men of talent," whose specific items are the methods by which sages and worthies observe men, the affairs by which emperors and kings know men, the arts of treacherous opportunists, and the dispositions of sycophantic and wicked men; and as for "investigating the conditions of the people," does it not lie in the allegiance or estrangement of the living populace, and the joys and sorrows of the rural villages? As for the essentials of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind: one is called "revering awe and respect," which consists in revering respect in cultivating oneself and serving Heaven, revering respect when encountering calamities and facing the people, as well as the effort of holding fast to the mind and self-examination, and the aid of admonition, warning, and remonstrance; the other is called "guarding against indolence and desires," which consists in guarding against wallowing in…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
酒戒荒淫於色及夫盤逸游田之戒窮奢極
修之戒也謹言行為脩身之要則發號施令
之際其可以不慎正威儀為脩身之要則在
宮在廷之容不可以不謹若夫齊家之要不
外乎重妃匹嚴內治也謹選立之道賴規警
之益以至內臣忠謹之福非其目而何又不
外乎定國本教戚屬建立之討宜蚤諭教之
法宜豫以至外家驕溢之禍非其目而何夫
大學之綱目如彼其大而詳衍義之具載又
如此其備而切信矣哉聖賢進德之方帝王
致治之道不可一日無者也雖然明大學之
道在致知推大學之道在力行而所以致知
力行之方則又在一敬而已愚生於此實踐
之功固有所未盡而探討之功則未嘗不力
倘蒙執事與而進之使得立
玉階寸地續
翠幄一貂敢不以平生所學竭涓埃以助
海嶽之萬一乎謹對
punctuated: 酒，戒荒淫於色，及夫盤逸游田之戒、窮奢極修之戒也。謹言行為脩身之要，則發號施令之際，其可以不慎？正威儀為脩身之要，則在宮在廷之容，不可以不謹。若夫齊家之要，不外乎重妃匹、嚴內治也。謹選立之道，賴規警之益，以至內臣忠謹之福，非其目而何？又不外乎定國本、教戚屬。建立之討宜蚤，諭教之法宜豫，以至外家驕溢之禍，非其目而何？夫《大學》之綱目如彼其大而詳，《衍義》之具載又如此其備而切。信矣哉！聖賢進德之方，帝王致治之道，不可一日無者也。雖然，明《大學》之道在致知，推《大學》之道在力行，而所以致知力行之方，則又在一敬而已。愚生於此，實踐之功固有所未盡，而探討之功則未嘗不力。倘蒙執事與而進之，使得立玉階寸地，續翠幄一貂，敢不以平生所學，竭涓埃以助海嶽之萬一乎？謹對。
translation_en:
…wine, guarding against debauchery in sensual pleasures, as well as the warnings against idleness, touring, and hunting, and the warnings against extreme extravagance and luxury [?修 for 侈]. Being cautious in speech and conduct is an essential of cultivating the personal life; when issuing commands and promulgating orders, how could one not be careful? Rectifying one's dignified demeanor is an essential of cultivating the personal life; one's deportment inside the palace and at court must not lack circumspection.

As for the essentials of regulating the family, they are nothing other than attaching importance to the royal consort and strictly governing the inner palace. Being careful in the way of selecting and installing the consort, relying on the benefit of her admonition and warning, down to the blessings of loyalty and circumspection among palace eunuchs—what are these if not its detailed items? Furthermore, they are nothing other than establishing the foundation of the state [the heir apparent] and instructing imperial relatives by marriage. The deliberation [?討 for 計] on establishing the heir should be done early, and the method of his instruction and guidance should be prepared in advance, down to the calamities of arrogance and excess among the consort clans—what are these if not its detailed items?

Now, the main principles and detailed items of the Great Learning (Daxue) are as grand and detailed as that, and what is fully recorded in the Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning] (Yanyi) is as comprehensive and pertinent as this. Truly indeed, as the method by which sages and worthies advance in virtue, and the way by which emperors and kings bring about good governance, they cannot be dispensed with for a single day! Nevertheless, illuminating the way of the Great Learning lies in extending knowledge, carrying out the way of the Great Learning lies in strenuous practice, and the method by which one extends knowledge and engages in strenuous practice lies simply in a single word: reverence (jing).

In this regard, although your foolish student has admittedly not exhausted the work of practical implementation, in the work of investigation and inquiry I have never failed to exert my strength. Should I be favored by Your Excellency's approval and advancement, so that I am permitted to stand on an inch of ground at the Jade Steps and add a sable tail behind the Kingfisher Curtains [i.e., serve at court], how would I dare not take what I have learned all my life and exhaust my tiny drops and grains of dust to assist the vast seas and lofty mountains in even one part in ten thousand? I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第三問
同考試官學正張　批〔治教一策關涉甚大此作識〕
〔見善措置而又不失治教之本用世之士也高薦〕
何疑
考試官教諭吾　批〔策有處置非識義理通時務〕
〔者不能錄出之當〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔究政教之要的時措之宜可〕
〔謂達於治體者表而出之〕
王佐
===
君天下者莫先於爲政而立教成政教者必
本於制禮以作樂蓋政教不舉固不足以言
治禮樂不脩又何以爲政教之本君天下者
可不知所本乎執事以此爲問其期待愚生
以用世之意非淺淺也敢不援古據今以對
夫禮以辨上下樂以和民情虞之禮樂本於
帝舜之德而典以夷夔三禮脩而五禮明六
律和而八音諧後世固莫能尚矣然禮緣人
情樂隨風氣而損益先生之舊以備一代之
punctuated:
第三問

同考試官學正張　批〔治教一策，關涉甚大，此作識見善措置，而又不失治教之本，用世之士也，高薦〕何疑？
考試官教諭吾　批〔策有處置，非識義理、通時務者不能，錄出之，當。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔究政教之要，的時措之宜，可謂達於治體者，表而出之。〕

王佐

君天下者，莫先於爲政而立教；成政教者，必本於制禮以作樂。蓋政教不舉，固不足以言治；禮樂不脩，又何以爲政教之本？君天下者，可不知所本乎？執事以此爲問，其期待愚生以用世之意，非淺淺也，敢不援古據今以對！夫禮以辨上下，樂以和民情。虞之禮樂，本於帝舜之德，而典以夷、夔；三禮脩而五禮明，六律和而八音諧，後世固莫能尚矣。然禮緣人情，樂隨風氣，而損益先生之舊，以備一代之
translation_en:
Third Policy Question

Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Zhang, comments: "This policy question on governance and moral transformation touches upon matters of great importance. This essay shows discerning insight and skillful practical arrangements without losing sight of the root of governance and instruction. He is a scholar useful to the world—what doubt could there be in recommending him highly?"
Examiner, County Director of Studies Wu, comments: "The policy essay offers practical arrangements that no one could produce without understanding moral principles and being versed in current affairs. Selecting it for publication is fitting."
Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhao, comments: "It investigates the essentials of administration and instruction and hits upon what is appropriate for timely implementation. He may be called one who understands the fundamental structure of governance; we single it out for publication."

Wang Zuo

For one who rules the world, nothing takes precedence over conducting administration and establishing moral instruction; and for one who brings administration and instruction to completion, it must be rooted in instituting rites and creating music. Indeed, if administration and instruction are not upheld, it is certainly insufficient to speak of good governance; yet if rites and music are not cultivated, wherewith can one establish the root of administration and instruction? Can one who rules the world fail to know where the root lies? By asking about this, Your Excellency's expectation that this foolish student be of service to the world is by no means shallow; how dare I not cite antiquity and draw upon the present in reply! Now, rites serve to distinguish superior and inferior, and music serves to harmonize the feelings of the people. The rites and music of Yu were rooted in the virtue of Emperor Shun and administered by Boyi and Kui; the three rites were cultivated and the five rites made clear, the six pitch-pipes were harmonized and the eight timbres brought into accord, so that later ages could certainly never surpass them. title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
制者不能不有待於周公也周之禮樂成於
周公之手而典以宗伯有五禮以親邦民六
樂以和神人後世固莫能加矣然聖王不作
禮樂廢壞而斟酌先王之制以為萬世之法
者不能不有假於孔子也厥後嬴秦無道典
籍煨燼禮之亡也著者非一家若曾褒之漢
禮韋公肅之新儀王彥威之曲臺惟陳太常
之禮書辯論精博雖識者所愛然較之文公
家禮諱名分崇愛敬以為之本畧浮文務本實
===
以為之用者則不及焉今禮司於春官行於
朝廷之上者郁郁乎其盛可以匹休於虞周矣
而冠昏喪祭之典頒在有司燦然備具然民
間行之有未周者特以承亘者有未至而勢
未能革其因襲之弊也樂之亡也論者非一
葉若聶冠卿之樂圖胡瑗之樂記房庶之補
亡惟陳正字之樂書綱羅綜貫雖識者所許
然比之蔡氏新書本原器數之成備辭約理
明之易曉者則未若焉今樂司於太常奏於
punctuated: 制者，不能不有待於周公也。周之禮樂，成於周公之手，而典以宗伯。有五禮以親邦民，六樂以和神人，後世固莫能加矣。然聖王不作，禮樂廢壞，而斟酌先王之制，以為萬世之法者，不能不有假於孔子也。厥後嬴秦無道，典籍煨燼。禮之亡也，著者非一家，若曾褒之《漢禮》、韋公肅之《新儀》、王彥威之《曲臺》，惟陳太常之《禮書》，辯論精博，雖識者所愛，然較之文公《家禮》，諱名分、崇愛敬以為之本，畧浮文、務本實以為之用者，則不及焉。今禮司於春官，行於朝廷之上者，郁郁乎其盛，可以匹休於虞、周矣。而冠昏喪祭之典，頒在有司，燦然備具。然民間行之有未周者，特以承亘者有未至，而勢未能革其因襲之弊也。樂之亡也，論者非一葉，若聶冠卿之《樂圖》、胡瑗之《樂記》、房庶之《補亡》，惟陳正字之《樂書》，綱羅綜貫，雖識者所許，然比之蔡氏《新書》，本原器數之成備，辭約理明之易曉者，則未若焉。今樂司於太常，奏於
translation_en:
… the institutions [of a dynasty] could not but await the Duke of Zhou. The rites and music of the Zhou were brought to completion by the hand of the Duke of Zhou and were administered by the Minister of Rites (Zongbo). There were the Five Rites to bring harmony to the people of the realm, and the Six Musical Dances to harmonize spirits and men; later generations indeed could add nothing to them. Yet when sage-kings no longer arose and rites and music fell into decay, weighing and adapting the institutions of the former kings to establish a model for ten thousand generations could not but rely upon Confucius.

Thereafter, the Ying clan of Qin acted without the Way, and the canonical records were reduced to ashes. Following the loss of the rites, those who wrote on them were not of a single school—such as Zeng Bao [Cao Bao 曹褒?] with his Rites of Han (Hanli), Wei Gongsu with his New Ceremonials (Xinyi), and Wang Yanwei with his Qu Tai [Rites] (Qutai). Only the Treatise on Rites (Lishu) by Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chen [Chen Xiangdao 陳祥道] argues with precision and breadth; though cherished by men of discernment, when compared to the Family Rituals (Jiali) of Lord Wen [Zhu Xi 朱熹]—which takes strictness [諱, for 謹?] regarding status and duty and the exaltation of love and reverence as its foundation, and the setting aside of superficial ornament and devotion to fundamental substance as its application—it falls short. Today, the rites administered by the Ministry of Rites (Chunguan) and practiced at court are resplendent in their flourishing, worthy of matching the glories of Yu [Shun] and Zhou. Moreover, the canons of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice have been promulgated to the authorities, brilliantly complete. Yet if their practice among the people is not yet comprehensive, it is merely because those who disseminate them [承亘, for 承宣?] have not yet done so fully, and circumstances have not yet allowed the eradication of entrenched abuses.

Following the loss of music, those who discussed it were not of a single generation [葉, or school 家?]—such as Nie Guanqing with his Diagrams of Music (Yuetu), Hu Yuan with his Record of Music (Yueji), and Fang Shu with his Supplement to the Lost Texts (Buwang). Only the Treatise on Music (Yueshu) by Proofreader Chen [Chen Yang 陳暘] encompasses and synthesizes the material comprehensively; though praised by men of discernment, when compared to the New Treatise (Xinshu) of Master Cai [Cai Yuanding 蔡元定]—in which fundamental principles, instruments, and mathematical proportions are all complete, and whose concise words and clear principles are easy to understand—it does not equal it. Today, the music administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and performed…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之上者洋洋乎其盛可以追美於韶武矣
而聲音器數之制布在有司井然有條然民
間之音律有未協者特以奉行者有未盡耳
力亦未能振其誠和之俗也夫國以民爲本
而民之師師則守令也古之守令若龔遂之
化盜黃霸之寬和卓茂之愛民魯恭之三異
其見稱於世也尚矣今守令之選多出賢科
其於牧民之道視四子宜不多讓矣以才質
有高下民俗有淳漓其間非棘而勢則寬而
===
漫其民力尚疲而卓成之績未著者職此故
也國以兵爲衛而兵之統御則將帥也古之
將帥若吳起之治兵王翦之善戰廉頗之勇
氣李牧之備邊其見稱於人也久矣今將帥
之選類出世冑其於治兵之道視四子當有
所加焉以綺紈叙蔭之徒御夫游逸不練之
兵又加之以非貪而刻則縱而弛其智勇尚
少而決勝之策猶有未見者職此由也方今
聖天子在上而於禮樂兵民四者惓惓注意然而
punctuated:
朝廷之上者，洋洋乎其盛，可以追美於《韶》、《武》矣。而聲音、器數之制，布在有司，井然有條。然民間之音律有未協者，特以奉行者有未盡耳，力亦未能振其誠和之俗也。
夫國以民爲本，而民之師師則守令也。古之守令，若龔遂之化盜、黃霸之寬和、卓茂之愛民、魯恭之三異，其見稱於世也尚矣。今守令之選，多出賢科，其於牧民之道，視四子宜不多讓矣。以才質有高下，民俗有淳漓，其間非棘而勢，則寬而漫，其民力尚疲而卓成之績未著者，職此故也。
國以兵爲衛，而兵之統御則將帥也。古之將帥，若吳起之治兵、王翦之善戰、廉頗之勇氣、李牧之備邊，其見稱於人也久矣。今將帥之選，類出世冑，其於治兵之道，視四子當有所加焉。以綺紈叙蔭之徒，御夫游逸不練之兵，又加之以非貪而刻，則縱而弛，其智勇尚少而決勝之策猶有未見者，職此由也。
方今聖天子在上，而於禮樂、兵民四者惓惓注意，然而
translation_en:
… the imperial court, so grand in its flourishing, can rival the beauty of the Shao and Wu music. Moreover, the regulations regarding sounds, notes, instruments, and measures have been promulgated among the authorities in perfect order. Yet if the musical pitches among the populace are not yet in harmony, it is merely because those who implement them have not yet done so to the fullest; nor has their strength been able to rouse customs of sincere harmony.

Now, the state takes the people as its foundation, and the leaders of the people are the prefects and magistrates. As for the prefects and magistrates of antiquity—such as Gong Sui 龔遂 in transforming bandits, Huang Ba 黃霸 in his leniency and harmony, Zhuo Mao 卓茂 in his love for the people, and Lu Gong 魯恭 with his Three Marvels—they have been praised by the world for ages. Today, those selected as prefects and magistrates mostly come from the ranks of the examination graduates; in the way of shepherding the people, compared to those four masters, they ought not to yield much. Yet because natural talents vary from high to low, and popular customs vary from pure to decadent, among them, if they are not harsh and tangled [? 勢, perhaps for 棼], then they are lax and negligent. That the people's strength remains exhausted and outstanding achievements have not yet become manifest is precisely for this reason.

The state takes the military as its defense, and the command of the troops lies with the generals and commanders. As for the generals and commanders of antiquity—such as Wu Qi 吳起 in training troops, Wang Jian 王翦 in his skill at warfare, Lian Po 廉頗 in his valor, and Li Mu 李牧 in his defense of the frontier—they have long been praised by people. Today, those selected as generals and commanders mostly come from hereditary lineages; in the way of governing troops, compared to those four masters, they ought to surpass them. Yet because men in silk garments promoted through hereditary privilege command idle and untrained troops, and furthermore, if they are not greedy and harsh, then they are indulgent and lax—that their wisdom and courage are still scarce and strategies for decisive victory are still unseen is precisely due to this.

Right now, the sacred Son of Heaven is on high, and he devotes his earnest attention to these four matters of rites, music, the military, and the people; however, …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之用未盡周治民兵者未盡得人誠有
如執事之所慮者茲欲教民以禮當以文公
家禮申而明之使庠序日加講習而推及閭
閻之下薰陶日久自然成俗禮豈有不行者
乎茲欲教民以樂當以元定新書嚴而教之
俾學校詳加考究而達於鄉黨之間涵泳日
深自然成風樂豈有不用者乎至於治民也
惟在乎慎選守令使布列郡縣者能若程顥
之令晉城朱熹之知漳州則教化乎而黎元
===
自安何龔黃之徒難及乎治兵也惟在乎謹
擇將帥使統御中外者能如韓琦之宣撫陜
西仲淹之經畧環慶則武備脩而兵威自振
何頗牧之輩足數乎然為政固莫先於教化
而禮樂又教化之本也禮樂有本有文本諸
敬以為禮則禮得其體而當然之禮行本諸
和以為樂則樂得其本而自然之和生矣夫
然則本末兼該禮樂畢舉政無不立俗無不
美而治化之隆何虞周之不可及哉謹對
punctuated: 禮樂之用未盡周，治民兵者未盡得人，誠有如執事之所慮者。茲欲教民以禮，當以文公《家禮》申而明之，使庠序日加講習，而推及閭閻之下，薰陶日久，自然成俗，禮豈有不行者乎？茲欲教民以樂，當以元定《新書》嚴而教之，俾學校詳加考究，而達於鄉黨之間，涵泳日深，自然成風，樂豈有不用者乎？至於治民也，惟在乎慎選守令，使布列郡縣者能若程顥之令晉城、朱熹之知漳州，則教化乎而黎元自安，何龔、黃之徒難及乎？治兵也，惟在乎謹擇將帥，使統御中外者能如韓琦之宣撫陜西、仲淹之經畧環慶，則武備脩而兵威自振，何頗、牧之輩足數乎？然為政固莫先於教化，而禮樂又教化之本也。禮樂有本有文，本諸敬以為禮，則禮得其體，而當然之禮行；本諸和以為樂，則樂得其本，而自然之和生矣。夫然，則本末兼該，禮樂畢舉，政無不立，俗無不美，而治化之隆，何虞、周之不可及哉？謹對。
translation_en: … the application of rites and music is not yet completely comprehensive, and those who govern the people and the military have not yet all been the right men—this is truly just as Your Excellency is concerned about. If we now wish to instruct the people in rites, we ought to expound and clarify them through Duke Wen's (Zhu Xi 朱熹) Family Rituals (Jiali 家禮), causing the local schools to daily increase their study and practice of them and extending them down to the village lanes; when the molding influence continues for a long time, it will naturally form customs—how could rites fail to be practiced? If we now wish to instruct the people in music, we ought to strictly teach them through Cai Yuanding's 蔡元定 New Book on Music (Lülü xinshu 律呂新書), causing the schools to thoroughly investigate and study it and extending it among the rural communities; when immersion in it grows daily deeper, it will naturally form a prevailing ethos—how could music fail to be employed? As for governing the people, it lies solely in carefully selecting prefects and magistrates. If those stationed throughout the prefectures and counties can be like Cheng Hao 程顥 serving as Magistrate of Jincheng or Zhu Xi serving as Prefect of Zhangzhou, then moral transformation will inspire trust [?] [reading 乎 as 孚] and the common people will naturally be at peace—why would the likes of Gong Sui 龔遂 and Huang Ba 黃霸 be difficult to equal? As for governing the military, it lies solely in prudently choosing generals and commanders. If those commanding inside and outside the capital can be like Han Qi 韓琦 serving as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi or Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹 serving as Military Commissioner of Huanqing, then military preparedness will be well maintained and martial prestige will naturally be roused—how would the likes of Lian Po 廉頗 and Li Mu 李牧 even be worth counting? Yet in administering government, nothing takes precedence over moral transformation, and rites and music are in turn the root of moral transformation. Rites and music have both their fundamental root and their outward refinement. If one grounds rites in reverence, then rites attain their substance and the proper rites are practiced; if one grounds music in harmony, then music attains its root and natural harmony arises. When it is thus, both root and branch are encompassed, rites and music are both fully promoted, no governance fails to be established, no custom fails to be admirable, and in the flourishing of governance and transformation, why would the eras of Yu (Shun 舜) and Zhou 周 be unattainable? I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第四問
同考試官訓導李　批〔貿諸經傳斷以義理有學之〕
曾煥
〔士也〕
同考試官教諭韓　批〔此策有考據而斷以理宜錄〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔能答所問〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔決未決之疑有識之士〕
道無往而不在雖聖人無不師理有疑而不
決在學者所嘗辨夫道之所存師之所在也
===
聖人非生不能於師而亦未嘗不取諸人以
為善賢人之學不能不資於師而亦未嘗無
自得之妙然而議論紛紜莫知所定學者其
可不稽之經傳斷之義理以求一定之說哉
請因明問而言之黃帝生而神靈長而聰
慧仰觀俯察作則垂憲顓頊淵靜淵有
謀疏通達事帝嚳繼之聰以知遠明以察微
既執厥中民罔弗從以至堯舜禹湯文武皆
生知之聖而謂其學於大填錄圖赤松子君
punctuated:
第四問
同考試官訓導李批：〔貿諸經傳，斷以義理，有學之士也。〕
曾煥
同考試官教諭韓批：〔此策有考據而斷以理，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭吾批：〔能答所問。〕
考試官教諭趙批：〔決未決之疑，有識之士。〕

道無往而不在，雖聖人無不師；理有疑而不決，在學者所嘗辨。夫道之所存，師之所在也。聖人非生不能於師，而亦未嘗不取諸人以為善；賢人之學不能不資於師，而亦未嘗無自得之妙。然而議論紛紜，莫知所定，學者其可不稽之經傳、斷之義理，以求一定之說哉？請因明問而言之。黃帝生而神靈，長而聰慧，仰觀俯察，作則垂憲；顓頊淵靜，淵有謀，疏通達事；帝嚳繼之，聰以知遠，明以察微，既執厥中，民罔弗從；以至堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，皆生知之聖，而謂其學於大填、錄圖、赤松子、君…
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li comments: [Verified against [? 貿 for 質] the Classics and commentaries and judged according to moral principle; this is a scholar of learning.]
Zeng Huan 曾煥
Associate Examiner Instructor Han comments: [This policy essay is grounded in textual evidence and judged according to principle; it ought to be selected.]
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: [Able to answer what was asked.]
Examiner Instructor Zhao comments: [Resolves unresolved doubts; a scholar of insight.]

The Way is present everywhere, and even a sage has no one from whom he does not learn; when principles are doubtful and unresolved, it rests with scholars to discriminate them. Now where the Way abides is where the teacher is to be found. It is not that a sage is born unable to act as a teacher himself, yet he never fails to draw upon others in order to do good; the learning of a worthy cannot do without relying on a teacher, yet neither is it ever without the subtlety of personal realization. However, when discussions are confused and divergent and no one knows how to settle them, how can scholars fail to examine them against the Classics and commentaries and judge them by moral principle so as to seek a definitive explanation? Allow me to speak of this by following your clear question. The Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) was divine andnuminous from birth, and intelligent and wise as he grew; looking up to observe and looking down to examine, he created models and handed down laws. Zhuanxu 顓頊 was deep and tranquil, profound and resourceful [? 淵有謀], perceptive and conversant with affairs. Emperor Ku 帝嚳 succeeded him, acute in knowing what was distant and clear-sighted in discerning the subtle; having grasped the Mean, there were none among the people who did not follow him. Coming down to Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, Tang 湯, Wen 文, and Wu 武, all were sages born with knowledge—yet to say that they studied with the likes of Datian 大填, Lutu 錄圖, Master Red Pine (Chisongzi 赤松子), Jun…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
疇務成昭之輩西王國伯成子時子思郭叔
之徒雖曰載之傳記其果然耶夫自黃帝至
於武王皆以聖人之德居君師之位所以繼
天而立極者也其道統之傳心法之妙見諸
經傳者若帝嚳帝堯舜禹之執中成湯文武
之建中建極昭如日星矣今乃謂數聖人反
師於大填郭叔之徒蓋道之至也聖人有所
不知謂其師一端之善容或有之謂其學於
其門親授其業豈足信哉雖其說之出於孔
===
門高為意好事者爲之託子夏之名以取信
於人不然何其授受之旨經傳無一語以及
之耶此其不足信也明矣自是之後若孔子
之於老聃左丘明之於孔子公羊高穀梁赤
之於子夏孟子之於子思二程之於周子皆
謂之師弟子也或又謂其不然學者不能無
疑夫孔子之聖天理之純人道之極其於古
今名物制度沿革蓋亦於彼或有所詢如適
周問禮於老聃是孔子之無常師也而謂孔
punctuated: 疇、務成昭之輩，西王國、伯成子、時子思、郭叔之徒，雖曰載之傳記，其果然耶？夫自黃帝至於武王，皆以聖人之德，居君師之位，所以繼天而立極者也。其道統之傳、心法之妙，見諸經傳者，若帝嚳、帝堯、舜、禹之執中，成湯、文、武之建中、建極，昭如日星矣。今乃謂數聖人反師於大填、郭叔之徒，蓋道之至也，聖人有所不知，謂其師一端之善，容或有之；謂其學於其門，親授其業，豈足信哉？雖其說之出於孔門高為，意好事者爲之，託子夏之名以取信於人。不然，何其授受之旨，經傳無一語以及之耶？此其不足信也明矣。自是之後，若孔子之於老聃，左丘明之於孔子，公羊高、穀梁赤之於子夏，孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，皆謂之師弟子也。或又謂其不然，學者不能無疑。夫孔子之聖，天理之純，人道之極，其於古今名物、制度沿革，蓋亦於彼或有所詢，如適周問禮於老聃，是孔子之無常師也。而謂孔
translation_en:
…Chou, and Wucheng Zhao, or followers such as Xi Wangguo, Bocheng Zi, Shi Zisi, and Guo Shu—even though it is said to be recorded in traditions and commentaries, is it really so? Now, from the Yellow Emperor down to King Wu, all possessed the virtue of sages and occupied the position of ruler and teacher, whereby they succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. The transmission of their orthodox Way and the subtlety of their method of the mind, as seen in the Classics and commentaries—such as holding fast to the Mean by Emperor Ku, Emperor Yao, Shun, and Yu, and establishing the Mean and establishing the supreme standard by Tang the Completer, King Wen, and King Wu—are as bright as the sun and stars. Now to claim that these several sages instead took as their teachers the likes of Datian and Guo Shu: because the Way is so vast that even a sage does not know everything, to say that they learned some single point of goodness from them may perhaps have happened; but to say that they studied at their gate and personally received their instruction—how could that be worthy of belief? Even though this account is said to come from a high disciple [高為 for 高弟?] of Confucius's school, I suspect meddlesome people fabricated it, borrowing the name of Zixia to win credence from others. Otherwise, why is it that the Classics and commentaries do not have a single word mentioning the purport of what they taught and received? That this is unworthy of belief is clear.

After this, in cases such as Confucius in relation to Lao Dan, Zuo Qiuming in relation to Confucius, Gongyang Gao and Guliang Chi in relation to Zixia, Mencius in relation to Zisi, and the two Cheng brothers in relation to Master Zhou [Zhou Dunyi], all are called teacher and disciple. Yet some say it was not so, and scholars cannot be without doubt. Now, with Confucius's sageliness, the purity of Heavenly Principle and the ultimate of the human Way, when it came to the names and objects of antiquity and the present, and the evolution of institutions, he perhaps also made inquiries of others—as when he went to Zhou and asked about rites from Lao Dan. This shows that Confucius had no fixed teacher. Yet to say that Confucius…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
子爲老聃弟子豈不妄哉至若左氏公穀之
所傳受實得孔子子夏而爲宗師然春秋一
書褒貶是非撥亂反正人道之大綱王法之
所寓以卜氏之賢當筆削之際尚無一辭之
可賛彼左氏之傳果能得其奥旨而不失之
誣哉以親炙之丘明而尚有所失況公穀去
聖既遠顧欲立傳以明乎經是亦不免有所
失也又何名家之有哉使二子能知子夏所
以不敢賛經　亦未敢輕爲立傳以取
===
誣妄之譏是又　即其所學而遂疑其師
授也他如孟子之於子思二程之於周子是
皆亞聖大賢之資而又難以左氏公穀例也
且孟子以命世亞聖之才受業子思之門故
思誠之語與中庸同符而合轍也二程負特
立之村學於周子之門實始尊信庸學爲之
表章斥二家似是之非續千載不傳之緒俾
吾道之明如日麗天其學雖出周子而得於
經者爲多其與孟子自非說正人心之功同
punctuated: 子爲老聃弟子，豈不妄哉！至若左氏、公、穀之所傳受，實得孔子、子夏而爲宗師。然《春秋》一書，褒貶是非，撥亂反正，人道之大綱、王法之所寓。以卜氏之賢，當筆削之際，尚無一辭之可賛，彼左氏之傳，果能得其奥旨而不失之誣哉？以親炙之丘明而尚有所失，況公、穀去聖既遠，顧欲立傳以明乎經，是亦不免有所失也，又何名家之有哉！使二子能知子夏所以不敢賛經，　亦未敢輕爲立傳以取誣妄之譏。是又　即其所學而遂疑其師授也。他如孟子之於子思、二程之於周子，是皆亞聖大賢之資，而又難以左氏、公、穀例也。且孟子以命世亞聖之才，受業子思之門，故「思誠」之語，與《中庸》同符而合轍也。二程負特立之村，學於周子之門，實始尊信《庸》、《學》，爲之表章，斥二家似是之非，續千載不傳之緒，俾吾道之明如日麗天。其學雖出周子，而得於經者爲多，其與孟子自非說、正人心之功同…
translation_en:
… [Confu]cius was a disciple of Lao Dan—how could that not be absurd! As for what was transmitted and received by Master Zuo [Zuo Qiuming 左丘明], Gongyang [Gongyang Gao 公羊高], and Guliang [Guliang Chi 穀梁赤], they indeed took Confucius and Zixia 子夏 as their foundational masters. Yet the single work of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) dispenses praise and blame, distinguishes right from wrong, suppresses disorder and restores rectitude; it is the great framework of the human way and the repository of kingly law. Even with the worthiness of Master Bu [Zixia], when Confucius was writing and pruning the text, he could not add a single word to it. How then could Master Zuo's commentary truly grasp its profound purport without lapsing into falsity? If Qiuming, who personally received instruction from the Sage, still had his failings, how much more so Gongyang and Guliang, who were already far removed from the Sage and yet sought to establish commentaries to elucidate the Classic! They too inevitably had their failings; what claim could they have to being renowned masters of a school? Had the two masters been able to understand why Zixia dared not add a word to the Classic, [lacuna] they too would not have dared to lightly compose commentaries and thereby invite ridicule for falsity and absurdity. Therefore one again [lacuna: cannot] on the basis of what they learned go so far as to doubt their transmission from their master.

As for others, such as Mencius in relation to Zisi 子思, and the two Cheng brothers [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] in relation to Master Zhou [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], they all possessed the endowments of a Second Sage or great worthy, and cannot be judged by the same standard as Master Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang. Moreover, Mencius, with the world-renowned talent of a Second Sage, studied at the gate of Zisi; thus his words on "reflecting upon sincerity" tally and move in the same tracks as the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong). The two Chengs, endowed with extraordinary talent [reading 材 for 村], studied at the gate of Master Zhou. They were indeed the first to revere and place faith in the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning (Daxue), honoring and elucidating them, refuting the specious fallacies of the two schools [Buddhism and Daoism], and continuing the thread that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years, causing the brilliance of our Way to shine like the sun in the heavens. Although their learning originated from Master Zhou, what they obtained directly from the Classics was even greater; their merit is on a par with that of Mencius in refuting perverse doctrines [? reading 距詖說 for 自非說] and rectifying human minds…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
一揆也此伊川所以謂其得不傳之學於遺
經孟子之後一人而已故朱子之序庸學亦
直以程子而繼孟子也耶嘗見區區未能究
其源流以祛古今之疑惟進而教之
第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃　批叙江西之風俗人物歷歷指
掌未復以師先哲爲言非博學有志者不能得
士如斯其粹養之效歟
同考試官教諭唐　批此策有事實有發揚有歸宿
博洽之士也
同考試官教諭桂　批答者徒知誇美風俗人物之
盛而不知以名節道德爲尚此作能景行先哲其
有志者歟
同考試官學正張　批此策乃究實迹者易而居德
善俗者難多士出衆見無如此作故錄之
考試官教諭吾　批風俗人物鋪叙殆盡且師古
善俗之志藹然言表可嘉可嘉
punctuated:
一揆也。此伊川所以謂其「得不傳之學於遺經，孟子之後一人而已」；故朱子之序《庸》、《學》，亦直以程子而繼孟子也耶！嘗見區區，未能究其源流，以祛古今之疑，惟進而教之。

第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃　批：叙江西之風俗人物，歷歷指掌，未復以師先哲爲言，非博學有志者不能。得士如斯，其粹養之效歟！
同考試官教諭唐　批：此策有事實，有發揚，有歸宿，博洽之士也。
同考試官教諭桂　批：答者徒知誇美風俗人物之盛，而不知以名節道德爲尚。此作能景行先哲，其有志者歟！
同考試官學正張　批：此策乃究實迹者易，而居德善俗者難。多士出衆見，無如此作，故錄之。
考試官教諭吾　批：風俗人物，鋪叙殆盡，且師古善俗之志，藹然言表。可嘉，可嘉！
translation_en:
… follows the exact same principle. This is why Yichuan (Cheng Yi 程頤) said of him [Cheng Hao 程顥] that he "attained the unheralded learning from the surviving Classics, and after Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) there was only this one man." Is this not why Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹), in his prefaces to the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) and the Great Learning (Daxue 大學), also directly placed the Masters Cheng (Chengzi 程子) in succession to Mencius? My humble views are superficial and have not been able to thoroughly trace the origins and developments so as to dispel the doubts of past and present; I pray only to be advanced and instructed.

Fifth Question
Xiao Sheng 蕭昇
Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang comments: He recounts the customs and notable figures of Jiangxi as clearly as pointing to the palm of one's hand, and at the end [reading 未 as 末] goes on to speak of emulating the former worthies—none but a scholar of broad learning and high aspiration could achieve this. Obtaining a scholar like this—is it not the result of pure cultivation!
Associate Examiner and Instructor Tang comments: This policy essay has factual substance, eloquent elaboration, and a sound conclusion; he is a scholar of broad and thorough learning.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Gui comments: Other respondents merely knew to boast of the flourishing of customs and notable figures, without knowing to esteem moral integrity and virtue. This composition is able to admire and follow the conduct of the former worthies; is he not a man of high aspiration!
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Zhang comments: For this policy question, investigating the actual historical traces is easy, whereas abiding in virtue to improve customs is difficult. Among the many scholars who put forth their views, none matched this composition, so we have selected it.
Examiner and Instructor Wu comments: The customs and notable figures are set forth almost exhaustively, and moreover his aspiration to emulate antiquity and improve customs shines warmly through his words. Most praiseworthy, most praiseworthy!

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙　批〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上抱奇器之士也士風不爲之倚重乎〕
橐籥之中以倡以化而天下之風俗所由美
陶冶之內以感以興而天下之人物所由盛
此
國家氣運之隆治化之美超越於往古也尚矣
然輿圖之廣在在皆然而江西特一大方也
爲郡一十有三統邑六十有九在禹貢隷揚
州之域在天文屬斗牛之墟山有匡廬之秀
===
特水有彭蠡之環匯其間風俗之異人物之
盛誠有關於
國家之氣化者安得不來執事之問哉愚也
生長是地得之父師考之圖志竊有所知
敢不爲執事陳之以言其風俗也南昌在
藩省之中而饒州與之相屬一則講誦爲
業而衣冠萃止一則忠孝繼出而文物相
續廣信居藩省之東而南康爲其接壤一
則矜謹節義而士風貧薄一則淳固慤實有
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙　批：〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上，抱奇器之士也，士風不爲之倚重乎？〕

橐籥之中，以倡以化，而天下之風俗所由美；陶冶之內，以感以興，而天下之人物所由盛。此國家氣運之隆、治化之美，超越於往古也尚矣。然輿圖之廣，在在皆然，而江西特一大方也。爲郡一十有三，統邑六十有九，在《禹貢》隷揚州之域，在天文屬斗、牛之墟，山有匡廬之秀特，水有彭蠡之環匯。其間風俗之異、人物之盛，誠有關於國家之氣化者，安得不來執事之問哉？愚也生長是地，得之父師，考之圖志，竊有所知，敢不爲執事陳之？以言其風俗也：南昌在藩省之中，而饒州與之相屬，一則講誦爲業而衣冠萃止，一則忠孝繼出而文物相續；廣信居藩省之東，而南康爲其接壤，一則矜謹節義而士風貧薄，一則淳固慤實，有
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: [Born in this land yet befriending the ancients of a thousand ages past, he is a scholar who harbors extraordinary talent. Does the ethos of the literati not depend heavily upon such a person?]

…Within the bellows of creation, through leading and transforming, the customs of the realm are thereby made fine; within the potter's mold of governance, through moving and inspiring, the men of talent of the realm thereby flourish. In this, the prosperity of the State's destiny and the beauty of its transformative rule have long surpassed those of antiquity. Yet throughout the vastness of the empire's territory this is everywhere the case, and Jiangxi in particular is one great region. It comprises thirteen prefectures governing sixty-nine counties; in the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) it belonged to the domain of Yangzhou, and in astrological pitch-divisions it corresponds to the region of the Dipper and the Ox. Among its mountains is the sublime distinction of Mount Kuanglu, and among its waters is the encircling confluence of Lake Pengli. The diversity of its customs and the flourishing of its figures therein truly have a bearing upon the transformative vitality of the State—how could they fail to prompt Your Excellency's question? Ignorant as I am, I was born and raised in this land; having learned from my father and teachers and having examined the maps and gazetteers, I venture to have some modest knowledge of it—how could I dare not set it forth for Your Excellency? To speak of its customs: Nanchang lies at the center of the province, and Raozhou is contiguous with it; in the one, scholarly recitation and lecturing are the chosen calling and gentry gather in abundance, while in the other, men of loyalty and filial piety emerge in succession and cultural refinement continues unbroken. Guangxin is situated in the east of the province, and Nankang borders upon it; in the one, people value and guard integrity and righteousness while the literati ethos is frugal and plain, while in the other, they are simple, steadfast, and honest, possessing…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
先儒遺風至於士習詩書而農勤稼穡□□
和平而人物秀麗者非九江與建昌乎風流
儒雅而民樂耕桑崇德尚禮而勤力知分者
非撫州與臨江乎瑞之吏民朴野而不囂於
訟袁之廉恥儉嗇而事不煩此二郡之風俗
不同也贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節南安
則民習淳古而士果於義此又二郡之風俗各
異也至於人鮮淳而多壽考家詩書而□庠
塾其吉安之風俗何厚哉以言乎人物也総
===
樺非其力不食陳蕃稱為南州高士黃庭堅
為江西詩宗蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表致力中
原陶侃之運甓以自勵克定大計趙汝愚之謀
國不顧身此南昌饒州之人物也□知□身
歸國葉大用受金牌之賜□□□□□得
獲全婦之安保衛鄉閭鄒元靖有□□才
請救襄樊江萬里以峭直見忌此廣信南康
之人物也可見九江建昌則有周訪之沉
毅果斷陶潛之恥身後代與夫曾鞏齊名
punctuated:
先儒遺風。至於士習《詩》《書》而農勤稼穡，□□和平而人物秀麗者，非九江與建昌乎？風流儒雅而民樂耕桑，崇德尚禮而勤力知分者，非撫州與臨江乎？瑞之吏民朴野而不囂於訟，袁之廉恥儉嗇而事不煩，此二郡之風俗不同也；贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節，南安則民習淳古而士果於義，此又二郡之風俗各異也。至於人鮮淳而多壽考，家《詩》《書》而□庠塾，其吉安之風俗何厚哉！
以言乎人物也：総樺非其力不食，陳蕃稱為南州高士；黃庭堅為江西詩宗，蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表；致力中原，陶侃之運甓以自勵；克定大計，趙汝愚之謀國不顧身：此南昌、饒州之人物也。□知□身歸國，葉大用受金牌之賜；□□□□□，得獲全婦之安；保衛鄉閭，鄒元靖有□□才；請救襄、樊，江萬里以峭直見忌：此廣信、南康之人物也可見。九江、建昌則有周訪之沉毅果斷，陶潛之恥身後代，與夫曾鞏齊名…
translation_en:
…the legacy of the former Confucian scholars. As for where the literati study the Odes and the Documents while the farmers are diligent in sowing and reaping, and where [customs?] are harmonious and peaceful while the people and things are refined and handsome—are these not Jiujiang and Jianchang? Where manners are cultured and scholarly while the commoners delight in plowing and sericulture, and where virtue is revered and ritual esteemed while people work hard and know their station—are these not Fuzhou and Linjiang? In Ruizhou, clerks and commoners are simple and rustic and not clamorous in litigation, while in Yuanzhou, people have a sense of honor and shame, are frugal and thrifty, and public affairs are not burdensome; such are the differing customs of these two prefectures. In Ganzhou, people are vigorous and skilled in craftsmanship while holding lofty ambitions and encouraging moral integrity; in Nan'an, the commoners' habits are pure and ancient while the scholars are resolute in righteousness; such again are the distinct customs of these two prefectures. As for where the people are pure [?] and many enjoy long life, and where every household has the Odes and the Documents and [establishes?] community and village schools—how generous indeed are the customs of Ji'an!

To speak of their notable figures: Xu Zhi [transcribed 総樺] would not eat except by his own labor, and Chen Fan praised him as the "Lofty Scholar of the Southern Prefectures"; Huang Tingjian was the patriarch of the Jiangxi poetry school, and Su Shi marveled that he stood independent beyond the material world; devoting his strength to the Central Plains, Tao Kan carried bricks to spur himself on; able to settle the great dynastic plan, Zhao Ruyu planned for the state without regard for his own person—these are the notable figures of Nanchang and Raozhou. Knowing [...] [?] and returning to the state in person, Ye Dayong received the bestowal of a golden tally; [...], able to secure peace for keeping a wife's chastity intact [?]; defending his native villages, Zou Yuanjing possessed [...] talent; requesting relief for Xiangyang and Fancheng, Jiang Wanli was resented for his stern uprightness—such are the notable figures to be seen in Guangxin and Nankang. In Jiujiang and Jianchang, there were Zhou Fang with his deep resolve and decisiveness, Tao Qian who was ashamed to serve a successor dynasty in person, as well as Zeng Gong whose fame equaled…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
於歐陽陳宗禮之直言淸節者焉撫州臨江則
有陸九淵之講明道學吳澂之力學聖賢與
夫陳喬以社稷爲己任劉淸之之博極群書者
焉他如劉恕篤好史學陳仲微涵飫六經廖
洪之孝築墳廬陳重之友堅膠漆非瑞袁之
人物乎李朴之操履勁特曾開之大節不奪
盧汝舟之廉約守正田闢之嗜學不倦非贛
南之人物乎以至盡心匡直文章與韓愈並
稱歐陽脩一代之宗也死不屈節而父子相
===
繼楊邦乂名世之人也胡銓之力排和議劾
奸一疏與日月以爭光文天祥之九死不悔
正氣一歌與宇宙相爲悠久其吉安之人物
何盛哉然風俗之美於今者無以異乎古人
物之盛乎古者何有間於今故今之篤行文
章濟濟相望功名事業燁燁馳聲愚固未暇
以縷數惟於一風俗師先哲之意竊亦有志
不敢無言夫欲一風俗莫先於明禮義而
養廉恥戒浮靡而崇節儉其所以化導之
punctuated: 於歐陽，陳宗禮之直言淸節者焉。撫州、臨江則有陸九淵之講明道學，吳澂之力學聖賢，與夫陳喬以社稷爲己任，劉淸之之博極群書者焉。他如劉恕篤好史學，陳仲微涵飫六經，廖洪之孝築墳廬，陳重之友堅膠漆，非瑞、袁之人物乎？李朴之操履勁特，曾開之大節不奪，盧汝舟之廉約守正，田闢之嗜學不倦，非贛、南之人物乎？以至盡心匡直，文章與韓愈並稱，歐陽脩一代之宗也；死不屈節，而父子相繼，楊邦乂名世之人也；胡銓之力排和議，劾奸一疏，與日月以爭光；文天祥之九死不悔，正氣一歌，與宇宙相爲悠久。其吉安之人物何盛哉！然風俗之美於今者，無以異乎古；人物之盛乎古者，何有間於今？故今之篤行文章，濟濟相望，功名事業，燁燁馳聲，愚固未暇以縷數。惟於一風俗、師先哲之意，竊亦有志，不敢無言。夫欲一風俗，莫先於明禮義而養廉恥，戒浮靡而崇節儉。其所以化導之…
translation_en:
…with Ouyang, and Chen Zongli 陳宗禮, noted for his forthright remonstrance and pure integrity. In Fuzhou 撫州 and Linjiang 臨江, there were Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵, who expounded and clarified the Learning of the Way, and Wu Cheng 吳澂, who strove to learn from the sages and worthies, as well as Chen Qiao 陳喬, who took the altars of state as his personal responsibility, and Liu Qingzhi 劉淸之, who was exhaustively learned in all books. As for others—such as Liu Shu 劉恕, who was deeply devoted to historical studies; Chen Zhongwei 陳仲微, who was steeped in the Six Classics; Liao Hong 廖洪, whose filial piety led him to build a hut by his parents' grave; and Chen Chong 陳重, whose friendship was as firm as glue and lacquer—were they not the notable figures of Ruizhou 瑞州 and Yuanzhou 袁州? Li Pu 李朴, whose conduct and integrity were vigorous and outstanding; Zeng Kai 曾開, whose great principles could not be compromised; Lu Ruzhou 盧汝舟, who was incorrupt, frugal, and upright; and Tian Pi 田闢, who loved learning tirelessly—were they not the notable figures of Ganzhou 贛州 and Nan'an 南安? Coming down to Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, who devoted his heart to rectifying the state and whose literary writings were ranked alongside those of Han Yu 韓愈—he was the master of an entire generation; Yang Bangyi 楊邦乂, who died without bending his integrity, with father and son succeeding one another in loyalty—he was a man renowned throughout the age; Hu Quan 胡銓, who forcefully rejected peace negotiations and whose single memorial impeaching the treacherous vies in brilliance with the sun and moon; and Wen Tianxiang 文天祥, who had no regrets even through nine deaths and whose single "Song of Righteous Qi" (Zhengqige 正氣歌) endures as long as the cosmos—how flourishing indeed are the notable figures of Ji'an 吉安!

Yet how does the beauty of customs in the present differ from that of antiquity, and how is the flourishing of notable figures in antiquity separated from the present? Thus today, men of earnest conduct and literary attainment look upon one another in scores, and their achievements, honors, and enterprises win resplendent renown; I truly have no leisure to enumerate them one by one. Only regarding the intent of unifying customs and taking the former worthies as models do I privately harbor an aspiration, and dare not remain silent. Now, if one wishes to unify customs, nothing comes before clarifying ritual and righteousness and nurturing a sense of honor and shame, guarding against superficial extravagance and exalting frugality. As for the means of transforming and guiding them…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
者固當造端乎民牧所以鼓舞而倡率之則又
在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳若夫靖節之介
得其正文忠公之文本於德文安文正之學
根乎道此道德文章之可師也澹菴憂中興
之社稷信國決萬世之綱常此功名節義之
可師也為士者誠能師先哲以脩己寄民社
者又能師先哲以化民則民風之所以淳者
在是士風之所以正者在是人物之所以盛
者亦在是愚也不敏倘蒙與進俾得以行其
言敢不景行先哲以副執事之望謹對
punctuated: 者，固當造端乎民牧；所以鼓舞而倡率之，則又在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳。若夫靖節之介得其正，文忠公之文本於德，文安、文正之學根乎道，此道德文章之可師也；澹菴憂中興之社稷，信國決萬世之綱常，此功名節義之可師也。為士者誠能師先哲以脩己，寄民社者又能師先哲以化民，則民風之所以淳者在是，士風之所以正者在是，人物之所以盛者亦在是。愚也不敏，倘蒙與進，俾得以行其言，敢不景行先哲，以副執事之望！謹對。
translation_en: … surely ought to begin with the shepherds of the people [local officials]; yet the means of inspiring and leading them in turn depends entirely on how the scholar-officials and gentlemen apply their minds. As for how Master Jingjie [Tao Yuanming 陶淵明] attained rectitude in his unyielding integrity, how Duke Wenzhong [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修] rooted his writings in virtue, and how the learning of Wen'an [Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵] and Wenzheng [Zeng Gong 曾鞏 / Wu Cheng 吳澄] was grounded in the Way—these are the exemplars of moral virtue and literary composition worthy of emulation. And as for how Dan'an [Hu Quan 胡銓] worried over the altars of state during the Dynastic Restoration, and how the Duke of Xinguo [Wen Tianxiang 文天祥] upheld with finality the cardinal principles and constant virtues for ten thousand generations—these are the exemplars of meritorious achievement and righteous integrity worthy of emulation. If those who are scholars can truly take the former sages as their teachers in cultivating themselves, and those entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil can likewise take the former sages as their teachers in transforming the people, then herein lies that whereby popular customs become pure, herein lies that whereby the ethos of the literati becomes upright, and herein too lies that whereby men of talent flourish. Though I am dull-witted, if I am favored with advancement and enabled to put my words into practice, how could I dare not emulate the luminous conduct of the former sages so as to fulfill the expectations of Your Excellencies? I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西爲東南鉅服英賢之
生萃焉發于漢唐盛于有宋
而尤盛于我
朝或以文學鳴或以政事顯或
以忠烈震撼轟天地焕爛簡
冊海宇之廣人材之夥率推
===
先焉況自我
朝迨今踵大拜者垂百數年連
大魁者踰十數人雖其所樹
立有隆有庳然至於大貽誚
於時者尠矣於戲誠盛矣哉
乃今成化十三年實維大比
之秋合列郡之士幾三千人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

江西爲東南鉅服，英賢之生萃焉。發于漢、唐，盛于有宋，而尤盛于我朝。或以文學鳴，或以政事顯，或以忠烈震撼，轟天地，焕爛簡冊。海宇之廣，人材之夥，率推先焉。況自我朝迨今，踵大拜者垂百數年，連大魁者踰十數人。雖其所樹立有隆有庳，然至於大貽誚於時者尠矣。於戲，誠盛矣哉！

乃今成化十三年，實維大比之秋，合列郡之士幾三千人，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Jiangxi is a vast territory in the southeast, where the birth of heroes and worthies is concentrated. It began to emerge in the Han and Tang dynasties, flourished in the Song dynasty, and has flourished even more so in our dynasty. Some have gained renown through literature and scholarship, some have achieved prominence through governance, and some have shaken the world through loyalty and martyrdom, resounding through heaven and earth and shining brightly in the historical records. Across the vastness of the empire and the multitude of its men of talent, Jiangxi is generally ranked first. Moreover, from the founding of our dynasty down to the present, those who have succeeded one another in rising to the Grand Secretariat have spanned nearly a hundred and some years, and those who have consecutively taken first place in the examinations exceed ten and more men. Although their achievements have been both lofty and modest, those who have brought great ridicule upon themselves in their own time have been few indeed. Alas, how truly flourishing it is!

Now, in the thirteenth year of the Chenghua reign (1477), it is truly the autumn of the triennial examination. Bringing together nearly three thousand scholars from the various prefectures, …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
三試之自監臨以曁內外諸
執事旣皆殫公竭力防範周
詳哥等濫竽考官敢不精白
一心以公去取於是擇其文
之中式者遵
制得九十五人登之賢書獻之
天子稽首爲
===
人賀復僭序諸小錄爲
登名諸君子告焉夫江右人
材於今固盛矣而其所以盛
諸君子容不知所勉哉勉之
唯無負
天之所以命我者之大而遜其第
一等者於人以文學鳴必爲
punctuated:
三試之。自監臨以曁內外諸執事，旣皆殫公竭力，防範周詳；哥等濫竽考官，敢不精白一心，以公去取？於是擇其文之中式者，遵制得九十五人，登之賢書，獻之天子，稽首爲人賀。復僭序諸小錄，爲登名諸君子告焉。

夫江右人材，於今固盛矣，而其所以盛，諸君子容不知所勉哉？勉之唯無負天之所以命我者之大，而遜其第一等者於人。以文學鳴，必爲
translation_en:
…and tested them in three sessions. Since the Supervising Official down to all the inner and outer functionaries had already exhausted their public spirit and devoted their utmost strength to ensure that the precautions and regulations were thorough and detailed, how could I, Ge, and my colleagues—unworthy as we are to serve as Examiners—dare not keep our hearts pure and single-minded so as to be impartial in selecting and rejecting? Accordingly, we chose those whose essays met the standard; in compliance with the imperial system, we obtained ninety-five men, entered their names on the roster of the worthy, presented it to the Son of Heaven, and bowed our heads to the ground to offer congratulations on behalf of the people [?]. I further presume to write this preface to the examination record to address the gentlemen whose names have been registered.

Now, the men of talent in Jiangxi are certainly flourishing today; yet as to the reason why they flourish, how could you gentlemen not know wherewith to exert yourselves? To exert yourselves means simply not to fail the greatness of what Heaven has conferred upon us, nor to yield the highest rank of achievement to others. If one gains renown through literature and learning, one must…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
往聖繼絶學爲萬世開太平
斯第一流之文學歟以政事
顯必爲天地立心爲生民立
命斯第一流之政事歟忠烈
自文學政事中事無庸言已
若然則諸君子負挾之弘建
千豈徒爲當今人物將
===
□□三代人物等而我
□□雍熈泰和之治所以登三
□□五者亦將愈遠彌隆矣
主司深望實在于茲唯諸君
子副之
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開
化吾昇謹序
punctuated:
往聖繼絶學，爲萬世開太平，斯第一流之文學歟？以政事顯，必爲天地立心，爲生民立命，斯第一流之政事歟？忠烈自文學、政事中事，無庸言已。若然，則諸君子負挾之弘、建千，豈徒爲當今人物，將□□三代人物等，而我□□雍熈泰和之治，所以登三□□五者，亦將愈遠彌隆矣。主司深望實在于茲，唯諸君子副之。
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開化吾昇謹序。
translation_en:
… carry on the lost learning of the past sages and open up universal peace for ten thousand generations—is this not literature and learning of the first rank? If one becomes prominent through statecraft and administration, one must establish the mind of Heaven and Earth and establish the destiny of the living people—is this not statecraft and administration of the first rank? Loyalty and heroic integrity naturally arise from within literature, learning, and statecraft, so there is no need to speak further of them. If this be so, then with the breadth of what you gentlemen cherish and uphold, and the establishment [of achievements? 建千][?], how could you merely be men of note in the present day? You will [surely be? □□] the equals of the men of note of the Three Dynasties, and the harmonious, luminous, and supremely peaceful governance of our [August Ming / Imperial Court? □□], whereby it ascends to the Three [Kings] and [surpasses the? □□] Five [Emperors], will also become ever more far-reaching and ever more flourishing. The deep hopes of the examination officials truly lie in this; may you gentlemen live up to them.

Respectfullywritten as a postface by Wu Sheng 吾昇 of Kaihua 開化, Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭) of the Confucian School of Jiangpu County 江浦縣 in Yingtian Prefecture 應天府.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
之朔至于既望霖雨相屬陰
霾四布而唯當試之三日則
天日明霽纖雲不生謂非天
啓文明之象兆得人之徵也
耶試既技其尤者九十五人
仍錄其文章姓名為書以獻
天子示天下僉謂欽宜序諸首欽
===
嘗思古之世所以理後不可
幾也古之人所以直後不可
幾也古之禮樂所以明後不
可幾也古之刑罰賦斂所以
省且薄後不可幾也於乎萬
古此天地萬古此日月萬古
此山川何獨至于斯世斯人
punctuated: 之朔至于既望，霖雨相屬，陰霾四布；而唯當試之三日，則天日明霽，纖雲不生。謂非天啓文明之象，兆得人之徵也耶？試既，技其尤者九十五人，仍錄其文章、姓名為書，以獻天子、示天下。僉謂欽宜序諸首。欽嘗思古之世所以理，後不可幾也；古之人所以直，後不可幾也；古之禮樂所以明，後不可幾也；古之刑罰賦斂所以省且薄，後不可幾也。於乎！萬古此天地，萬古此日月，萬古此山川，何獨至于斯世、斯人，
translation_en: … from the first day of the month until the sixteenth, continuous rains fell one after another and gloomy haze spread everywhere; yet only on the three days of the examination sessions did the sky and sun clear brightly, without a wisp of cloud arising. Could one say this was not a phenomenon of Heaven inaugurating cultural brilliance and a sign foretelling the acquisition of talented men? Once the examination was completed, we selected [? 技 for 拔] the ninety-five most outstanding candidates, and according to precedent recorded their essays and names into a book to present to the Son of Heaven and display to the Empire. All said that I, Qin 欽, ought to write a preface at the head of it. I, Qin, have often reflected on how in ancient ages governance was achieved in a way that later times cannot hope to match; how in ancient times people were upright in a way that later times cannot hope to match; how in ancient times rites and music were illustrious in a way that later times cannot hope to match; and how in ancient times punishments and taxes were sparing and light in a way that later times cannot hope to match. Alas! Through ten thousand ages it has been this same heaven and earth, through ten thousand ages this same sun and moon, through ten thousand ages these same mountains and rivers—why is it that only when it comes to this age and these people…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
變而殊哉蓋有所由來者矣
古者分疆畫野以定民居布
德宣政以定民志養老慈幼
以哀民窮禁暴止亂以除民
患士生其間有鄉舉里選以
旌其善有圭田恒產以固其
節王政之大如此然所治不
===
過五服荒服之外不治也暨
聲教而已周弱秦暴盡廢先
王之良法美意後世不能推
本反諸正謂王政不可行而
雜霸雜夷士於是時退無恒
產進有定格精力疲于歲月
廉恥移于困窮古今之變異
punctuated: 變而殊哉？蓋有所由來者矣。古者分疆畫野以定民居，布德宣政以定民志，養老慈幼以哀民窮，禁暴止亂以除民患。士生其間，有鄉舉里選以旌其善，有圭田恒產以固其節。王政之大如此，然所治不過五服，荒服之外不治也，暨聲教而已。周弱秦暴，盡廢先王之良法美意。後世不能推本反諸正，謂王政不可行，而雜霸雜夷。士於是時，退無恒產，進有定格，精力疲于歲月，廉恥移于困窮。古今之變異，
translation_en: … change and become different? Truly, there is a reason from which this derives. In antiquity, they divided boundaries and demarcated territories to settle the people's dwellings, spread virtue and proclaimed governance to settle the people's aspirations, nourished the aged and showed compassion to the young to pity the people's distress, and prohibited violence and stopped disorder to remove the people's afflictions. For scholars born in that era, there were district recommendations and village selections to honor their goodness, and sacrificial fields (guitian) and constant livelihoods (hengchan) to make firm their integrity. Such was the greatness of kingly governance; yet what it governed did not exceed the Five Zones of Submission (wufu)—beyond the Wild Zone (huangfu), it did not govern directly, extending only its prestige and teachings. When the Zhou grew weak and the Qin grew tyrannical, they completely abolished the good laws and fine intentions of the former kings. Later ages were unable to trace back to the roots and return them to rectitude; claiming that kingly governance could not be practiced, they mixed in the ways of hegemons and the ways of barbarians. At such times, scholars in retirement have no constant livelihood, and in advancing are bound by fixed qualifications; their vital energy is exhausted over the months and years, and their sense of honor and shame is altered by poverty and distress. The changes and differences between antiquity and the present …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
至于虎如之何其可相及而
不相反哉雖然世可變而人
不可變人可變而心不可變
心可變而理不可變孔子不
曰性相近也習相遠也孟子
所以道性善稱堯舜孔孟生
于衰周憫王政之湮微俗習
===
之汙下乃述六經作七篇俾
後世願治之主籍是可以致
王道有志之士緣是可以立
天德是以去古雖遠而或理
或亂斯人卒不淪于禽獸夷
狄者蓋有不變者存焉欽惟
我
punctuated: 至于虎，如之何其可相及而不相反哉？雖然，世可變而人不可變，人可變而心不可變，心可變而理不可變。孔子不曰「性相近也，習相遠也」？孟子所以道性善，稱堯、舜。孔、孟生于衰周，憫王政之湮微、俗習之汙下，乃述《六經》、作七篇，俾後世願治之主籍是可以致王道，有志之士緣是可以立天德。是以去古雖遠，而或理或亂，斯人卒不淪于禽獸、夷狄者，蓋有不變者存焉。欽惟我
translation_en: … have reached this extreme [?], how could they possibly catch up with one another and not instead be mutually opposed? Even so, the age may change, yet people cannot change; people may change, yet the mind cannot change; the mind may change, yet principle cannot change. Did not Confucius say, "By nature, men are nearly alike; by practice, they get to be wide apart"? That is why Mencius discoursed on the goodness of human nature and always cited Yao and Shun. Confucius and Mencius were born during the decline of the Zhou; grieving over theobscuration and decay of kingly governance and the debasement of customs and habits, they transmitted the Six Classics and composed the Seven Books [the Mencius], enabling rulers of later generations who desired good order to rely on these to attain the Kingly Way, and scholars of high aspiration to follow these to establish heavenly virtue. Therefore, although we are far removed from antiquity, whether in times of order or disorder, the reason people ultimately do not sink to the level of birds and beasts or barbarians is because that which does not change remains preserved therein. I reverently reflect that our …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖皇帝受命創業用夏變夷遵
六典以建官約三代而封建
語治道則躋虞周語家法則
陋漢宋蓋後三代而獨追古
者是以
列聖承承咸臻有道今
皇帝在位允恪遵成憲恭默賢才
===
君濟斯世聖賢之道具乎書發爲
諸士乎學古入官將以相吾
文章曲折盡矣獨不可反之
身心爲自得之學乎山澤之
叟田野之夫目未嘗知詩書
口未嘗談仁義而其真誠朴
如者不移乎習也斯與古之
punctuated: 太祖皇帝受命創業，用夏變夷，遵六典以建官，約三代而封建。語治道則躋虞、周，語家法則陋漢、宋，蓋後三代而獨追古者。是以列聖承承，咸臻有道。今皇帝在位，允恪遵成憲，恭默賢才。君濟斯世，聖賢之道具乎書，發爲諸士乎，學古入官，將以相吾文章，曲折盡矣，獨不可反之身心，爲自得之學乎？山澤之叟，田野之夫，目未嘗知《詩》、《書》，口未嘗談仁義，而其真誠朴如者，不移乎習也，斯與古之
translation_en: … Grand Progenitor Emperor received the Mandate and founded the dynasty, transforming the barbarians through Chinese civilization, following the Six Canons to establish offices, and summarizing the institutions of the Three Dynasties to enfeoff princes. Speaking of his way of governance, it ascended to that of Yu and Zhou; speaking of his dynastic family regulations, they made Han and Song look base. Indeed, coming after the Three Dynasties, he alone pursued antiquity. Therefore, the successive Sacred Emperors carried on the heritage, all attaining the Way of good order. Now that the reigning Emperor is on the throne, he truly and reverently observes the established constitutions, in reverent silence [seeking?] worthy talents. [Note: column order in the original appears transposed here: "You scholars study antiquity to enter office, wherewith to assist our ruler in rescuing this world; the Way of the sages and worthies is complete in books, and when expressed as essays, its intricacies are exhausted."] … [to assist our] ruler in rescuing this world; the Way of the sages and worthies is complete in books, and is expressed as [essays?]; you scholars [?], studying antiquity to enter office, wherewith to assist our [ruler, expressed as] essays, its intricacies are exhausted—yet can you not reflect it back upon your own person and mind to make it learning acquired for oneself? The old men of the mountains and marshes and the rustics of the fields have never known the Odes and Documents with their eyes, nor ever spoken of benevolence and righteousness with their mouths, yet their genuine sincerity and simple plainness are not altered by habit; how does this differ from [people] of ancient…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
世之人何異是不可變之徵
也諸士子乃欲以學校詩書
移其性乎慎其習吾以爲聖
賢可至也豈特如古之世之
人哉諸士子思而勗之立不
變之地以挽其變者可也是
爲序
===
山東東昌府清平縣儒學教
諭趙欽謹序
punctuated:
世之人何異？是不可變之徵也。諸士子乃欲以學校詩書移其性乎？慎其習，吾以爲聖賢可至也，豈特如古之世之人哉！諸士子思而勗之，立不變之地以挽其變者，可也。是爲序。

山東東昌府清平縣儒學教諭趙欽謹序。
translation_en:
…How do they differ from the people of ancient ages? This is proof of what cannot be changed. Would you scholars, then, allow the Classic of Odes and Classic of Documents taught in the schools to alter your innate nature? If you are careful about your habits, I believe even the state of the sages and worthies can be attained—how could you merely be like the ordinary people of ancient ages! Reflect upon this, scholars, and exert yourselves: take your stand on unchanging ground so as to turn back what has changed, and all will be well. This serves as the preface.

Respectfully prefaced by Zhao Qin 趙欽, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qingping County 清平縣, Dongchang Prefecture 東昌府, Shandong 山東.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
禮之用和爲貴先王之道斯爲美小大由之
有所不行知和而和不以禮節之亦不可
行也
悠久所以成物也
我善養吾浩然之氣敢問何謂浩然之氣曰
難言也其爲氣也至大至剛以直養而無
害則塞于天地之間其爲氣也配義與道
===
無是餒也是集義所生者非義襲而取之
也行有不慊於心則餒矣我故曰告子未
嘗知義以其外之也必有事焉而勿正心
勿忘勿助長也
易
七日來復天行也利有攸往剛長也
恒亨无咎利貞利有攸往彖曰恒久也剛上
而柔下雷風相與巽而動剛柔皆應恒恒
亨无咎利貞久於其道也天地之道恒久
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
禮之用，和爲貴。先王之道，斯爲美，小大由之。有所不行，知和而和，不以禮節之，亦不可行也。
悠久，所以成物也。
我善養吾浩然之氣。「敢問何謂浩然之氣？」曰：「難言也。其爲氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其爲氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。行有不慊於心，則餒矣。我故曰，告子未嘗知義，以其外之也。必有事焉而勿正，心勿忘，勿助長也。」
易
七日來復，天行也。利有攸往，剛長也。
恒：亨，无咎，利貞，利有攸往。《彖》曰：恒，久也。剛上而柔下，雷風相與，巽而動，剛柔皆應，恒。恒亨，无咎，利貞，久於其道也。天地之道，恒久
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"In the application of ritual propriety, harmony is to be prized. Of the ways of the Former Kings, this is what made them admirable, and in things both small and great we follow them. Yet there are cases where this cannot be put into practice: if one knows the value of harmony and pursues harmony for its own sake, without regulating it by means of ritual propriety, that too cannot be put into practice."

"Being enduring and long-lasting is that whereby things are brought to completion."

"'I am good at nourishing my flood-like qi.' 'May I venture to ask what is meant by flood-like qi?' He replied: 'It is difficult to put into words. As for this qi, it is supremely great and supremely unyielding. If it is nourished with uprightness and suffered no harm, it will fill the space between Heaven and Earth. As for this qi, it is the companion of righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves. It is born from the accumulation of righteous deeds, not something seized through a single sporadic display of righteousness. Whenever one's conduct leaves any dissatisfaction in the heart, it starves. Therefore I say that Gaozi (告子) has never understood righteousness, because he regards it as external. One must always be engaged in this work, yet without fixed anticipation; do not let the heart forget, yet do not try to help it grow.'"

Book of Changes (Yijing)

"'In seven days comes its return': this is the movement of Heaven. 'It is advantageous to have somewhere to go': the firm is growing."

"Heng (恒, Duration): Success, no blame; advantageous to be steadfast and upright; advantageous to have somewhere to go. The Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan 彖) says: Heng means long-lasting. The firm is above and the柔 [yielding] is below; thunder and wind act together; mild and yet moving; the firm and the yielding lines all correspond to one another: this is Heng. 'Heng, success, no blame, advantageous to be steadfast and upright' means enduring in its proper Way. The Way of Heaven and Earth is enduring and long-lasting…"

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
而不已也利有攸往終則有始也日月得
天而能久照四時變化而能久成聖人久
於其道而天下化成觀其所恒而天地萬
物之情可見矣
默而成之不言而信存乎德行
易曰憧憧往來朋從爾思子曰天下何思何
慮天下同歸而殊塗一致而百慮天下何
思何慮日往則月來月往則日來日月相
推而明生焉寒往則暑來暑往則寒來寒
===
暑相推而歲成焉往者屈也來者信也屈
信相感而利生焉
書
帝曰來禹汝亦昌言禹拜曰都帝予何言予
思日孜孜皐陶曰吁如何禹曰洪水滔天
浩浩懷山襄陵下民昏墊予乘四載隨山
刊木曁益奏庶鮮食予決九川距四海濬
畎澮距川曁稷播奏庶艱食鮮食懋遷有
無化居烝民乃粒萬邦作乂皐陶曰俞師
punctuated:
而不已也。利有攸往，終則有始也。日月得天而能久照，四時變化而能久成，聖人久於其道而天下化成；觀其所恒，而天地萬物之情可見矣。
默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。
《易》曰：「憧憧往來，朋從爾思。」子曰：「天下何思何慮？天下同歸而殊塗，一致而百慮。天下何思何慮？日往則月來，月往則日來，日月相推而明生焉。寒往則暑來，暑往則寒來，寒暑相推而歲成焉。往者屈也，來者信也，屈信相感而利生焉。」
書
帝曰：「來，禹！汝亦昌言。」禹拜曰：「都！帝，予何言？予思日孜孜。」皐陶曰：「吁！如何？」禹曰：「洪水滔天，浩浩懷山襄陵，下民昏墊。予乘四載，隨山刊木，曁益奏庶鮮食。予決九川，距四海，濬畎澮，距川；曁稷播，奏庶艱食鮮食。懋遷有無化居，烝民乃粒，萬邦作乂。」皐陶曰：「俞！師…
translation_en:
…without ceasing. "It is advantageous to have somewhere to go" means that when there is an end, there is a beginning. The sun and moon, having attained their place in heaven, can shine enduringly; the four seasons, changing and transforming, can bring things to completion enduringly; the sage, enduring long in his Way, transforms and perfects all under heaven. By observing that in which things endure, the nature of heaven, earth, and the myriad things can be seen.
To accomplish it in silence, and to command trust without words, lies in virtuous conduct.
The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Unsettled in going and coming, only your friends will follow your thoughts." The Master said: "What need is there for thought and anxious deliberation in the world? In the world, all things return to the same destination though by different paths, and reach the same result though through a hundred deliberations. What need is there for thought and anxious deliberation in the world? When the sun goes, the moon comes; when the moon goes, the sun comes; the sun and moon propel each other, and brightness is born therefrom. When cold goes, heat comes; when heat goes, cold comes; cold and heat propel each other, and the year is completed therefrom. What goes away contracts; what comes expands. Contraction and expansion act upon one another, and benefit is born therefrom."
Book of Documents (Shu)
The Emperor said, "Come, Yu! Do you also utter splendid words." Yu bowed and said, "Oh! Emperor, what can I say? I think only of being diligent day by day." Gao Yao said, "Alas! How is that?" Yu said, "The floodwaters swelled to heaven; vast and boundless, they encircled the mountains and overtopped the hills, and the common people were bewildered and overwhelmed. I rode in my four conveyances, moving along the mountains and hewing the trees, and together with Yi procured fresh food for the multitudes. I opened up the nine rivers to reach the four seas, and dredged the field channels and ditches to reach the rivers; and together with Ji sowed the grain, procuring for the multitudes hard-won food and fresh food. I urged the exchange of what they had for what they had not, and the disposal of accumulated stores, so that the multitude of the people obtained grain to eat, and the myriad states were brought to order." Gao Yao said, "Yes! We should take as our model…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
汝昌言
江漢朝宗于海九江孔殷沱潛既道雲土夢
作乂
昔在文武聰明齊聖小大之臣咸懷忠良其
侍御僕從罔匪正人以旦夕承弼厥辟出
入起居罔有不欽發號施令罔有不臧下
民祗若萬邦咸休
簡乎有衆惟貌有稽無簡不聽具嚴天威
詩
===
有嚴有翼共武之服共武之服以定王國玁
狁匪茹整居焦穫侵鎬及方至于涇陽織
文鳥章白旆央央元戎十乘以先啓行戎
車既安如輊如軒四牡既佶既佶且閑薄
伐玁狁至于太原文武吉甫萬邦爲憲
假樂君子顯顯令德宜民宜人受祿于天保
右命之自天申之干祿百福子孫千億穆
穆皇皇宜君宜王不愆不忘率由舊章威
儀抑抑德音秩秩無怨無惡率由羣匹受
punctuated:

「江漢朝宗于海，九江孔殷，沱潛既道，雲土、夢作乂。」
「昔在文武，聰明齊聖，小大之臣，咸懷忠良；其侍御僕從，罔匪正人，以旦夕承弼厥辟，出入起居，罔有不欽，發號施令，罔有不臧，下民祗若，萬邦咸休。」

「假樂君子，顯顯令德，宜民宜人，受祿于天；保右命之，自天申之。干祿百福，子孫千億。穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王；不愆不忘，率由舊章。威儀抑抑，德音秩秩；無怨無惡，率由羣匹。受
