… your splendid words."

"The Jiang and the Han pay court as to a sovereign to the sea; the Nine Rivers are brought into complete order; the Tuo and the Qian have been guided into their channels; the land of Yun appears, and Meng is brought under cultivation."

"Formerly, under Kings Wen and Wu, who were perceptive, astute, impartial, and sagely, their ministers, great and small, all cherished loyalty and goodness. Their attendants, charioteers, and personal followers were none of them other than upright men. Morning and evening they waited upon and assisted their sovereign, so that in his goings out and comings in, in his rising up and sitting down, there was nothing that was not reverent; in his issuing of commands and promulgation of orders, there was nothing that was not good. The lower people reverently complied, and the myriad states all enjoyed felicity."

"When verified among the multitude, examine also their countenance and demeanor. Where there is no verification, do not hear the case; in all things hold in awe the majesty of Heaven."

Book of Odes (Shi):

"Majestic and reverent, they attended to their military service; they attended to their military service to settle the royal state. The Xianyun did not reckon the cost; they occupied Jiaohuo in force, invading Hao and Fang as far as the north bank of the Jing. With woven patterns of bird emblems, the white streamers gleamed brightly. Ten great war chariots led the way to open the march. The war chariots were steady, balanced alike in front and behind; the four stallions were strong, both strong and well-trained. We smote the Xianyun as far as Taiyuan. Civil and martial is Jifu, a model to the myriad states."

"Admirable and amiable is the princely man, illustrious is his virtuous character! He orders well the common people and the officers, and receives his emolument from Heaven. Heaven protects, aids, and appoints him, renewing its favor from on high. In seeking emolument he gains a hundred blessings, and his descendants shall number a hundred million. August and majestic, fit to be lord, fit to be king; neither erring nor forgetting, he follows the ancient statutes. His dignified demeanor is circumspect, his virtuous reputation is orderly; without resentment or hatred, he follows the ways of his peers. Receiving…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
福無疆四方之綱之綱之紀燕及朋友百
辟卿士媚于天子不解于位民之攸塈
㮚此萬邦聞于四國
帝命式于九圍受小球大球爲下國綴旒何
天之休不競不絿不剛不柔敷政優優百
祿是遒受小共大共爲下國駿厖何天之
龍敷奏其勇不震不動不戁不竦百祿是
總武王載旆有虔秉鉞如火烈烈則莫我
敢曷
===
春秋
秋八月壬午大閱〔桓公六年〕
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯會

盟于踐土　天王狩于河陽〔僖公二十八年〕

齊師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗

福無疆，四方之綱。之綱之紀，燕及朋友。百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸塈。
㮚此萬邦，聞于四國。
帝命式于九圍，受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。不競不絿，不剛不柔，敷政優優，百祿是遒。受小共大共，爲下國駿厖，何天之龍。敷奏其勇，不震不動，不戁不竦，百祿是總。武王載旆，有虔秉鉞，如火烈烈，則莫我敢曷。

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公十八年〕公會晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子齊世子光伐鄭〔襄公九年〕
舍中軍〔昭公五年〕公會齊侯莒子邾子杞伯盟于
鄟陵〔昭公二十六年〕公會齊侯于夾谷　齊人來
歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕叔孫州仇帥師墮
郈　季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費〔定公十二年〕
禮記
貴者獻以爵賤者獻以散尊者舉觶卑者舉
===
角
是故先王本之情性稽之度數制之禮義合
生氣之和道五常之行使之陽而不散陰
而不密剛氣不怒柔氣不懾四暢交於中
而發作於外皆安其位而不相奪也然後
立之學等廣其節奏省其文采以繩德厚
律小大之稱比終始之序以象事行使親
疏貴賤長幼男女之理皆形見於樂
君子隱而顯不矜而莊不厲而威不言而信
punctuated:
公子貞帥師伐鄭。〔襄公十八年〕　公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。〔襄公九年〕

《禮記》
貴者獻以爵，賤者獻以散，尊者舉觶，卑者舉角。
是故先王本之情性，稽之度數，制之禮義，合生氣之和，道五常之行，使之陽而不散，陰而不密，剛氣不怒，柔氣不懾，四暢交於中而發作於外，皆安其位而不相奪也。然後立之學等，廣其節奏，省其文采，以繩德厚；律小大之稱，比終始之序，以象事行；使親疏、貴賤、長幼、男女之理，皆形見於樂。
君子隱而顯，不矜而莊，不厲而威，不言而信。
translation_en:
…Gongzi Zhen led a force to attack Zheng. [18th year of Duke Xiang] — The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, to attack Zheng. [9th year of Duke Xiang]
The middle army was abolished. [5th year of Duke Zhao] — The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and the Earl of Qi, and made a covenant at Zhuanling. [26th year of Duke Zhao] — The Duke met with the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. — The people of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. [10th year of Duke Ding] — Shusun Zhouqiu led a force and dismantled the walls of Hou. — Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led a force and dismantled the walls of Bi. [12th year of Duke Ding]
Record of Rites (Liji):
"Those of noble rank present their offerings with the jue cup; those of lowly rank present theirs with the san cup. Those of honored status raise the zhi goblet; those of humble status raise the jiao horn."
"Therefore, the former kings grounded it in human feelings and nature, examined it by means of degrees and numbers, and regulated it through ritual and righteousness. They brought it into harmony with the vital breath of life and guided the practice of the five constant virtues, causing the yang energy not to dissipate and the yin energy not to become overly dense, the firm spirit not to burst into anger and the gentle spirit not to cower in fear. When these four flow freely and intermingle within, and are manifested without, all rest securely in their proper places without encroaching upon one another. Only then did they establish grades of instruction for it, broaden its rhythms and cadences, and examine itspatterned adornments so as to measure the depth of virtue; they regulated the proportions of small and great, and arranged the sequence of beginning and end so as to symbolize the conduct of affairs; thus causing the principles governing near and distant kin, noble and base, elder and younger, and male and female all to become visibly manifested in music."
"The gentleman is hidden yet manifest; without self-importance, he is dignified; without severity, he is awe-inspiring; without speaking, he is trusted."

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第叄場
策五道
問自古帝王之君臨億兆既躬行道德以化
導天下尤垂訓立教以陶民生於至治之
域經傳具載可考而知也洪惟我
國家
聖祖神宗道隆德盛逺邁前古萬幾之暇製為
大誥為善陰隲孝順事實五倫書
宸翰輝煌須示中外無非欲人明五倫以惇道化
===
而已夫五倫一書紀古今能盡五倫之道
者夥矣請舉一二言之君道莫大乎敬天
法祖節儉剛明也古今能盡其道者可得
言與臣道莫先乎守法持正忠義廉介也
古今能盡其道者可得言與他如夫婦父
子昆弟朋友能盡其道者古今又誰與其
間抑果有合於
大誥為善陰隲孝順事實三書之旨與諸士子欽
服
punctuated:
第叄場

策五道

問：自古帝王之君臨億兆，既躬行道德以化導天下，尤垂訓立教以陶民生於至治之域，經傳具載，可考而知也。洪惟我國家，聖祖神宗，道隆德盛，逺邁前古，萬幾之暇，製為《大誥》、《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》、《五倫書》，宸翰輝煌，須示中外，無非欲人明五倫以惇道化而已。夫《五倫》一書，紀古今能盡五倫之道者夥矣，請舉一二言之。君道莫大乎敬天法祖、節儉剛明也，古今能盡其道者，可得言與？臣道莫先乎守法持正、忠義廉介也，古今能盡其道者，可得言與？他如夫婦、父子、昆弟、朋友，能盡其道者，古今又誰與？其間抑果有合於《大誥》、《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》三書之旨與？諸士子欽服
translation_en:
Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, when emperors and kings have ruled over the myriad people, they have not only personally practiced morality and virtue to transform and guide the world, but have especially handed down instructions and established teachings to mold the populace in the realm of supreme governance. These are fully recorded in the Classics and commentaries, and can be examined and known. Humbly considering our Dynasty, the Sacred Ancestor and Divine Progenitors possessed lofty Way and flourishing virtue, far surpassing former antiquity. In their leisure from the myriad affairs of state, they composed the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao), Secret Blessings for Doing Good (Wei shan yin zhi), True Exemplars of Filial Piety (Xiao shun shi shi), and Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wu lun shu). Their imperial writings shine brilliantly and have been promulgated [reading 頒 for 須] inside and outside the court, desiring nothing other than for people to understand the five human relationships so as to strengthen moral transformation. Now, the single work Book of the Five Human Relationships records a great many from past and present who were able to fulfill the Way of the five human relationships; allow me to raise a few points to discuss. In the Way of the ruler, nothing is greater than revering Heaven and modeling oneself on the ancestors, frugality, and firm clarity; can you speak of those in past and present who were able to fulfill this Way? In the Way of the minister, nothing comes before upholding the law and maintaining rectitude, loyalty, righteousness, and incorruptible integrity; can you speak of those in past and present who were able to fulfill this Way? As for the others—husband and wife, father and son, elder and younger brothers, and friends—who in past and present were able to fulfill their Way? And among them, are there indeed connections that accord with the purport of the three books, the Grand Pronouncements, Secret Blessings for Doing Good, and True Exemplars of Filial Piety? You gentlemen have reverently abided by…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖訓蓋亦有年必講之素明習之素熟矣幸為我
條舉以對
問大學一書聖賢進德之閫奧君天下者之
律令格例也昔真文忠公作為衍義首劉
聖賢性命道德之言旁采古今治亂安危
之迹凡帝王為治之序為學之本與夫格
物致知誠意正心脩身齊家之道皆大提
其要詳著其目將以稗聖學而補治道也
其格致之要曰明道術辨人才審治體察
===
民情誠正脩齊之要曰崇畏敬戒逸欲謹
言行正威儀重妃匹嚴內治定國本教戚
屬所以為治之序安在所以為學之本何
居所以明辨審察崇戒謹正與夫重嚴定
教之目又何如今日之問非以發難也諸
君子行且陟巍科膺顯位設預
經筵必將進讀以熙
聖學於無疆其可不素講而詳究之乎試悉陳之
問治教之道君天下者不可一日而不脩士
punctuated:
聖訓，蓋亦有年，必講之素明，習之素熟矣，幸為我條舉以對。

問：《大學》一書，聖賢進德之閫奧，君天下者之律令格例也。昔真文忠公作為《衍義》，首劉聖賢性命道德之言，旁采古今治亂安危之迹，凡帝王為治之序、為學之本，與夫格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家之道，皆大提其要，詳著其目，將以稗聖學而補治道也。其格致之要，曰明道術、辨人才、審治體、察民情；誠正脩齊之要，曰崇畏敬、戒逸欲、謹言行、正威儀、重妃匹、嚴內治、定國本、教戚屬。所以為治之序安在？所以為學之本何居？所以明、辨、審、察、崇、戒、謹、正，與夫重、嚴、定、教之目又何如？今日之問，非以發難也。諸君子行且陟巍科、膺顯位，設預經筵，必將進讀以熙聖學於無疆，其可不素講而詳究之乎？試悉陳之。

問：治教之道，君天下者不可一日而不脩，士
translation_en:
… the Sacred Instructions, presumably for some years now, and must have long expounded them clearly and practiced them thoroughly; pray enumerate your answers for me item by item.

Question: The book Great Learning (Daxue) is the inner sanctuary for sages and worthies in advancing their virtue, and the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and precedents for those who rule all under heaven. In former times, Zhen Wenzhonggong [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] composed the Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning] (Yanyi). At the outset, he arrayed [? 劉, for 列] the words of sages and worthies concerning human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue, and on all sides he gathered historical traces of order and disorder, security and peril, from antiquity to the present. Regarding the sequence of governance for emperors and kings, the foundation of their learning, as well as the ways of investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, and regulating the family—in all of these he broadly highlighted the essentials and set forth the sub-headings in detail, intending thereby to aid [? 稗, for 裨] sacred learning and supplement the way of governance. The essentials of investigating things and extending knowledge are called: clarifying theWay and its arts, distinguishing men of talent, examining the substance of governance, and observing the conditions of the people. The essentials of making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, and regulating the family are called: exalting awe and reverence, guarding against idleness and desires, being cautious in speech and conduct, rectifying dignified demeanor, attaching importance to the consort, maintaining strictness in the governance of the inner palace, establishing the foundation of the state [the heir apparent], and instructing imperial relatives. Wherein lies the sequence of governance? Wherein resides the foundation of learning? And what are the detailed sub-headings for clarifying, distinguishing, examining, observing, exalting, guarding, being cautious, rectifying, as well as attaching importance, maintaining strictness, establishing, and instructing? Today's question is not meant to pose a thorny conundrum. You gentlemen are about to ascend to the lofty examination ranks and receive illustrious offices; suppose you participate in the Classics Colloquium (jingyan), you will surely present readings to brighten the Emperor's Sacred Learning without bound—how could you not expound upon this beforehand and investigate it in detail? Try to set it forth in full.

Question: As for the way of governance and instruction, he who rules all under heaven cannot go a single day without cultivating it, and scholar-…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
君子不可一日而不講也安上治民莫善
於禮移風易俗莫善於樂虞之禮樂典於
夷夔後世莫能尚矣而制作又何待於周
公乎周之禮樂掌以宗伯後世莫能加矣
而正定又何假於孔子乎厥後禮之亡也
著者非一家若陳太常之禮書識者謂其
辯論精愽較之文公家禮何如今禮司於
朝廷之上者郁郁乎其盛矣然冠昏喪祭之用
春官行于
於民間者有未周何歟樂之亡也論者非
一輩若陳正字之樂書識者謂其綱羅綜
貫比之蔡氏新書何若今樂司於太常奏
于
===
朝廷之上者洋洋乎其盛矣然聲音器數之在
於民間者有未協何歟民為邦之本而親
民者守令也古之守令動稱龔黃卓魯今
守令之選多出科目而昔人之賢宜恒見
也何民力猶未阜成之績罕聞歟兵乃
punctuated: 君子不可一日而不講也。安上治民，莫善於禮；移風易俗，莫善於樂。虞之禮樂，典於夷、夔，後世莫能尚矣，而制作又何待於周公乎？周之禮樂，掌以宗伯，後世莫能加矣，而正定又何假於孔子乎？厥後禮之亡也，著者非一家，若陳太常之《禮書》，識者謂其辯論精愽，較之文公《家禮》何如？今禮司於春官，行于朝廷之上者，郁郁乎其盛矣，然冠、昏、喪、祭之用於民間者有未周，何歟？樂之亡也，論者非一輩，若陳正字之《樂書》，識者謂其綱羅綜貫，比之蔡氏《新書》何若？今樂司於太常，奏于朝廷之上者，洋洋乎其盛矣，然聲音器數之在於民間者有未協，何歟？民為邦之本，而親民者守令也。古之守令，動稱龔、黃、卓、魯；今守令之選，多出科目，而昔人之賢宜恒見也，何民力猶未阜，成之績罕聞歟？兵乃
translation_en: … [and scholar-]gentlemen cannot let a single day pass without discussing them. For securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than rites; for altering manners and changing customs, nothing is better than music. The rites and music of Yu [Shun] were presided over by Boyi 伯夷 and Kui 夔, whom later generations could not surpass; why then did their creation and institution have to await the Duke of Zhou 周公? The rites and music of Zhou were placed in the charge of the Minister of Rites (zongbo), to which later generations could add nothing; why then did their rectification and settlement have to rely on Confucius 孔子? Thereafter, following the loss of the rites, those who wrote on them were not of a single school. Take, for instance, the Treatise on Rites (Lishu) by Chamberlain for Ceremonials Chen [Chen Xiangdao 陳祥道], which men of discernment say is precise and broad in its disquisitions—how does it compare with Master Wen's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] Family Rituals (Jiali)? Today, the rites are administered by the Ministry of Rites (chunguan), and as practiced at court they are resplendently flourishing; yet why is it that the practice of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrificial rites among the common people remains incomplete? Following the loss of music, those who discussed it were not of a single generation. Take, for instance, the Treatise on Music (Yueshu) by Proofreader Chen [Chen Yang 陳暘], which men of discernment say is comprehensive and systematic—how does it compare with Mr. Cai's [Cai Yuan 定/Cai Yuanding 蔡元定] New Treatise [on Pitch-Pipes] (Lülü xinshu)? Today, music is administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as performed at court it is grandly flourishing; yet why is it that the tones, instruments, and numerical proportions found among the common people remain unharmonized? The people are the foundation of the state, and those who are close to the people are the prefects and magistrates. In speaking of ancient prefects and magistrates, one invariably cites Gong [Sui 龔遂], Huang [Ba 黃霸], Zhuo [Mao 卓茂], and Lu [Gong 魯恭]. Today, prefects and magistrates are mostly selected through the civil-service examinations, so the worthiness of the men of old ought regularly to be seen; why then is the people's strength still not abundant, and why are achievements of completion rarely heard of? The military is…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
國之衛而理兵者將師也古之將師動稱
起翦頗牧今將師之選類出世胄而昔將
之良宜倍出也何智勇尠少而決勝之策
罕聞歟方今
聖人在上於禮樂民兵四者尤惓惓焉伊欲冠昏
喪祭之禮比屋皆行而家無殊俗聲音律
呂之樂人人皆習而國□同風其道何施
伊欲守令皆賢而沛福澤於□□將師皆
良而鼓智勇於六軍其術安在諸士子進
===
用有日必能言之
問人之有師自聖人至於士一也故黃帝學
於大填顓頊學於錄圖帝嚳學於赤松子
堯學於君疇舜學於務成昭禹學於西王
國湯學於成子伯文王學於時子思武王
學於郭叔載之傳記有可考焉然黃帝至
於武王所謂繼天立極之聖人其道統心
法之相傳見諸經傳不誣矣以天生之神
聖反師於大填郭叔之徒謂其非師之
punctuated:
國之衛，而理兵者將師也。古之將師動稱起、翦、頗、牧，今將師之選類出世胄，而昔將之良宜倍出也；何智勇尠少，而決勝之策罕聞歟？方今聖人在上，於禮、樂、民、兵四者尤惓惓焉。伊欲冠、昏、喪、祭之禮比屋皆行，而家無殊俗；聲音、律呂之樂人人皆習，而國□同風，其道何施？伊欲守令皆賢，而沛福澤於□□；將師皆良，而鼓智勇於六軍，其術安在？諸士子進用有日，必能言之。

問：人之有師，自聖人至於士，一也。故黃帝學於大填，顓頊學於錄圖，帝嚳學於赤松子，堯學於君疇，舜學於務成昭，禹學於西王國，湯學於成子伯，文王學於時子思，武王學於郭叔，載之傳記，有可考焉。然黃帝至於武王，所謂繼天立極之聖人，其道統心法之相傳，見諸經傳不誣矣。以天生之神聖，反師於大填、郭叔之徒，謂其非師之
translation_en:
…the defense of the state, and those who manage the troops are the generals and commanders. The generals and commanders of antiquity are constantly cited as Bai Qi 白起, Wang Jian 王翦, Lian Po 廉頗, and Li Mu 李牧. Today, the selection of generals and commanders mostly comes from hereditary lineages, so the excellence of the generals of the past ought to appear twice as often; why then are wisdom and courage so scarce, and strategies for decisive victory rarely heard of? At present, the Sage is on the throne, and he is especially earnest regarding the four matters of ritual, music, the people, and the military. If one wishes for the rites of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice to be practiced in every household so that families have no disparate customs, and for the music of tones, voices, and pitch-pipes to be practiced by everyone so that the state [?] shares the same ethos—what way should be implemented? If one wishes for Prefects and Magistrates to all be worthy so as to shower blessings upon [?][?], and for generals and commanders to all be capable so as to rouse wisdom and courage in the Six Armies—wherein lies the method? You gentlemen will one day advance to take up office, and must certainly be able to speak of this.

Question: That men have teachers is the same from sages down to scholars. Thus the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) learned from Datian 大填, Zhuanxu 顓頊 learned from Lutu 錄圖, Emperor Ku 帝嚳 learned from Master Red Pine (Chisongzi 赤松子), Yao 堯 learned from Junchou 君疇, Shun 舜 learned from Wucheng Zhao 務成昭, Yu 禹 learned from Xiwang Guo 西王國, Tang 湯 learned from Cheng Zibo 成子伯, King Wen 文王 learned from Shi Zisi 時子思, and King Wu 武王 learned from Guo Shu 郭叔; these are recorded in biographical traditions and can be examined. Yet from the Yellow Emperor down to King Wu, they were the so-called sages who succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard; the transmission of their succession of the Way (daotong 道統) and method of the mind (xinfa 心法) is seen in the classics and commentaries without falsehood. That such heaven-born divine sages should on the contrary take the likes of Datian and Guo Shu as teachers—if we say they did not take them as teachers…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
歟而其説則出於孔門之高弟謂其師之
歟而授受之旨經傳無一語以及何歟自
是之後若孔子之於老聃左丘明之於孔
子公羊高穀梁赤之於子夏孟子之於子
思二程之於周子而皆謂之師弟子也或
又謂其不然學者不能無疑謂孔子不學
於老聃何以適周而問禮耶謂丘明果孔
子弟子何其傳經而失之誣耶謂公穀出
於子夏之門而春秋之成商也不能賛一
===
辭二子乃各以其經名家何耶謂孟子非
親炙子思何思誠之語與中庸同一揆耶
謂二程之學出於周子然叔子以伯子繼
孟子之絶學畧無一語以及周子抑又何
歟願究其源流詳著乎篇以祛古今之惑
問風俗人物關於
國家之氣運尚矣然輿圖之廣未易悉舉姑以
大江之西言之為藩維於天下統郡一十
有三其載於志也以言乎風俗或講誦以
punctuated:
歟？而其説則出於孔門之高弟。謂其師之歟？而授受之旨，經傳無一語以及，何歟？自是之後，若孔子之於老聃，左丘明之於孔子，公羊高、穀梁赤之於子夏，孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，而皆謂之師弟子也。或又謂其不然，學者不能無疑。謂孔子不學於老聃，何以適周而問禮耶？謂丘明果孔子弟子，何其傳經而失之誣耶？謂公、穀出於子夏之門，而《春秋》之成，商也不能賛一辭，二子乃各以其經名家，何耶？謂孟子非親炙子思，何「思誠」之語與《中庸》同一揆耶？謂二程之學出於周子，然叔子以伯子繼孟子之絶學，畧無一語以及周子，抑又何歟？願究其源流，詳著乎篇，以祛古今之惑。
問：風俗、人物關於國家之氣運尚矣。然輿圖之廣，未易悉舉，姑以大江之西言之。為藩維於天下，統郡一十有三，其載於志也：以言乎風俗，或講誦以
translation_en:
…? Yet this account comes from an eminent disciple of Confucius's school. Or if one says that they did take them as teachers, why is it that the Classics and commentaries have not a single word mentioning the purport of what they transmitted and received? After this, in cases such as Confucius in relation to Lao Dan 老聃, Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 in relation to Confucius, Gongyang Gao 公羊高 and Guliang Chi 穀梁赤 in relation to Zixia 子夏, Mencius in relation to Zisi 子思, and the two Chengs 二程 in relation to Master Zhou 周子 [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], all are spoken of as teacher and disciple. Yet some say this was not so, and scholars cannot be without doubt. If one says that Confucius did not study with Lao Dan, why did he go to Zhou to ask about ritual? If one says that Qiuming was indeed a disciple of Confucius, why did he, in transmitting the Classic, err in falsity? If one says that Gongyang and Guliang came from the school of Zixia, yet when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) was completed, Shang 商 [Zixia] could not add a single word—how then did the two masters each establish a renowned school of the Classic? If one says that Mencius did not personally receive instruction from Zisi, why do his words on "reflecting upon sincerity" follow the exact same principle as the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong)? If one says that the learning of the two Chengs came from Master Zhou, yet when the younger brother [Cheng Yi 程頤] stated that the elder brother [Cheng Hao 程顥] succeeded to the lost learning of Mencius, he had not a single word mentioning Master Zhou—why was this as well? Please investigate their origins and developments, and set them forth in detail in your essay to dispel the doubts of past and present.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
業衣冠萃止或忠孝繼出文獻相續者果
何地歟或士風貧薄矜謹節義或淳固愨
實先儒餘風果何方歟有士習詩書而農
勤稼穡風氣和平而人物秀顯與夫風流
儒雅民樂耕桑尚禮崇德勤力知分者矣
有吏民朴野而不嚚於訟廉耻儉嗇而事
簡民醇與夫伉健工巧抗志勵節民習淳
古士果而義者矣又有人厖淳而多壽考
家詩書而多儒雅而文風之盛甲於他郡
===
其風俗何其異哉以言乎人物有南州高
士與獨立物表者有運甓自勵與奮不顧
身者可指其人歟有拔身歸國與忠義自
奮者有才兼文武與峭直見忌者又可指
其人歟有沉毅果斷耻身後代歐陽齊名
直言清節者焉有講道驪湖力踐聖賢社
稷已任博極羣書者焉或篤好史學涵飫
六經捧土成塋膠漆友誼或操履勁特大
節不奪廉約守正嗜學不倦至於盡心匡
punctuated: 業，衣冠萃止；或忠孝繼出，文獻相續者，果何地歟？或士風貧薄，矜謹節義；或淳固愨實，先儒餘風，果何方歟？有士習詩書而農勤稼穡，風氣和平而人物秀顯，與夫風流儒雅、民樂耕桑、尚禮崇德、勤力知分者矣；有吏民朴野而不嚚於訟，廉耻儉嗇而事簡民醇，與夫伉健工巧、抗志勵節、民習淳古、士果而義者矣；又有人厖淳而多壽考，家詩書而多儒雅，而文風之盛甲於他郡，其風俗何其異哉！以言乎人物，有南州高士與獨立物表者，有運甓自勵與奮不顧身者，可指其人歟？有拔身歸國與忠義自奮者，有才兼文武與峭直見忌者，又可指其人歟？有沉毅果斷，耻身後代，歐陽齊名，直言清節者焉；有講道驪湖，力踐聖賢，社稷已任，博極羣書者焉。或篤好史學，涵飫六經，捧土成塋，膠漆友誼；或操履勁特，大節不奪，廉約守正，嗜學不倦。至於盡心匡
translation_en:
…their occupation, where the gentry gather; or places where loyalty and filial piety emerge in succession, and scholarly traditions continue unbroken—just which places are these? Or where the literati ethos is impoverished yet proud and scrupulous in moral integrity; or where it is simple, steadfast, and honest, retaining the lingering风 (customs) of former Confucians—just which regions are these? There are places where scholars study the Odes and Documents while farmers are diligent in sowing and reaping, where the local ethos is harmonious and tranquil and the notable figures are refined and eminent, along with those marked by cultured elegance, where the people delight in farming and sericulture, esteeming ritual, honoring virtue, working diligently, and knowing their lot. There are places where clerks and commoners are plain and rustic and not given to deceitful litigation, having a sense of shame and frugality so that official business is simple and the people are pure, along with those who are vigorous, robust, and skillful in crafts, exalting their ambitions and sharpening their integrity, where the commoners' habits are simple and antique, and the scholars are resolute and righteous. And there are also places where the people are generous and pure and many enjoy long life, where families study the Odes and Documents and many are cultured and refined, so that the flourishing of their literary culture ranks first among all other prefectures—how varied indeed are these customs!

As for notable figures: there was the "Lofty Scholar of the Southern Prefecture" (Nanzhou gaoshi) and the one who stood independent beyond the material world; there was the one who moved bricks to spur himself on and the one who roused himself without regard for his own life—can you point out who these men were? There was the one who extricated himself to return to his state and the one who roused himself in loyalty and righteousness; there was the one whose talents encompassed both the civil and the military and the one who incurred jealousy for his stern uprightness—can you also point out who these men were? There were those who were composed, resolute, and decisive, or who were ashamed to live on into a succeeding dynasty, or who matched Ouyang Xiu in fame, or who were known for forthright speech and pure integrity; there were those who lectured on the Way at Lihu (Ehu / Goose Lake), or who strenuously put into practice the teachings of the sages and worthies, or who took the altars of state as their personal responsibility, or who were exhaustively learned in all books. Some were deeply fond of historical studies or steeped in the Six Classics, or carried earth in their hands to build a parent's tomb, or formed friendships as fast as glue and lacquer; others were firm and distinctive in conduct, unyielding in great moral principles, incorruptible, frugal, and upright, or untiring in their love of learning. As for those who devoted their whole hearts to rectifying…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
直臣韓愈並稱至死不屈以節義自許力
排和議奏疏爭光於日月九死不悔正氣
獨存於宇宙其人物抑何盛哉然民俗本
於士風人物盛則風俗美方今
聖化鼓舞動盪而人物之盛風俗之淳超邁往古
諸士子生長是邦聞而見之審矣當考其
實而論其世於風俗之不同者思以同之
於人物之可法者思以法之請著于篇以
觀居德善俗之學
punctuated: 直臣韓愈並稱，至死不屈，以節義自許；力排和議，奏疏爭光於日月；九死不悔，正氣獨存於宇宙。其人物抑何盛哉！然民俗本於士風，人物盛則風俗美。方今聖化鼓舞動盪，而人物之盛、風俗之淳，超邁往古。諸士子生長是邦，聞而見之審矣。當考其實而論其世，於風俗之不同者思以同之，於人物之可法者思以法之。請著于篇，以觀居德善俗之學。
translation_en: …ranked alongside the upright minister Han Yu 韓愈, and those who remained unyielding unto death, priding themselves on integrity and righteousness; those who vigorously rejected peace negotiations, their memorials rivaling the sun and moon in brilliance; and those who felt no regret even facing death nine times over, their righteous spirit enduring alone throughout the cosmos. How flourishing indeed are such figures! Yet popular customs are rooted in the ethos of the literati; when notable figures flourish, customs are admirable. At present, the sagely transformative influence inspires and stirs the realm, so that the flourishing of notable figures and the purity of customs surpass those of antiquity. You gentlemen, born and raised in this region, have heard and seen these things thoroughly. You ought to examine the realities and discuss their eras, reflecting on how to harmonize customs where they differ, and how to emulate figures who are worthy of emulation. Please set this forth in your essays, so that we may observe your learning in abiding in virtue and improving customs.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
四書義
禮之用和爲貴先王之道斯爲美小大由之
有所不行知和而和不以禮節之亦不可
行也
趙鏓
同考試官教諭黄　批〔禮嚴而和和而節乃禮之全〕
〔體不可分爲二也此作得之〕
同考試官教諭桂　批〔作此題者多失旨惟是篇得〕
〔之録以示學者〕
===
同考試官教諭詹　批〔文理貫通筆力老健可取〕
同考試官學正張　批〔理明詞贍盖用心於本領者〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔明白可采〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔題似易而難作者多遺於理〕
〔而畧於詞詞理俱到無如此作〕
賢者論禮之所以可行而必言其所以不可行也
盖禮之所以可行者以其用之貴於和而先王之
所尚也苟一於和而不節之以禮則失其本然矣
夫豈可行哉且禮原於天命具於人心人非禮不
punctuated:
四書義

「禮之用，和爲貴。先王之道，斯爲美；小大由之。有所不行，知和而和，不以禮節之，亦不可行也。」

趙鏓
同考試官教諭黄　批：〔禮嚴而和，和而節，乃禮之全體，不可分爲二也。此作得之。〕
同考試官教諭桂　批：〔作此題者多失旨，惟是篇得之，録以示學者。〕

考試官教諭趙　批：〔題似易而難，作者多遺於理而畧於詞。詞理俱到，無如此作。〕

賢者論禮之所以可行，而必言其所以不可行也。盖禮之所以可行者，以其用之貴於和，而先王之所尚也；苟一於和而不節之以禮，則失其本然矣，夫豈可行哉？且禮原於天命，具於人心。人非禮不
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books (Sishu yi)

"In the application of the rites, harmony is to be prized. Of the ways of the former kings, this is the most admirable; in matters small and great they followed it. Yet there are cases where this cannot be put into practice: to know harmony and pursue harmony alone, without regulating it by the rites—this likewise cannot be put into practice."

By Zhao Cong 趙鏓.
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Huang comments: [That the rites are strict yet harmonious, and harmonious yet regulated, constitutes the complete substance of the rites; they cannot be divided into two. This composition grasps that.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Gui comments: [Those who write on this topic mostly miss its purport; this piece alone grasps it. Record it to show to scholars.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhan comments: [Its argumentation and principles are thoroughly coherent, and its brush-strength is seasoned and vigorous. Worthy of selection.]
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zhang comments: [Its principles are clear and its diction is rich; evidently the work of someone who has applied his mind to the fundamentals.]
Examiner, Instructor Wu comments: [Clear and worthy of adoption.]
Examiner, Instructor Zhao comments: [The topic seems easy yet is difficult; writers mostly neglect the underlying principle and are cursory in their diction. For achieving both diction and principle, none surpasses this composition.]

The worthy discusses why the rites can be put into practice, yet necessarily speaks of why they cannot be put into practice. For the reason the rites can be put into practice is that in their application harmony is prized, which was what the former kings esteemed; yet if one is wholly devoted to harmony and does not regulate it by the rites, then their intrinsic nature is lost—how then could that be put into practice? Moreover, the rites originate in the Mandate of Heaven and are complete within the human mind. Without the rites, a person cannot…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
立禮待人而行是禮也其體雖嚴而其用則和如
君上臣下分固嚴矣然皆出於自然之理故其交
際之間必從容不迫乃為可貴如父坐子立分亦
嚴矣是皆本於自然之天故其相接之頃必安舒
自如乃為可尚彼先王之道禮之所在也曷嘗外
於自然乎此其所以為美而事之小者如曲禮三
千之類無不由之焉先王之道禮之所寓也何嘗
有所勉強乎此其所以為貴而事之大者如經禮
三百之屬莫不從之焉夫禮之尚於和者固可行
===
矣然猶有所不行者何哉蓋以其和而無節用而
遺體也如君臣交際徒知和之為貴而流於和不
復以禮節之則堂陛陵夷無所嚴憚而君臣之禮
缺矣夫豈可行乎如父子相接徒知和之可尚而
一於和不復以禮制之則狎恩恃愛□□□□而
父子之分乖矣又豈可行乎是知禮必以和□□
和必以禮為節體用相須斯為無弊有子言之以
示人厥旨微矣雖然禮之在人不可一日而無本
之於身形之於家國天下者在是致中和位天地
punctuated: 立，禮待人而行。是禮也，其體雖嚴，而其用則和。如君上臣下，分固嚴矣，然皆出於自然之理，故其交際之間，必從容不迫，乃為可貴。如父坐子立，分亦嚴矣，是皆本於自然之天，故其相接之頃，必安舒自如，乃為可尚。彼先王之道，禮之所在也，曷嘗外於自然乎？此其所以為美，而事之小者，如曲禮三千之類，無不由之焉。先王之道，禮之所寓也，何嘗有所勉強乎？此其所以為貴，而事之大者，如經禮三百之屬，莫不從之焉。夫禮之尚於和者，固可行矣，然猶有所不行者，何哉？蓋以其和而無節，用而遺體也。如君臣交際，徒知和之為貴，而流於和，不復以禮節之，則堂陛陵夷，無所嚴憚，而君臣之禮缺矣，夫豈可行乎？如父子相接，徒知和之可尚，而一於和，不復以禮制之，則狎恩恃愛，□□□□，而父子之分乖矣，又豈可行乎？是知禮必以和□□，和必以禮為節，體用相須，斯為無弊。有子言之以示人，厥旨微矣。雖然，禮之在人，不可一日而無。本之於身，形之於家國天下者在是；致中和、位天地、
translation_en: … establish himself, and ritual awaits men in order to be practiced. As for this ritual, although its substance is strict, its function is harmonious. For instance, the ruler above and the minister below—their distinction in status is certainly strict; yet all of this issues from natural principle, so in their intercourse they must be unhurried and unforced for it to be prized. Or for instance, the father seated and the son standing—their distinction in status is likewise strict; all of this is rooted in natural Heaven, so in the moments when they meet they must be at ease and natural for it to be esteemed. That Way of the Former Kings is where ritual resides; how could it ever lie outside what is natural? This is why it is admirable, and in minor matters—such as the three thousand rules of detailed ceremony (quli)—there is none that does not proceed from it. The Way of the Former Kings is where ritual is lodged; how could there ever be anything forced in it? This is why it is prized, and in great matters—such as the three hundred rules of cardinal ceremony (jingli)—there is none that does not follow it. Now, when ritual esteems harmony, it can certainly be practiced; yet why is there still a point where it cannot be practiced? It is because one is harmonious without restraint, attending to the function while neglecting the substance. For instance, if in the intercourse of ruler and minister they merely know that harmony is prized and drift into harmony without any longer regulating it by ritual, then the distinction between the hall and the steps will be eroded, there will be no awe or reverence, and the ritual between ruler and minister will be wanting—how then could it be practiced? Or if in the meeting of father and son they merely know that harmony is to be esteemed and devote themselves solely to harmony without any longer restraining it by ritual, then they will presume upon kindness and rely on affection, [4 illegible characters, probably meaning "losing all sense of respect"], and the proper distinction between father and son will be violated—how could that be practiced either? Thus we know that ritual must take harmony [2 illegible characters: as its function (為用)], and harmony must take ritual as its restraint; when substance and function depend upon each other, then there is no defect. When Master You (Youzi 有子) spoke of this to instruct others, his meaning was subtle indeed. Even so, ritual in man cannot be absent for a single day. What is rooted in the person and manifested in the family, the state, and all under Heaven lies in this; achieving equilibrium and harmony, placing Heaven and Earth in their proper positions, …
