悠久所以成物也
一
楊廉
同考試官學正陳　批〔作者往往以功業爲外而不知久之兼内此作得之且文足以發是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭吾　批發揮聖人與天地同用
得旨
考試官教諭趙　批〔認理真佳作也〕
===
功業有常而天下化成此聖人與天地同用也夫
聖人之功業常於内外而不已者一至誠之所致
也使其無常豈能化成天下而與天地同其用哉
中庸二十六章論至誠之德積中著外而及於此
意謂聖人之功業本以悠遠致高厚而高厚又悠
久也自其悠久言之功業之積非徒浩乎其廣博
淵乎其深厚而已吾見其氣象寛緩表裏如
是而無終窮之可言也功業之發非徒巍乎其
punctuated:
育萬物者在是。苟非和敬，則失其中正而倚於一偏，行之於身且不可，況可推之於天下國家、位天地、育萬物哉？若有子者，可謂達禮樂之本矣。

「悠久，所以成物也。」一
楊廉
同考試官學正陳　批：〔作者往往以功業爲外，而不知久之兼内。此作得之，且文足以發是，宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭吾　批：發揮聖人與天地同用，得旨。
考試官教諭趙　批：〔認理真，佳作也。〕

功業有常而天下化成，此聖人與天地同用也。夫聖人之功業，常於内外而不已者，一至誠之所致也。使其無常，豈能化成天下，而與天地同其用哉？《中庸》二十六章論至誠之德積中著外而及於此，意謂：聖人之功業，本以悠遠致高厚，而高厚又悠久也。自其悠久言之：功業之積，非徒浩乎其廣博、淵乎其深厚而已；吾見其氣象寛緩，表裏如是，而無終窮之可言也。功業之發，非徒巍乎其…
translation_en:
… and nourishing the myriad things reside in this. If there is not both harmony and reverence, one loses impartiality and correctness and leans to one side; it cannot even be practiced in one's own person, how much less can it be extended to the empire, the state, and the family, to set Heaven and Earth in their places and nourish the myriad things? Someone like Master You (Youzi 有子) may truly be said to have grasped the foundation of rites and music.

"Long-enduring, and thus it brings things to completion." [1st answer]
Yang Lian 楊廉
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen 陳 comments: 〔Writers often treat meritorious achievements as external and fail to understand that endurance encompasses the internal as well. This composition has grasped this point, and its prose suffices to bring it out; it ought to be selected for publication.〕
Examiner, District Director of Studies Wu 吾 comments: It brings out how the sage shares the same function as Heaven and Earth, grasping the essential meaning.
Examiner, District Director of Studies Zhao 趙 comments: 〔Its grasp of principle is genuine; a fine composition.〕

When meritorious achievements have constancy and the world is transformed and brought to completion, this is how the sage shares the same function as Heaven and Earth. Now, that the sage's meritorious achievements remain constant both internally and externally without ceasing is entirely brought about by utmost sincerity. Were they without constancy, how could they transform and bring the world to completion, sharing the same function as Heaven and Earth? Chapter 26 of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) discusses how the virtue of utmost sincerity accumulates within and manifests without, and arriving at this passage, its meaning is that the sage's meritorious achievements originally attain height and thickness through being far-reaching and long-lasting, and that this height and thickness are themselves long-enduring. Speaking from the standpoint of their being long-enduring: the accumulation of meritorious achievements is not merely vast in its breadth andabyssal in its depth and thickness; we see that its manner is unhurried and expansive, being thus both on the surface and within, with no end or exhaustion that can be spoken of. The manifestation of meritorious achievements is not merely lofty in its…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
大煥乎其光明而已吾見其功效優裕外如是內
如是而無止極之可擬也唯其博厚之悠久也則
凡物之載於我者皆有以遂其生而四海九州凞
然於至治之域其視地之博厚久載而品物流形
者何殊耶惟其高明之悠久也則凡物之覆於我
者皆有以安其所而八荒四表翕然於大化之中
其視天之高明久覆而萬物並育者何異耶噫天
地悠久而有以成乎物聖人悠久而與之同其用
至誠之功業一何盛哉雖然以形而論天地聖人
===
為有異以誠而論天地聖人為不殊人知聖人之
功業配乎天地而不知其至誠之功為不息人知
聖人之至誠同乎天地而不知其成物之功為尤
大盖天地非聖人無以立其極而聖人非天地無
以著其功然則聖人天地其相參而為三者與
我善養吾浩然之氣敢問何謂浩然之氣曰
難言也其為氣也至大至剛以直養而無
害則塞于天地之間其為氣也配義與道
無是餒也是集義所生者非義襲而取之
punctuated:
大，煥乎其光明而已；吾見其功效優裕，外如是，內如是，而無止極之可擬也。唯其博厚之悠久也，則凡物之載於我者，皆有以遂其生，而四海九州凞然於至治之域，其視地之博厚久載而品物流形者，何殊耶？惟其高明之悠久也，則凡物之覆於我者，皆有以安其所，而八荒四表翕然於大化之中，其視天之高明久覆而萬物並育者，何異耶？噫！天地悠久而有以成乎物，聖人悠久而與之同其用，至誠之功業一何盛哉！雖然，以形而論，天地聖人為有異；以誠而論，天地聖人為不殊。人知聖人之功業配乎天地，而不知其至誠之功為不息；人知聖人之至誠同乎天地，而不知其成物之功為尤大。盖天地非聖人無以立其極，而聖人非天地無以著其功。然則聖人天地，其相參而為三者與！

「我善養吾浩然之氣。」「敢問何謂浩然之氣？」曰：「難言也。其為氣也，至大至剛，以直養而無害，則塞于天地之間。其為氣也，配義與道；無是，餒也。是集義所生者，非義襲而取之…」
translation_en:
…great, and brilliantly luminous; I see that their efficacious effects are abundant and unhurried, thus on the outside and thus on the inside, with no limit that can be compared to them. Precisely because this breadth and thickness are long-enduring, all things borne up by the sage are able to fulfill their lives, and the Four Seas and Nine Provinces flourish harmoniously within the realm of ultimate order—how does this differ from the earth, which in its breadth and thickness long bears things up so that the myriadthings flow into form? And precisely because this loftiness and brilliance are long-enduring, all things sheltered by the sage are able to rest securely in their places, and the Eight Wildernesses and Four Reaches are united within the great transformation—how is this any different from heaven, which in its loftiness and brilliance long shelters things so that the myriad things are nourished together? Ah! Heaven and earth are long-enduring and thereby bring things to completion; the sage is long-enduring and shares in their function. How magnificent indeed are the achievements of utmost sincerity! Even so, if discussed in terms of physical form, heaven, earth, and the sage are different; if discussed in terms of sincerity, heaven, earth, and the sage are no different. People know that the achievements of the sage match those of heaven and earth, yet they do not know that the work of his utmost sincerity is unceasing; people know that the utmost sincerity of the sage is the same as that of heaven and earth, yet they do not know that his achievement in bringing things to completion is especially great. For without the sage, heaven and earth have no means to establish their ultimate standard, and without heaven and earth, the sage has no means to manifest his achievement. This being so, do not the sage, heaven, and earth form a triad with one another?

"I am good at nourishing my flood-like qi." "May I ask what is meant by flood-like qi?" He said: "It is difficult to put into words. Such is this qi: it is supremely great and supremely unyielding. If it is nourished with uprightness and not harmed, then it fills the space between heaven and earth. Such is this qi: it is the companion of righteousness and the Way; without these, it starves. It is born from the accumulation of righteous deeds, not seized by a sporadic display of righteousness…"

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
行湯之政成王繼序不忘此其敬天法祖蓋
與我
太祖之遇旱憂農徒步請禱
太宗之繼承天位恪遵成憲者同一道焉禹之菲
食惡衣周文之卑服即功武帝斥田蚡之請
孝宣辨燕王之誣此其節儉剛明蓋與我
太祖之不作苑臺以費民財
太宗之辨民交通特釋其罪者同一揆焉以臣道
言之莫先於守法持正也莫先於忠義蕭何
===
也如犯蹕之止於罰金不肯順旨故人必正
以贓罪不徇私恩非張釋之蘇章之守法乎
龍鬪洧淵力拒禳祟之請帝欲廢立廷爭而
不奉詔非子產周昌之持正乎至如我
朝宋文為天策知事守將欲擅殺人而力爭
其不可卒蒙賚予之榮較諸張釋之蘇章之
輩何讓拒蘇峻之逆賊而父死於忠子死於
孝當祿山之不道而兄死於前弟死於後此
卞壼顏杲卿之忠義也以不貪為寶而不寶
punctuated:
行湯之政，成王繼序不忘。此其敬天法祖，蓋與我太祖之遇旱憂農、徒步請禱，太宗之繼承天位、恪遵成憲者，同一道焉。禹之菲食惡衣，周文之卑服即功，武帝斥田蚡之請，孝宣辨燕王之誣。此其節儉剛明，蓋與我太祖之不作苑臺以費民財，太宗之辨民交通、特釋其罪者，同一揆焉。

以臣道言之，莫先於守法持正也，莫先於忠義蕭何也。如犯蹕之止於罰金，不肯順旨；故人必正以贓罪，不徇私恩，非張釋之、蘇章之守法乎？龍鬪洧淵，力拒禳祟之請；帝欲廢立，廷爭而不奉詔，非子產、周昌之持正乎？至如我朝宋文為天策知事，守將欲擅殺人而力爭其不可，卒蒙賚予之榮，較諸張釋之、蘇章之輩何讓？拒蘇峻之逆賊，而父死於忠、子死於孝；當祿山之不道，而兄死於前、弟死於後，此卞壼、顏杲卿之忠義也。以不貪為寶，而不寶
translation_en:
… practiced the governance of Tang, and King Cheng succeeded to the line without forgetting his predecessors. In their reverence for Heaven and emulation of the ancestors, they shared the very same Way as our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), who, worried for the farmers during a drought, walked on foot to pray for rain, and our Grand Ancestor (Taizong), who upon succeeding to the heavenly throne strictly abided by the established institutions. Yu ate meager food and wore coarse clothes; King Wen of Zhou dressed humbly and devoted himself to his work; Emperor Wu of Han rebuffed the request of Tian Fen 田蚡; and Emperor Xiaoxuan of Han saw through the false accusation against the Prince of Yan (Huo Yu 霍禹 [?]). In their frugality, firmness, and clarity of judgment, they followed the very same principle as our Grand Progenitor, who refused to build park terraces lest he waste the people's wealth, and our Grand Ancestor, who discerned the truth about commoners accused of treasonous collusion and specially absolved them of guilt.

Speaking of the Way of the minister, nothing comes before upholding the law and maintaining rectitude, and nothing comes before loyalty, righteousness, and spotless integrity [蕭何 for 廉介?]. For instance, insisting that violating the imperial procession's cleared route merited only a fine and refusing to bend to the sovereign's wish, or insisting on punishing an old friend for the crime of corruption without indulging private favor—was this not the upholding of the law by Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 and Su Zhang 蘇章? When dragons fought in the abyss of the Wei River, firmly refusing the request to perform exorcistic sacrifices; or when the Emperor wished to depose the heir apparent and install another, arguing against it at court and refusing to carry out the edict—was this not the maintenance of rectitude by Zichan 子產 and Zhou Chang 周昌? As for our own dynasty, when Song Wen 宋文 served as Administrative Clerk (zhishi) of the Tiance Guard, the defending general wanted to kill people without authorization, and Song forcefully argued that this was impermissible, ultimately receiving the honor of imperial rewards; how is he any inferior when compared to the likes of Zhang Shizhi and Su Zhang? Resisting the rebel traitor Su Jun 蘇峻 so that the father died in loyalty and the sons died in filial piety, or facing the lawless rebellion of An Lushan 安祿山 so that the elder cousin died first and the younger died after—this was the loyalty and righteousness of Bian Kun 卞壼 and Yan Gaoqing 顏杲卿. Taking non-covetousness as one's treasure rather than treasuring …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
金玉以清白遺子孫而不計產業此司城子
罕司徒楊震之廉介也至若我
朝孫炎為處州總制禁黠之徒欲脅以降而罵
賊以死終獲爵土之封較諸卞壼顏杲卿之
儔何亞古者百里負米之仲由名有家法之
公綽與今之母病不愈吮疽嘗糞之李英親
沒哀慟蔬食廬墓之張翼同一父子之盡道
也可知古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺不忘糟
糠之宋弘與今之夫溺水而自投二屍並出
===
之袁氏夫死不嫁雙節並稱之俞氏同一夫
婦之盡道也可見若趙孝趙禮之爭死不懼
逆式張元之雖死不易以至不肯分財異居
隨所欲取之李貞非古今能盡兄弟朋友之
倫者乎然以五倫一書質之於
大誥孝順事實為善陰隲三書之旨則
大誥所載君臣同游者非五倫書所謂盡君臣之
道者乎孝順事實所載武王之達孝非五倫
書所謂盡父子之倫者乎為善陰隲所載馮
punctuated: 金玉，以清白遺子孫而不計產業，此司城子罕、司徒楊震之廉介也。至若我朝孫炎為處州總制，禁黠之徒欲脅以降，而罵賊以死，終獲爵土之封，較諸卞壼、顏杲卿之儔何亞？古者百里負米之仲由、名有家法之公綽，與今之母病不愈、吮疽嘗糞之李英，親沒哀慟、蔬食廬墓之張翼，同一父子之盡道也可知。古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺、不忘糟糠之宋弘，與今之夫溺水而自投、二屍並出之袁氏，夫死不嫁、雙節並稱之俞氏，同一夫婦之盡道也可見。若趙孝、趙禮之爭死不懼，逆式、張元之雖死不易，以至不肯分財異居、隨所欲取之李貞，非古今能盡兄弟、朋友之倫者乎？然以《五倫》一書質之於《大誥》、《孝順事實》、《為善陰隲》三書之旨，則《大誥》所載「君臣同游」者，非《五倫書》所謂盡君臣之道者乎？《孝順事實》所載武王之達孝，非《五倫書》所謂盡父子之倫者乎？《為善陰隲》所載馮
translation_en: …gold and jade, and bequeathing incorruptibility to one's descendants without reckoning family property—this was the incorruptible integrity of Minister of Works Zihan 子罕 and Minister over the Masses Yang Zhen 楊震. And when we come to our dynasty's Sun Yan 孫炎, who served as Regional Commander of Chuzhou: when the unruly and cunning rebels sought to coerce him into surrender, he cursed the bandits and went to his death, ultimately receiving a posthumous enfeoffment of nobility and territory; compared with the likes of Bian Kun 卞壼 and Yan Gaoqing 顏杲卿, how was he any inferior? In antiquity, Zhong You 仲由, who carried rice on his back from a hundred li away, and Liu Gongchuo 柳公綽, who was renowned for his family discipline, along with in the present era Li Ying 李英, who sucked abscesses and tasted feces when his mother's illness did not heal, and Zhang Yi 張翼, who mourned in grief upon his parent's death, eating coarse vegetables and dwelling in a hut by the grave—it can be known that all alike fulfilled the Way of father and son. In antiquity, Ji Que 冀缺, where husband and wife treated each other with the respect due to a guest, and Song Hong 宋弘, who did not forget the wife who had shared his chaff and husks, along with in the present era Madam Yuan 袁氏, who threw herself into the water when her husband drowned so that their two corpses emerged together, and the ladies of the Yu 俞氏 family, who refused to remarry after their husbands died and were jointly praised for their twin chastity—it can be seen that all alike fulfilled the Way of husband and wife. As for Zhao Xiao 趙孝 and Zhao Li 趙禮, who vied with each other to die without fear; Fan Shi 范式 [transcribed as 逆式][?] and Zhang Yuan 張元 [Zhang Shao 張劭], whose devotion remained unchanged even in death; down to Li Zhen 李貞, who refused to divide the family property or live apart, letting his brothers take whatever they wished—were these not men of ancient and modern times capable of fulfilling the human relations of elder and younger brother, and of friends? Yet if we examine the single book Treatise on the Five Human Relations (Wulun shu 五倫書) against the purport of the three books—the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao 大誥), True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi 孝順事實), and Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi 為善陰隲)—then is not the section on "Ruler and Minister Sharing Fellowship" recorded in the Grand Pronouncements what the Treatise on the Five Human Relations calls fulfilling the Way of ruler and minister? Is not the far-reaching filial piety of King Wu 武王 recorded in the True Records of Filial Piety what the Treatise on the Five Human Relations calls fulfilling the human relation of father and son? And do not the accounts recorded in the Secret Merits of Doing Good of Feng…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
式嬰嚚叔通瑕蹬不與五倫書所謂盡夫婦
之道者同一意歟是則五倫之理包天括地
而是書足以該之三書之旨殊塗異轍而是
書足以會之溥天率土不賓烏號之弓而寶
此書四方萬國不藏曲阜之履而藏此書斯
世斯民得以盡彝倫惇道化熙熙然於光天
化日之下可以匹休唐虞三代之治者豈無
所自
第二問
===
同考試官學正陳　批〔欵欵對詳明必熟於大學衍義　者也兼學如此場屋幾人〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔條答無遺且忠愛之意溢於　言表蓋久學而有志者歟歟羨歎羨〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔答問詳悉非熟於衍義者不能〕
對甚矣天下不可一日無大學之書而衍義
一書亦不可以一日不講也脩己治人之道
於焉而存化民成俗之本於焉而在涵養君
punctuated:
式、嬰嚚、叔通、瑕蹬，不與《五倫書》所謂盡夫婦之道者同一意歟？是則五倫之理，包天括地，而是書足以該之；三書之旨，殊塗異轍，而是書足以會之。溥天率土，不賓烏號之弓，而寶此書；四方萬國，不藏曲阜之履，而藏此書。斯世斯民，得以盡彝倫、惇道化，熙熙然於光天化日之下，可以匹休唐虞三代之治者，豈無所自？

第二問
同考試官學正陳　批〔欵欵對詳明，必熟於《大學衍義》者也。兼學如此，場屋幾人！〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔條答無遺，且忠愛之意溢於言表，蓋久學而有志者歟！歟羨，歎羨！〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔答問詳悉，非熟於《衍義》者不能。〕

對：甚矣，天下不可一日無《大學》之書，而《衍義》一書，亦不可以一日不講也！脩己治人之道，於焉而存；化民成俗之本，於焉而在；涵養君
translation_en:
…[Feng] Shi 馮式, [Liang] Yingyin 梁嬰嚚 [?], Shutong 叔通 [Liang Hong 梁鴻], and Xiadeng 瑕蹬 [Sun Xiadeng 孫瑕蹬?]: are these not of the very same purport as what the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu 五倫書) calls fulfilling the Way of husband and wife? Thus, the principles of the five human relationships encompass heaven and earth, and this book suffices to embrace them all; the aims of the three books follow different paths and tracks, and this book suffices to bring them together. Throughout the whole world, to the very margins of the land, people do not prize as a heirloom the Wuhao bow, but treasure this book; in all the four quarters and the myriad states, people do not store away the sandals of Qufu, but store away this book. That this age and this people are able to fulfill the constant human relationships and thicken moral transformation, living in harmonious contentment beneath the bright sky and transforming sun, so as to rival thesplendid governance of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties—how could this be without its source?

Second Question
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies (xuezheng 學正) Chen comments: [Each point is answered with clarity and detail; this must be someone thoroughly conversant with the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi 大學衍義). How many in the examination compound possess such breadth of learning!]
Examiner and District Director of Studies (jiaoyu 教諭) Wu comments: [The itemized responses leave nothing out, and a spirit of loyalty and devotion overflows beyond the words; surely this is one who has studied long and holds high aspirations! Admirable [?], truly admirable!]
Examiner and District Director of Studies Zhao comments: [The answers to the questions are detailed and thorough; none but one well versed in the Extended Meaning could achieve this.]

Response: Indeed! The world cannot go a single day without the book of the Great Learning (Daxue 大學), nor can the book of the Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning] go a single day without being expounded! The Way of cultivating oneself and governing others is preserved therein; the root of transforming the people and perfecting customs resides therein; and the nourishing of the ruler's…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
德緝熙聖學亦莫不於是而基學者一日不
由乎此則流於異端惑於邪說無以開發聰
明而措諸事業君天下者一日不由於此則
身有不脩化有不行而天下不得蒙至治之
澤此西山真文忠公衍義之所以作而執事
之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟愚雖不敏敢不
紬繹舊聞以荅明問之萬一乎夫大學一書
其經出於孔氏其傳出於曾子二程爲之表
章朱子爲之章句綱領條目畢備無遺誠聖
===
賢進德之閫奧君天下者之律例格令後世
莫能尚已至宋真文忠公當理宗之朝圖致
治之道以爲治道莫大於大學於是首𠛬聖
賢性命道德之言旁采古今治亂安危之迹
推本帝王爲治之序探求帝王爲學之本詳
著格物致知誠意正心脩身齊家之要而及
其目以爲衍義一書其所以闡義理之淵微
發聖賢之未發爲帝王之監戒豈小補哉觀
其述帝堯克明峻德而致黎民於變皐謨身
punctuated:
德、緝熙聖學，亦莫不於是而基。學者一日不由乎此，則流於異端，惑於邪說，無以開發聰明而措諸事業；君天下者一日不由於此，則身有不脩，化有不行，而天下不得蒙至治之澤。此西山真文忠公《衍義》之所以作，而執事之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟？愚雖不敏，敢不紬繹舊聞，以荅明問之萬一乎！

夫《大學》一書，其經出於孔氏，其傳出於曾子；二程爲之表章，朱子爲之章句，綱領條目畢備無遺，誠聖賢進德之閫奧，君天下者之律例格令，後世莫能尚已。至宋真文忠公當理宗之朝，圖致治之道，以爲治道莫大於《大學》，於是首𠛬聖賢性命道德之言，旁采古今治亂安危之迹，推本帝王爲治之序，探求帝王爲學之本，詳著格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家之要，而及其目，以爲《衍義》一書。其所以闡義理之淵微，發聖賢之未發，爲帝王之監戒，豈小補哉！觀其述帝堯「克明峻德」而致「黎民於變」，《皐謨》「身…
translation_en:
… the ruler's virtue and continuously illuminating sagely learning also have their foundation in nothing other than this. If scholars do not follow this for even a single day, they will drift into heterodoxy and be deluded by perverse doctrines, having no means to develop their intelligence and apply it to practical undertakings. If he who rules the world does not follow this for even a single day, his personal conduct will go uncultivated, his transforming influence will not take effect, and the world will be unable to receive the blessings of consummate governance. Is this not why Zhen Wenzhonggong 真文忠公 [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] of Xishan 西山 composed the Extended Meaning [of the Great Learning, Daxue yanyi], and why Your Excellency so earnestly questions us students about it? Though I am dull-witted, how dare I not draw out what I have previously learned in order to answer even one ten-thousandth of your discerning inquiry?

Now, as for the book of the Great Learning (Daxue), its classic text came from Confucius and its commentary from Master Zeng 曾子. The two Cheng 程 brothers [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] brought it to prominence, and Master Zhu 朱子 [Zhu Xi 朱熹] arranged it into chapters and phrases (Daxue zhangju). Its guiding principles and specific items are complete without omission; truly it is the inner sanctum for sages and worthies in advancing their virtue, and the statutes, precedents, regulations, and ordinances for one who rules the world, which later generations cannot surpass. Coming to the Song dynasty, Zhen Wenzhonggong, serving at the court of Emperor Lizong 理宗, sought the way to bring about good governance. Believing that nothing in the way of governance is greater than the Great Learning, he first set forth [? 𠛬, for 列] the words of sages and worthies on human nature, destiny, the Way, and virtue, and extensively gathered historical traces of order and disorder, security and peril from antiquity to the present. He traced the fundamental sequence by which emperors and kings effect governance, and explored the foundation of learning for emperors and kings. He set out in detail the essentials of investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, and regulating the family, extending to their sub-items, so as to compose the book Extended Meaning. In elucidating the profound subtleties of moral principle, expressing what the sages and worthies had left unexpressed, and serving as a mirror and admonition for emperors and kings, how could this be of merely minor benefit! Looking at his account of how Emperor Yao 帝堯 "was able to make illustrious his lofty virtue" and thereby brought "the black-haired people to be transformed," and in the Counsels of Gao Yao (Gaomo), how "cultivating the person…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩思永而邇可遠在茲與夫四海雖遠致治
在心之語則帝王爲治之序可知矣述伊訓
太甲立愛惟親立敬惟長以終於四海詩美
文王刑于寡妻至于兄弟以御于家邦與夫
治天下有本身之謂也之言又豈不可見其
序哉其述堯舜禹湯文武或執中懋德或宅
心建極以至勉彊學問行道之辭則帝王爲
學之本可知矣述漢唐魏陳諸君或以王霸
雜治或以音律爲高以至或專文賦游宴之
===
樂夫豈得其本哉其格物致知之要曰明道
術其目則天理人心之正吾道源流之正異
端之差王霸之異也而審治體非在分德刑
先後別義利輕重乎曰辨人材其目則聖賢
觀人之法帝王知人之事姦雄之術憸邪之
情也而察民情非在生靈嚮背田里休戚乎
若夫誠意正心之要曰崇畏敬則崇脩已事
天之敬崇遇灾臨民之敬及夫操存省察之
功規警箴戒之助並曰戒逸欲則戒沈湎于
punctuated: 脩思永而邇可遠在茲，與夫「四海雖遠，致治在心」之語，則帝王爲治之序可知矣。述《伊訓》、《太甲》「立愛惟親，立敬惟長」以終於四海，《詩》美文王「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦」，與夫「治天下有本，身之謂也」之言，又豈不可見其序哉？其述堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，或執中懋德，或宅心建極，以至勉彊學問、行道之辭，則帝王爲學之本可知矣。述漢、唐、魏、陳諸君，或以王霸雜治，或以音律爲高，以至或專文賦游宴之樂，夫豈得其本哉？其格物致知之要：曰「明道術」，其目則天理人心之正、吾道源流之正、異端之差、王霸之異也；而「審治體」，非在分德刑先後、別義利輕重乎？曰「辨人材」，其目則聖賢觀人之法、帝王知人之事、姦雄之術、憸邪之情也；而「察民情」，非在生靈嚮背、田里休戚乎？若夫誠意正心之要：曰「崇畏敬」，則崇脩己事天之敬、崇遇灾臨民之敬，及夫操存省察之功、規警箴戒之助；並曰「戒逸欲」，則戒沈湎于
translation_en:
…cultivating the person with thoughts of perpetuity so that what is near can reach what is far right here, along with the statement that "though the Four Seas are distant, bringing about order lies in the mind"—from these, the sequence of how emperors and kings govern can be known. When he recounts the Instructions of Yi (Yixun) and Tai Jia on "establishing love beginning with relatives, and establishing respect beginning with elders" and extending ultimately to all within the Four Seas; the Odes (Shi) praising King Wen for "setting an example for his consort, extending to his brothers, and so governing his family and state"; together with the words "governing the empire has a root: it refers to the person"—how could one not see this sequence in them as well? When he recounts Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—whether holding fast the Mean and exerting themselves in virtue, or settling the mind and establishing the supreme standard, down to their words on tirelessly pursuing learning and practicing the Way—from these, the root of learning for emperors and kings can be known. And when he recounts the various rulers of Han, Tang, Wei, and Chen—whether governing by a mixture of the Kingly Way and Hegemony, or prizing musical pitch-pipes as lofty, down to devoting themselves exclusively to the pleasures of literary compositions, rhapsodies, excursions, and banquets—how could they have grasped the root?

As for his essentials of investigating things and extending knowledge: First is "Clarifying the Way and Its Arts," whose sub-items are the correctness of Heavenly Principle and the human mind, the orthodoxy of the origin and transmission of our Way, the deviations of heterodox teachings, and the distinction between the Kingly Way and Hegemony; and as for "Examining the Substance of Governance," does it not lie in distinguishing the priority of virtue and punishment, and differentiating the relative weight of righteousness and profit? Next is "Discerning Men of Talent," whose sub-items are the methods by which sages and worthies observe men, the affairs by which emperors and kings know men, the stratagems of treacherous heroes, and the dispositions of sycophantic and wicked men; and as for "Investigating the Conditions of the People," does it not lie in the allegiance or alienation of the living souls, and the joys and sorrows of the rural villages?

As for the essentials of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind: First is "Revering Awe and Reverence," which means revering the reverence of cultivating oneself and serving Heaven, revering the reverence of encountering disasters and overseeing the people, as well as the effort of preserving the mind and self-examination, and the aid of remonstrances, warnings, and admonitions; and together with this is "Guarding Against Indulgence and Desires," which means guarding against being sunk in…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
酒戒荒淫於色及夫盤逸游田之戒窮奢極
修之戒也謹言行為脩身之要則發號施令
之際其可以不慎正威儀為脩身之要則在
宮在廷之容不可以不謹若夫齊家之要不
外乎重妃匹嚴內治也謹選立之道賴規警
之益以至內臣忠謹之禍非其目而何又不
外乎定國本教戚屬建立之討宜蚤諭教之
法宜豫以至外家驕溢之禍非其目而何夫
大學之綱目如彼其大而詳衍義之具載又
如此其備而切信矣哉聖賢進德之方帝王
致治之道不可一日無者也雖然明大學之
道在致知推大學之道在力行而所以致知
力行之方則又在一敬而已愚生於此實踐
之功固有所未盡而探討之功則未嘗不力
倘蒙執事與而進之使得立
玉階寸地續
翠幄一貂敢不以平生所學竭涓埃以助
海嶽之萬一乎謹對
punctuated: 酒、戒荒淫於色，及夫盤逸游田之戒、窮奢極修之戒也。謹言行為脩身之要，則發號施令之際，其可以不慎？正威儀為脩身之要，則在宮在廷之容，不可以不謹。若夫齊家之要，不外乎重妃匹、嚴內治也。謹選立之道，賴規警之益，以至內臣忠謹之禍，非其目而何？又不外乎定國本、教戚屬。建立之討宜蚤，諭教之法宜豫，以至外家驕溢之禍，非其目而何？夫《大學》之綱目如彼其大而詳，《衍義》之具載又如此其備而切。信矣哉！聖賢進德之方、帝王致治之道，不可一日無者也。雖然，明《大學》之道在致知，推《大學》之道在力行，而所以致知力行之方，則又在一敬而已。愚生於此，實踐之功固有所未盡，而探討之功則未嘗不力。倘蒙執事與而進之，使得立玉階寸地，續翠幄一貂，敢不以平生所學，竭涓埃以助海嶽之萬一乎？謹對。
translation_en:
… wine, warning against licentiousness in sensual pleasure, as well as warnings against amusement, idleness, and hunting excursions, and warnings against extreme luxury and extravagance [reading 修 as 侈]. Being cautious in speech and conduct is an essential of cultivating the person; when issuing proclamations and commands, how could one not be careful? Rectifying one's dignified demeanor is an essential of cultivating the person; one's deportment in the palace and at court cannot but be circumspect. As for the essentials of regulating the family, they are nothing other than valuing the royal consort and strictly governing the inner palace. Being cautious in the way of selecting and establishing the consort, relying on the benefit of her admonition and warning, down to the calamities caused by eunuchs—even those deemed loyal and cautious [?]—what are these if not its detailed items? Furthermore, they are nothing other than fixing the foundation of the state [the heir apparent] and instructing imperial relatives by marriage. Deliberations [reading 討 as 計] on establishing the heir should be made early, and the methods of instructing and guiding him should be prepared beforehand, down to the calamities of arrogance and excess among the consort clans—what are these if not its detailed items?

Now, the main principles and detailed items of the Great Learning (Daxue) are as grand and detailed as that, and what is fully recorded in the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) is as comprehensive and pertinent as this. Truly indeed! As the method by which sages and worthies advance in virtue and the way by which emperors and kings bring about good governance, they cannot be dispensed with for a single day. Even so, illuminating the Way of the Great Learning lies in extending knowledge, carrying out the Way of the Great Learning lies in strenuous practice, and the method by which to extend knowledge and practice strenuously lies simply in a single word: reverence (jing). In this regard, while your foolish student has admittedly not yet exhausted the effort of practical application, in the effort of inquiry and investigation I have never failed to exert myself. Should I be favored by Your Excellency's approval and advancement, so that I am enabled to stand upon an inch of ground at the jade steps and add a sable tail at the kingfisher-curtained throne, how would I dare not take what I have learned throughout my life and exhaust my tiny drops and specks of dust to assist, in some ten-thousandth part, the seas and mountains of imperial rule? I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第三問
王佐
同考試官學正張　批〔治教一策關涉甚大此作識人情善措置而又不失治教之本用世之士也高薦〕
何𥘉
考試官教諭吾　批〔策有處置非識義理達時務者不能録出允當〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔究政教之本酌時措之宜可謂達於治體者表而出之〕
===
君天下者莫先於脩政而立教成政敎者必
本於制禮以作樂盖政教不舉固不足以言
治禮樂不脩又何以為政教之本君天下者
可不知所本乎執事以此為問其期待愚生
以用世之意非淺淺也敢不援古據今以對
夫禮以辨上下樂以和民情虞之禮樂本於
帝舜之德而典以夷夔三禮脩而五禮明六
律和而八音諧後世固莫能尚矣然禮緣人
情樂隨風氣而損益先王之舊以備一代之
punctuated:
第三問
王佐
同考試官學正張　批〔治教一策，關涉甚大。此作識人情，善措置，而又不失治教之本，用世之士也。高薦。〕
何𥘉
考試官教諭吾　批〔策有處置，非識義理、達時務者不能。録出允當。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔究政教之本，酌時措之宜，可謂達於治體者。表而出之。〕

君天下者，莫先於脩政而立教；成政敎者，必本於制禮以作樂。盖政教不舉，固不足以言治；禮樂不脩，又何以為政教之本？君天下者，可不知所本乎？執事以此為問，其期待愚生以用世之意，非淺淺也。敢不援古據今以對！夫禮以辨上下，樂以和民情。虞之禮樂，本於帝舜之德，而典以夷、夔；三禮脩而五禮明，六律和而八音諧，後世固莫能尚矣。然禮緣人情，樂隨風氣，而損益先王之舊以備一代之
translation_en:
Third Policy Question
Wang Zuo 王佐
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Zhang 張 comments: [This policy question on governance and moral transformation has immense bearing. This composition understands human sentiment, excels at practical arrangement, and yet does not lose sight of the fundamentals of governance and instruction. He is a scholar useful to the world. Highly recommended.]
He Chu 何𥘉 [on Wang Zuo's paper?]
Examiner, County Instructor (jiaoyu) Wu 吾 comments: [This policy essay contains practical arrangements that could not be made by anyone who does not understand moral principles and comprehend current affairs. Selecting it for publication is entirely fitting.]
Examiner, County Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: [It investigates the root of governance and instruction, and weighs the appropriateness of timely measures. The author may be called one who understands the essentials of governance. Singled out and published.]

For one who rules all under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over cultivating governance and establishing moral instruction; for bringing governance and instruction to completion, one must necessarily take the institution of rites and the creation of music as the foundation. Indeed, if governance and instruction are not promoted, it is certainly insufficient to speak of order; yet if rites and music are not cultivated, how then can one establish the foundation of governance and instruction? How could one who rules all under Heaven not know where the foundation lies? In asking about this, Your Excellency's expectation that this foolish student be of service to the world is by no means shallow. How dare I not cite antiquity and draw upon the present in reply! Now, rites serve to distinguish superior and inferior, and music serves to harmonize the feelings of the people. The rites and music of Yu 虞 were rooted in the virtue of Emperor Shun 舜 and administered by伯夷 Boyi and 夔 Kui; the Three Rites were cultivated and the Five Rites made clear, the six pitch-pipes were harmonized and the eight timbres brought into accord—later ages certainly could not surpass them. Yet rites follow human feelings and music accords with the prevailing customs, so subtracting from and adding to the old institutions of the former kings in order to provide the…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
制者不能不有待於周公也周之禮樂成於
周公之手而典以宗伯有五禮以親邦民六
樂以和神人後世固莫能加矣然聖王不作
禮樂廢壞而斟酌先王之制以爲萬世之法
者不能不有俟於孔子也厥後嬴秦無道典
籍煨燼禮之亡也著者非一家若曾褒之漢
禮韋公肅之新儀王彥威之曲臺惟陳太常
之禮書辯論精博雖識者所愛然較之文公
家禮謹名分崇愛敬以爲之本略浮文務本實
===
以爲之用者則不及焉今禮司於春官行於
朝廷之上者郁郁乎其盛可以匹休於虞周矣
而冠昏喪祭之典頒在有司燦然備具然民
間行之有未周者特以承之者有未至而勢
未能革其因襲之弊也樂之亡也論者非一
䒢若聶冠卿之樂圖胡瑗之樂記房庶之補
亡惟陳正字之樂書網羅綜貫雖識者所許
然比之蔡氏新書本原器數之咸備辭約理
明之易曉者則未若焉今樂司於太常奏於
punctuated: 制者，不能不有待於周公也。周之禮樂，成於周公之手，而典以宗伯，有五禮以親邦民，六樂以和神人，後世固莫能加矣。然聖王不作，禮樂廢壞，而斟酌先王之制，以爲萬世之法者，不能不有俟於孔子也。厥後嬴秦無道，典籍煨燼。禮之亡也，著者非一家，若曾褒之《漢禮》、韋公肅之《新儀》、王彥威之《曲臺》，惟陳太常之《禮書》辯論精博，雖識者所愛，然較之文公《家禮》謹名分、崇愛敬以爲之本，略浮文、務本實以爲之用者，則不及焉。今禮司於春官，行於朝廷之上者，郁郁乎其盛，可以匹休於虞、周矣。而冠、昏、喪、祭之典，頒在有司，燦然備具；然民間行之有未周者，特以承之者有未至，而勢未能革其因襲之弊也。樂之亡也，論者非一䒢，若聶冠卿之《樂圖》、胡瑗之《樂記》、房庶之《補亡》，惟陳正字之《樂書》網羅綜貫，雖識者所許，然比之蔡氏《新書》本原、器數之咸備，辭約理明之易曉者，則未若焉。今樂司於太常，奏於
translation_en: … institutions could not but await the Duke of Zhou. The rites and music of the Zhou were completed by the hand of the Duke of Zhou and administered by the Minister of Rites (Zongbo); there were the Five Rites to bring harmony to the people of the states, and the Six Musical Dances to harmonize spirits and men, such that later ages truly could not surpass them. Yet when sage kings no longer arose, rites and music fell into decay, and weighing and adapting the institutions of the former kings to make a standard for ten thousand generations could not but await Confucius. Thereafter, the Ying-surname Qin was without the Way, and the canonical texts were reduced to ashes. Following the loss of the rites, those who wrote on them were not of a single school—such as Zeng Bao's Han Rites (Hanli), Wei Gongsu's New Ceremonials (Xinyi), and Wang Yanwei's Rites of the Qu Terrace (Qutai). Only Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Chen's [Chen Xiangdao's] Book of Rites (Lishu) was precise and broad in its discussions; although cherished by persons of discernment, when compared with Master Wengong's [Zhu Xi's] Family Rituals (Jiali)—which takes guarding名分 (status obligations) and exalting love and reverence as its foundation, and dispensing with superficial ornament and attending to fundamental substance as its application—it falls short. Today, the rites are administered by the Ministry of Rites (Chunguan), and as practiced above in the imperial court, how richly glorious is their flourishing, worthy of matching the excellence of Yu and Zhou! Moreover, the canons of capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice have been promulgated to the authorities, brilliantly complete in every detail; yet if in their practice among the people there remains some lack of thoroughness, it is merely because those who uphold them have not reached the utmost, and circumstances have not yet allowed the eradication of long-inherited abuses. Following the loss of music, those who discoursed upon it were not of a single school [? 䒢 for 家]—such as Nie Guanqing's Illustrations of Music (Yuetu), Hu Yuan's Record of Music (Yueji), and Fang Shu's Supplement to Lost Texts (Buwang). Only Proofreader Chen's [Chen Yang's] Book of Music (Yueshu) was comprehensive and systematic; although praised by persons of discernment, when compared with Master Cai's [Cai Yuanding's] New Book of Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu)—which is complete in both fundamental principles and instrumental numerology, and easily understood in its concise wording and clear reasoning—it is not its equal. Today, music is administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (Taichang), and as performed …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之上者洋洋乎其盛可以追美於韶武矣
而聲音器數之制布在有司井然有條然民
間之音律有未協者特以奉行者有未盡耳
力亦未能振其誠和之俗也夫國以民爲本
而民之師帥則守令也古之守令若龔遂之
化盜黃霸之寬和卓茂之愛民魯恭之三異
其見稱於世也尚矣今守令之選多出賢科
其於牧民之道視四子宜不多讓矣以才質
有高下民俗有淳澆況其間非棘而楚則寬而
===
漫其民力尚疲而卒戍之績未著者職此故
也國以兵爲衛而兵之統御則將帥也古之
將帥若吳起之治兵王翦之善戰廉頗之勇
氣李牧之備邊其見稱於人也久矣今將帥
之選類出世冑其於治兵之道視四子當有
所加素以綺紈叙蔭之徒御夫游逸不練之
兵又加之以非貪而刻則縱而弛其智勇尚
少而決勝之策猶有未見者職此由也方今
聖天子在上而於禮樂兵民四者惓惓注意然而
punctuated:
朝廷之上者，洋洋乎其盛，可以追美於《韶》、《武》矣。而聲音、器數之制，布在有司，井然有條。然民間之音律有未協者，特以奉行者有未盡耳，力亦未能振其誠和之俗也。
夫國以民爲本，而民之師帥則守令也。古之守令，若龔遂之化盜、黃霸之寬和、卓茂之愛民、魯恭之三異，其見稱於世也尚矣。今守令之選，多出賢科，其於牧民之道，視四子宜不多讓矣。以才質有高下，民俗有淳澆，況其間非棘而楚，則寬而漫，其民力尚疲而卒戍之績未著者，職此故也。
國以兵爲衛，而兵之統御則將帥也。古之將帥，若吳起之治兵、王翦之善戰、廉頗之勇氣、李牧之備邊，其見稱於人也久矣。今將帥之選，類出世冑，其於治兵之道，視四子當有所加。素以綺紈叙蔭之徒，御夫游逸不練之兵，又加之以非貪而刻，則縱而弛，其智勇尚少而決勝之策猶有未見者，職此由也。
方今聖天子在上，而於禮、樂、兵、民四者惓惓注意，然而
translation_en:
… court overflows in its grandeur and can rival the beauty of the Shao and Wu music. Moreover, the regulations for tones, melodies, instruments, and measures have been promulgated to the authorities in perfect order. Yet if the musical pitches among the populace are not yet in harmony, it is merely because those who implement them have not done so to the fullest, and their strength has likewise been unable to rouse customs of sincere harmony.

Now, the state takes the people as its foundation, and the leaders and teachers of the people are the prefects and magistrates. Among the prefects and magistrates of antiquity—such as Gong Sui 龔遂 transforming bandits, Huang Ba 黃霸 governing with leniency and harmony, Zhuo Mao 卓茂 loving the people, and Lu Gong 魯恭 achieving the "Three Marvels"—their praise in the world goes back a long way. Today, prefects and magistrates are mostly selected from the examination lists of the worthy, and in the way of shepherding the people, they ought not to yield much to those four masters. Yet because their talents and qualities vary from high to low, and popular customs vary from pure to decadent—and moreover, among them, if they are not harsh and punitive, then they are lax and negligent—it is for precisely this reason that the people's strength remains exhausted and the achievements of final pacification and defense [?] are not yet manifest.

The state takes the military as its guard, and those who command the military are the generals and commanders. Among the generals and commanders of antiquity—such as Wu Qi 吳起 training troops, Wang Jian 王翦 excelling in warfare, Lian Po 廉頗 possessing valor, and Li Mu 李牧 defending the frontier—their praise among men has endured for a long time. Today, generals and commanders are mostly selected from hereditary lineages, and in the way of governing troops, they ought to surpass those four masters. Yet because men raised in fine silks and appointed through hereditary privilege routinely command idle, untrained troops—and on top of that, if they are not greedy and harsh, then they are indulgent and lax—it is for precisely this reason that their wisdom and courage remain scarce and strategies for decisive victory are still unseen.

At present, the Sacred Son of Heaven reigns above and devotes earnest attention to the four matters of rites, music, the military, and the people; however, …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之用未盡用治民兵者未盡得人誠有
如執事之所慮者茲欲教民以禮當以文公
家禮申而明之使庠序日加講習而推及閭
閻之下薰陶日久自然成俗禮豈有不行者
乎茲欲教民以樂當以元定新書嚴而教之
俾學校詳加考究而達於鄉黨之間涵泳日
深自然成風樂豈有不用者乎至於治民也
惟在乎慎選守令使布列郡縣者能若程顥
之令晉城朱熹之知漳州則教化乎而黎元
===
自安何龔黃之徒難及乎治兵也惟在乎謹
擇將帥使統御中外者能如韓琦之宣撫陝
西仲淹之經畧環慶則武備脩而兵威自振
何頗牧之輩足數乎然為政固莫先於教化
而禮樂又教化之本也禮樂有本有文本諸
敬以為禮則禮得其體而當然之禮行本諸
和以為樂則樂得其本而自然之和生矣夫
然則本末兼該禮樂畢舉政無不立俗無不
美而治化之隆何虞周之不可及哉謹對
punctuated: 禮樂之用未盡用，治民、兵者未盡得人，誠有如執事之所慮者。茲欲教民以禮，當以文公《家禮》申而明之，使庠序日加講習，而推及閭閻之下，薰陶日久，自然成俗，禮豈有不行者乎？茲欲教民以樂，當以元定《新書》嚴而教之，俾學校詳加考究，而達於鄉黨之間，涵泳日深，自然成風，樂豈有不用者乎？至於治民也，惟在乎慎選守令，使布列郡縣者，能若程顥之令晉城、朱熹之知漳州，則教化孚而黎元自安，何龔、黃之徒難及乎？治兵也，惟在乎謹擇將帥，使統御中外者，能如韓琦之宣撫陝西、仲淹之經畧環慶，則武備脩而兵威自振，何頗、牧之輩足數乎？然為政固莫先於教化，而禮樂又教化之本也。禮樂有本有文，本諸敬以為禮，則禮得其體而當然之禮行；本諸和以為樂，則樂得其本而自然之和生矣。夫然，則本末兼該，禮樂畢舉，政無不立，俗無不美，而治化之隆，何虞、周之不可及哉！謹對。
translation_en:
…the uses of rites and music have not been fully put into practice, and those who govern the people and the troops are not all the right men—it is truly just as you, Sir, have worried.

If we now wish to instruct the people in rites, we should reiterate and clarify them using Master Wen's [Zhu Xi's] Family Rituals (Wengong Jiali), having the local schools practice and study them daily and extending them down to the common alleys and villages. Steeped in their influence over time, they will naturally form customs—how could rites fail to be practiced? If we now wish to instruct the people in music, we should strictly teach it using [Cai] Yuanding's New Book [of Music] (Lülu xinshu), causing the schools to investigate it in detail and extending it throughout the rural communities. Immersed in it ever more deeply, it will naturally become the prevailing ethos—how could music fail to be employed?

As for governing the people, it lies solely in carefully selecting prefects and magistrates. If those distributed across the prefectures and counties can be like Cheng Hao serving as District Magistrate of Jincheng or Zhu Xi serving as Prefect of Zhangzhou, then moral transformation will inspire trust [reading 乎 as 孚] and the common people will naturally be at peace—how would the likes of Gong [Sui] and Huang [Ba] be difficult to match? As for governing the troops, it lies solely in cautiously choosing generals and commanders. If those commanding inside and outside the capital can be like Han Qi serving as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi or [Fan] Zhongyan serving as Military Commissioner of Huanqing, then military preparedness will be maintained and martial prestige will naturally be roused—how would the likes of [Lian] Po and [Li] Mu even be worth counting?

Yet in conducting government, nothing takes precedence over moral transformation, and rites and music are in turn the root of moral transformation. Rites and music have both substance and outward form. When rooted in reverence to constitute rites, rites attain their fundamental substance and proper ritual conduct is practiced; when rooted in harmony to constitute music, music attains its foundation and natural harmony is generated. When this is so, both root and branch are encompassed, rites and music are wholly instituted, no governance fails to be established, no custom fails to be made fine, and in the flourishing of governance and transformation, how could Yu [Shun] and the Zhou dynasty be beyond our reach! I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第四問
同考試官訓導李　批〔貫諸經傳斷以義理有學之　士也〕　曾煥
同考試官教諭韓　批〔此策有考據而斷以理宜錄〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔能答所問〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔決未決之疑有識之士〕
道無往而不在雖聖人無不師理有疑而不
決在學者所當辨夫道之所存師之所在也
===
聖人之生不資於師而亦未嘗不取諸人以
為善賢人之學不能不資於師而亦未嘗無
自得之妙然而議論紛紜莫知所定學者其
可不稽之經傳斷之義理以求一定之說哉
請因明問而言之黃帝生而神靈長而聰
慧仰觀俯察作則垂憲顓頊淵靜淵有
謀疏通達事帝嚳繼之聰以知遠明以察微
既執厥中民罔弗從以至堯舜禹湯文武皆
生知之聖而謂其學於大填錄圖赤松子君
punctuated:
第四問
同考試官訓導李批〔貫諸經傳，斷以義理，有學之士也〕，曾煥。
同考試官教諭韓批〔此策有考據而斷以理，宜錄〕。
考試官教諭吾批〔能答所問〕。
考試官教諭趙批〔決未決之疑，有識之士〕。

道無往而不在，雖聖人無不師；理有疑而不決，在學者所當辨。夫道之所存，師之所在也。聖人之生，不資於師，而亦未嘗不取諸人以為善；賢人之學，不能不資於師，而亦未嘗無自得之妙。然而議論紛紜，莫知所定，學者其可不稽之經傳，斷之義理，以求一定之說哉？請因明問而言之。黃帝生而神靈，長而聰慧，仰觀俯察，作則垂憲。顓頊淵靜，淵有謀，疏通達事。帝嚳繼之，聰以知遠，明以察微，既執厥中，民罔弗從。以至堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，皆生知之聖，而謂其學於大填、錄圖、赤松子、君…
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li comments: “Thoroughly versed in the Classics and commentaries and judging by moral principle—a scholar of learning.” By Zeng Huan 曾煥.
Associate Examiner Instructor Han comments: “This policy essay is grounded in textual evidence and judged by principle; it ought to be selected.”
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: “Able to answer what was asked.”
Examiner Instructor Zhao comments: “Resolves hitherto unresolved doubts—a scholar of insight.”

The Way is present everywhere, and even a sage has no one from whom he does not learn; when principles are subject to doubt and remain unresolved, it is incumbent upon scholars to distinguish them clearly. Now, where the Way resides is where a teacher is to be found. At birth a sage does not depend upon a teacher, yet he has never failed to draw upon others in order to do good; in his learning a worthy cannot do without depending upon a teacher, yet he has never lacked the subtlety of personal realization. When, however, discussions and opinions are confused and divergent so that no one knows what to settle upon, how can scholars fail to examine the matter against the Classics and commentaries and judge it by moral principle in order to seek a definitive explanation? Allow me to speak of this in response to the enlightened question.

The Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) was divine and numinous at birth, and intelligent and wise as he grew; looking up to contemplate and looking down to examine, he created rules and handed down laws. Zhuanxu 顓頊 was deep and tranquil, profound and resourceful [?], and penetratingly conversant with affairs. Emperor Ku 帝嚳 succeeded him, acute in knowing what was distant and clear-sighted in discerning what was subtle; having held fast to the Mean, there were none among the people who did not follow him. Down to Yao 堯, Shun 舜, Yu 禹, Tang 湯, King Wen 文, and King Wu 武, all were sages born with knowledge—yet to claim that they studied with such figures as Datian 大填, Lutu 錄圖, Master Red Pine (Chisongzi 赤松子), Junchou 君…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
疇務成昭之輩西王國伯成子時子思郭叔
之徒雖曰載之傳記其果然耶夫自黃帝至
於武王皆以聖人之德居君師之位所以繼
天而立極者也其道統之傳心法之妙見諸
經傳者若帝嚳帝堯舜禹之執中成湯文武
之建中建極昭如日星矣今乃謂數聖人反
師於大塡郭叔之徒蓋道之至也聖人有所
不知謂其師一端之善容或有之謂其學於
其門親授其業豈足信哉雖其說之出於孔
===
門高弟意好事者爲之託子夏之名以取信
於人不然何其授受之旨經傳無一語以及
之耶此其不足信也明矣自是之後若孔子
之於老聃左丘明之於孔子公羊高穀梁赤
之於子夏孟子之於子思二程之於周子皆
謂之師弟子也或又謂其不然學若不能無
疑夫孔子之聖天理之純人道之極其於古
今名物制度沿革蓋亦於彼或有所詢如適
周問禮於老聃是孔子之無常師也而謂孔
punctuated: 疇、務成昭之輩，西王國、伯成子、時子思、郭叔之徒，雖曰載之傳記，其果然耶？夫自黃帝至於武王，皆以聖人之德，居君師之位，所以繼天而立極者也。其道統之傳、心法之妙，見諸經傳者，若帝嚳、帝堯、舜、禹之執中，成湯、文、武之建中建極，昭如日星矣。今乃謂數聖人反師於大塡、郭叔之徒，蓋道之至也，聖人有所不知，謂其師一端之善，容或有之；謂其學於其門，親授其業，豈足信哉？雖其說之出於孔門高弟，意好事者爲之，託子夏之名以取信於人，不然，何其授受之旨，經傳無一語以及之耶？此其不足信也明矣。自是之後，若孔子之於老聃，左丘明之於孔子，公羊高、穀梁赤之於子夏，孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，皆謂之師弟子也。或又謂其不然，學若不能無疑。夫孔子之聖，天理之純，人道之極，其於古今名物、制度沿革，蓋亦於彼或有所詢，如適周問禮於老聃，是孔子之無常師也。而謂孔
translation_en:
… Chou, Wucheng Zhao, and their like, or figures such as Xi Wangguo, Bocheng Zi, Shi Zisi, and Guo Shu—even though such claims are recorded in biographical traditions, can they really be true? Now, from the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi 黃帝) down to King Wu (Wuwang 武王), all possessed the virtue of sages and occupied the position of ruler and teacher, whereby they succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard. The transmission of the Orthodox Way (daotong 道統) and the subtlety of the Method of the Mind (xinfa 心法) as seen in the Classics and commentaries—such as the "holding fast to the Mean" of Emperor Ku (Di Ku 帝嚳), Emperor Yao (Di Yao 帝堯), Shun 舜, and Yu 禹, and the "establishing the Mean" and "establishing the supreme standard" of Cheng Tang 成湯, King Wen (Wenwang 文王), and King Wu—are as bright as the sun and stars! Now if one claims that these several sages instead took the likes of Datian and Guo Shu as their teachers—well, in the ultimate reaches of the Way, there are things even a sage does not know, so to say that they learned some particular point of goodness from them might perhaps be possible; but to say that they studied at their gate and personally received their instruction from them—how could that be worthy of belief? Even though this account is said to come from a leading disciple of the Confucian school, I suspect meddlesome people fabricated it and borrowed the name of Zixia 子夏 to win credibility from others; otherwise, why is there not a single word in the Classics and commentaries that mentions the purport of their instruction and transmission? That this is unworthy of belief is clear!

After this period, in cases such as Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) in relation to Lao Dan 老聃, Zuo Qiuming 左丘明 in relation to Confucius, Gongyang Gao 公羊高 and Guliang Chi 穀梁赤 in relation to Zixia, Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) in relation to Zisi 子思, and the two Cheng brothers (Er Cheng 二程) in relation to Master Zhou (Zhouzi 周子, Zhou Dunyi), all are referred to as teacher and disciple. Yet some say that this was not so, and scholars [reading 學者 for 學若][?] cannot be without doubt. Now, with Confucius's sageliness—the purity of Heavenly Principle and the ultimate standard of the human way—when it came to ancient and modern names and objects or the evolution of institutions, he too might occasionally have made inquiries of others, as when he went to Zhou and asked Lao Dan about ritual; this simply shows that Confucius had no fixed teacher. Yet to claim that Confucius…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
子爲老聃弟子豈不妄哉至若左氏公穀之
所傳受實得孔子子夏而爲宗師然春秋一
書褒貶是非撥亂反正人道之大綱王法之
所寓以卜氏之賢當筆削之際尚無一辭之
可贊彼左氏之傳果能得其奧旨而不失之
誣哉以親炙之丘明而尚有所失況公穀去
聖既遠顧欲立傳以明乎經是亦不免有所
失也又何名家之有哉使二子能知子夏所
以不敢贊經□□亦未敢輕爲立傳以取
===
謬妄之譏是又□□□即其所學而遂疑其師
授也他如孟子之於子思二程之於周子是
皆亞聖大賢之資而又難以左氏公穀例也
且孟子以命世亞聖之才受業子思之門故
思誠之語與中庸同符而合轍也二程負特
立之材學於周子之門實始尊信庸學爲之
表章斥二家似是之非續千載不傳之緒俾
吾道之明如日麗天其學雖出周子而得於
經者爲多其與孟子息邪說正人心之功同
punctuated: 子爲老聃弟子，豈不妄哉！至若左氏、公、穀之所傳受，實得孔子、子夏而爲宗師。然《春秋》一書，褒貶是非，撥亂反正，人道之大綱，王法之所寓。以卜氏之賢，當筆削之際，尚無一辭之可贊，彼左氏之傳，果能得其奧旨，而不失之誣哉？以親炙之丘明而尚有所失，況公、穀去聖既遠，顧欲立傳以明乎經，是亦不免有所失也，又何名家之有哉！使二子能知子夏所以不敢贊經□□，亦未敢輕爲立傳，以取謬妄之譏。是又□□□即其所學，而遂疑其師授也。他如孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，是皆亞聖大賢之資，而又難以左氏、公、穀例也。且孟子以命世亞聖之才，受業子思之門，故「思誠」之語，與《中庸》同符而合轍也。二程負特立之材，學於周子之門，實始尊信《庸》、《學》，爲之表章，斥二家似是之非，續千載不傳之緒，俾吾道之明，如日麗天。其學雖出周子，而得於經者爲多，其與孟子息邪說、正人心之功同
translation_en:
… Confucius was a disciple of Lao Dan 老聃—is this not absurd? As for what Zuo Qiuming 左丘明, Gongyang Gao 公羊高, and Guliang Chi 穀梁赤 transmitted and received, they indeed had Confucius and Zixia 子夏 as their foundational masters. Yet the single book of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) dispenses praise and blame, distinguishes right and wrong, brings order out of chaos and restores the正 (correct way); it is the great framework of the human way and the repository of kingly law. Even with the worthiness of Master Bu 卜氏 [Zixia], when Confucius was writing and editing it, he could not add a single word of assistance. Could Zuo's Commentary (Zuozhuan) really have grasped its profound meaning without falling into the error of fabrication? If Qiuming, who was personally instructed by the Sage, still had his failings, how much more so Gongyang and Guliang, who were already far removed from the Sage and yet sought to establish commentaries to elucidate the Classic! They too inevitably had their failings; how then can they be considered renowned schools of authority? Had those two masters understood why Zixia dared not add a word to the Classic […], they too would not have dared to lightly compose commentaries and thereby invite ridicule for being erroneous and absurd. Thus [one cannot] simply look at what they learned and consequently doubt the transmission from their teacher.

As for other cases, such as Mencius in relation to Zisi 子思, and the two Cheng brothers 二程 [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] in relation to Master Zhou 周子 [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], these were all men with the endowments of a Second Sage or great worthies, and they cannot be grouped together with Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang. Moreover, Mencius, with the talent of a world-renowned Second Sage, studied at the gate of Zisi; therefore, his words on "reflecting upon sincerity" tally completely and follow the exact same track as the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong). The two Cheng brothers, endowed with outstanding and independent talent, studied at the gate of Master Zhou. They were indeed the first to revere and believe in the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning (Daxue), honoring and elucidating them, refuting the specious fallacies of the two schools [Buddhism and Daoism], and continuing the thread of transmission that had been broken for a thousand years, causing our Way to shine as brightly as the sun in the heavens. Although their learning originated from Master Zhou, what they obtained directly from the Classics was even greater; their achievement is identical to Mencius's merit in putting an end to perverse doctrines and rectifying human minds…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
一揆也此伊川所以謂其得不傳之學於遺
經孟子之後一人而已故朱子之序庸學亦
直以程子而繼孟子也耶管見區區未能究
其源流以袪古今之疑惟進而教之
第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃　批〔敘江西之風俗人物歷歷指　掌未復以師先哲爲言非博學有志者不能得〕
士如斯其敎養之效歟
===
同考試官教諭屠　批〔此策有事實有發揚有歸宿　博洽之士也〕
同考試官教諭桂　批〔答者徒知誇美風俗人物之　盛而不知以名節道德爲尚此作能景行先哲其〕
有志者歟
同考試官學正張　批〔此策乃究實跡者易而居德　善俗者難多見出衆見無如此作故錄之〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔風俗人物鋪敘殆盡且師古　善俗之志藹然言表可嘉可嘉〕
punctuated:
一揆也。此伊川所以謂其得不傳之學於遺經，孟子之後一人而已。故朱子之序《庸》、《學》，亦直以程子而繼孟子也耶！管見區區，未能究其源流以袪古今之疑，惟進而教之。

第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃　批〔敘江西之風俗人物，歷歷指掌，未復以師先哲爲言，非博學有志者不能。得〕士如斯，其敎養之效歟！
同考試官教諭屠　批〔此策有事實、有發揚、有歸宿，博洽之士也。〕
同考試官教諭桂　批〔答者徒知誇美風俗人物之盛，而不知以名節道德爲尚。此作能景行先哲，其〕有志者歟！
同考試官學正張　批〔此策乃究實跡者易，而居德善俗者難。多見出衆，見無如此作，故錄之。〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔風俗人物，鋪敘殆盡，且師古善俗之志，藹然言表，可嘉可嘉！〕
translation_en:
… identical in principle. This is why Yichuan (Cheng Yi 程頤) said that he (Cheng Hao 程顥) had obtained the long-untransmitted learning from the surviving Classics, and that since Mencius there had been this one man alone. Is this not also why Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹), in writing his prefaces to the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) and the Great Learning (Daxue), directly placed the Masters Cheng in succession to Mencius? My humble, narrow view is unable to exhaustively trace these origins and developments so as to dispel the doubts of past and present; I pray only to be advanced and instructed.

Fifth Policy Question
Xiao Sheng 蕭昇

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Huang 黃 comments: "He recounts the customs and notable figures of Jiangxi as clearly as pointing to his palm, and at the end [reading 末 for 未] speaks further of taking the former worthies as models—none but a scholar of broad learning and high aspiration could accomplish this. To obtain a scholar like this: is it not the effect of education and nurturing?"

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Tu 屠 comments: "This policy essay has factual substance, elucidation, and a clear conclusion; he is a scholar of broad and thorough learning."

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Gui 桂 comments: "Other respondents merely know to boast of the flourishing of customs and notable figures, without knowing to esteem integrity and morality. This composition is able to look up to and emulate the former worthies; is he not a man of high aspiration?"

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Zhang 張 comments: "In this policy question, those who investigate actual historical traces do what is easy, whereas those who abide in virtue to improve customs do what is difficult. Among the many views that stand out from the crowd, I saw none to equal this composition, and therefore I have selected it for inclusion."

Examiner and County Director of Studies Wu 吾 comments: "The customs and notable figures are set forth almost exhaustively, and moreover his aspiration to model himself on antiquity and improve customs shines warmly through his words—most commendable, most commendable!"

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙　批〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上抱奇器之士也士風不爲之倚重乎〕
橐鑰之中以倡以化而天下之風俗所由美
陶冶之內以感以興而天下之人物所由盛
此
國家氣運之隆治化之美超越於往古也尚矣
然輿圖之廣在在皆然而江西特一大方也
爲郡一十有三統邑六十有九在禹貢隸揚
州之域在天文屬斗牛之墟山有匡廬之秀
===
特水有彭蠡之環匯其間風俗之異人物之
盛誠有關於
國家之氣化者安得不來執事之問哉愚也
生長是地得之父師考之圖志竊有所知
敢不爲執事陳之以言其風俗也南昌在
藩省之中而饒州與之相屬一則講誦爲
業而衣冠萃止一則忠孝繼出而文物相
續廣信居藩省之東而南康爲其接壤一
則矜謹節義而士風貧薄一則淳固戇實有
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙　批：〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上，抱奇器之士也，士風不爲之倚重乎！〕

橐鑰之中，以倡以化，而天下之風俗所由美；陶冶之內，以感以興，而天下之人物所由盛。此國家氣運之隆、治化之美，超越於往古也尚矣。然輿圖之廣，在在皆然，而江西特一大方也。爲郡一十有三，統邑六十有九；在《禹貢》隸揚州之域，在天文屬斗、牛之墟；山有匡廬之秀特，水有彭蠡之環匯。其間風俗之異、人物之盛，誠有關於國家之氣化者，安得不來執事之問哉？愚也生長是地，得之父師，考之圖志，竊有所知，敢不爲執事陳之！以言其風俗也：南昌在藩省之中，而饒州與之相屬，一則講誦爲業而衣冠萃止，一則忠孝繼出而文物相續；廣信居藩省之東，而南康爲其接壤，一則矜謹節義而士風貧薄，一則淳固戇實有
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: [Born in this land yet befriending the ancients across the millennia, he is a scholar who harbors extraordinary talent. Will not the ethos of the literati rely heavily upon him?]

Within the bellows of creation, by leading and transforming, the customs of the empire are thereby made admirable; within the potter's wheel and smelter's mold, by inspiring and rousing, the talents of the empire are thereby made flourishing. That the prosperity of the State's destiny and the excellence of its transformative governance surpass those of antiquity is indeed of long standing. Yet across the vastness of the imperial territory this is true everywhere, and Jiangxi 江西 is simply one great region. It comprises thirteen prefectures, governing sixty-nine counties. In the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong 禹貢), it belonged to the domain of Yangzhou 揚州; in astrological geography, it corresponds to the field of the Dipper (Dou 斗) and the Ox (Niu 牛). Among its mountains is the sublime distinction of Mount Kuanglu 匡廬 [Mount Lu]; among its waters is the encircling confluence of Pengli 彭蠡 [Poyang Lake]. The diversity of its customs and the abundance of its figures of talent therein truly have a bearing upon the transformative vital force of the State—how could this fail to prompt Your Excellency's question? Born and raised in this land, having learned from my fathers and teachers and examined maps and gazetteers, I in my humble way have some knowledge of it; how dare I not set it forth for Your Excellency?

To speak of its customs: Nanchang 南昌 lies at the center of the province, and Raozhou 饒州 is contiguous with it; in the former, lecturing and recitation are the main pursuits and officials and gentry gather together, while in the latter, men of loyalty and filial piety emerge in succession and refined culture continues unbroken. Guangxin 廣信 sits in the east of the province, and Nankang 南康 borders upon it; in the former, people prize and guard moral integrity and righteousness while the scholars' lifestyle is frugal and austere, whereas in the latter, they are simple, steadfast, and honest, possessing…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
先儒遺風至於士習詩書而農勤稼穡風□
和平而人物秀麗者非九江與建昌乎風流
儒雅而民樂耕桑崇德尚禮而勤力知分者
非撫州與臨江乎瑞之吏民朴野而不嚚於
訟袁之廉恥儉嗇而事不煩此二郡之風俗
不同也贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節南安
則民習淳古而士果於義此又二郡之風俗
異也至於人厖淳而多壽考家詩書而戶庠
塾其吉安之風俗何厚哉以言乎人物也徐
===
稺非其力不食陳蕃稱為南州高士黃庭堅
為江西詩宗蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表致力中
原陶侃之運甓以自勵充定大計逍遙之謀
國不顧身此南昌饒州之人物也可知奮身
歸國業大用受金牌之賜忠□□□□□得
獲全歸之安保衛鄉閭鄒元靖有□□□才
請救襄樊江萬里以峭直見忌此廣信南康
之人物也可見九江建昌則有周訪之沉
毅果斷陶潛之恥身後代與夫曾鞏齊名
punctuated:
先儒遺風。至於士習《詩》、《書》而農勤稼穡，風□和平而人物秀麗者，非九江與建昌乎？風流儒雅而民樂耕桑，崇德尚禮而勤力知分者，非撫州與臨江乎？瑞之吏民朴野而不嚚於訟，袁之廉恥儉嗇而事不煩，此二郡之風俗不同也；贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節，南安則民習淳古而士果於義，此又二郡之風俗異也。至於人厖淳而多壽考，家《詩》、《書》而戶庠塾，其吉安之風俗何厚哉！

以言乎人物也：徐稺非其力不食，陳蕃稱為南州高士；黃庭堅為江西詩宗，蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表；致力中原，陶侃之運甓以自勵；充定大計，逍遙之謀國不顧身，此南昌、饒州之人物也可知。奮身歸國，業大用受金牌之賜；忠□□□□□，得獲全歸之安；保衛鄉閭，鄒元靖有□□□才；請救襄樊，江萬里以峭直見忌，此廣信、南康之人物也可見。九江、建昌，則有周訪之沉毅果斷、陶潛之恥身後代，與夫曾鞏齊名…
translation_en:
…the lingering ethos of the former Confucians. As for places where scholars study the Odes and the Documents while farmers are diligent in sowing and reaping, and where the local ethos [?] is harmonious and peaceful while the people are refined and handsome—are these not Jiujiang 九江 and Jianchang 建昌? Where the style is cultured and scholarly while the commoners delight in plowing and sericulture, and where people revere virtue, esteem ritual, work diligently, and know their station—are these not Fuzhou 撫州 and Linjiang 臨江? In Ruizhou 瑞州, the subofficial functionaries and commoners are simple and rustic and not given to deceitful litigation; in Yuanzhou 袁州, they have a sense of shame, are frugal, and keep affairs uncomplicated—such are the differing customs of these two prefectures. In Ganzhou 贛州, the people are vigorous, robust, and skillful in crafts, upholding high aspirations and sharpening their integrity; in Nan'an 南安, the commoners are accustomed to antique simplicity while the scholars are resolute in righteousness—such again are the distinct customs of these two prefectures. And as for a place where the people are generous and pure and many enjoy long life, where every family has the Odes and Documents and every household has a school—how rich indeed are the customs of Ji'an 吉安!

To speak of notable figures: Xu Zhi 徐稺 would not eat except by his own labor, and Chen Fan 陳蕃 praised him as the "Lofty Scholar of the Southern Prefectures"; Huang Tingjian 黃庭堅 was the patriarch of the Jiangxi poetry school, and Su Shi 蘇軾 admired him for standing independent beyond the material world; devoting his strength to the Central Plains, Tao Kan 陶侃 carried bricks to spur himself on; formulating great plans, Xiaoyao 逍遙 [Yin Zhongkan 殷仲堪 / Peng Juyuan 彭居中?][?] took counsel for the state without regard for his own person—from these examples, the notable figures of Nanchang 南昌 and Raozhou 饒州 can be known. Throwing himself into returning allegiance to the state, Ye Dayong 業大用 [Ye Dayou 葉大有?][?] received the bestowal of a golden tablet; loyal […][?], he was able to attain the peace of returning whole; defending his home villages, Zou Yuanjing 鄒元靖 [Zou Jin 鄒近 / Zou Yinglong 鄒應龍?][?] possessed […][?] talent; requesting the relief of Xiangyang 襄陽 and Fancheng 樊城, Jiang Wanli 江萬里 was resented for his stern uprightness—from these examples, the notable figures of Guangxin 廣信 and Nankang 南康 can be seen. In Jiujiang and Jianchang, there were Zhou Fang 周訪 with his deep fortitude and decisive resolution, Tao Qian 陶潛 who was ashamed to serve a succeeding dynasty, as well as Zeng Gong 曾鞏, whose fame equaled…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
於歐陽陳宗禮之直言清節者焉撫州臨江則
有陸九淵之講明道學吴澂之力學聖賢與
夫陳喬以社稷為己任劉清之之博極群書者
焉他如劉恕篤好史學陳仲微涵飫六經廖
洪之孝築墳塋陳重之友堅膠漆非瑞袁之
人物乎李朴之操履勁特曽開之大節不奪
盧汝舟之廉約守正田闢之嗜學不倦非贑
南之人物乎以至盡心匡直文章與韓愈並
稱歐陽脩一代之宗也死不虧節而父子相
===
繼楊邦乂名世之人也胡銓之力排和議劾
奸一疏與日月以爭光文天祥之九死不悔
正氣一歌與宇宙相為悠久其吉安之人物
何盛哉然風俗之美於今者無以異乎古人
物之盛乎古者何有間於今故今之節行文
章濟濟相望功名事業燁燁馳聲愚固未暇
以縷數惟於一風俗師先哲之意竊亦有志
不敢無言夫欲一風俗莫先於明禮義而
養廉恥戒浮靡而崇節儉其所以化導之
punctuated: 於歐陽、陳宗禮之直言清節者焉。撫州、臨江，則有陸九淵之講明道學、吴澂之力學聖賢，與夫陳喬以社稷為己任、劉清之之博極群書者焉。他如劉恕篤好史學、陳仲微涵飫六經、廖洪之孝築墳塋、陳重之友堅膠漆，非瑞、袁之人物乎？李朴之操履勁特、曽開之大節不奪、盧汝舟之廉約守正、田闢之嗜學不倦，非贑、南之人物乎？以至盡心匡直，文章與韓愈並稱，歐陽脩一代之宗也；死不虧節，而父子相繼，楊邦乂名世之人也；胡銓之力排和議，劾奸一疏與日月以爭光；文天祥之九死不悔，《正氣》一歌與宇宙相為悠久。其吉安之人物何盛哉！然風俗之美於今者無以異乎古，人物之盛乎古者何有間於今？故今之節行文章濟濟相望，功名事業燁燁馳聲，愚固未暇以縷數。惟於一風俗、師先哲之意，竊亦有志，不敢無言。夫欲一風俗，莫先於明禮義而養廉恥，戒浮靡而崇節儉。其所以化導之…
translation_en: …with Ouyang [Xiu], and Chen Zongli 陳宗禮 with his forthright remonstrance and pure integrity. In Fuzhou 撫州 and Linjiang 臨江, there were Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵 who expounded and clarified the Learning of the Way, Wu Cheng 吴澂 who strove to learn from the sages and worthies, as well as Chen Qiao 陳喬 who took the altars of soil and grain (the state) as his personal responsibility, and Liu Qingzhi 劉清之 who was exhaustively versed in all books. As for others—such as Liu Shu 劉恕 who was deeply devoted to historical studies, Chen Zhongwei 陳仲微 who was steeped in the Six Classics, Liao Hong 廖洪 who filially built his parents' tomb, and Chen Zhong 陳重 whose friendship was as firm as glue and lacquer—were they not the notable figures of Ruizhou 瑞州 and Yuanzhou 袁州? Li Pu 李朴 with his firm and upright conduct, Zeng Kai 曽開 whose great integrity could not be shaken, Lu Ruzhou 盧汝舟 who was incorrupt, frugal, and held fast to rectitude, and Tian Pi 田闢 who loved learning tirelessly—were they not the notable figures of Ganzhou 贑州 and Nan'an 南安? Coming down to Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩, who devoted his heart to rectifying the ruler and whose literary writings were ranked alongside those of Han Yu 韓愈—he was the master of an entire age; Yang Bangyi 楊邦乂, who died without compromising his integrity and whose father and son succeeded one another in loyalty—he was a renowned figure of his generation; Hu Quan 胡銓, who vigorously rejected peace negotiations and whose single memorial impeaching the treacherous shines in rivalry with the sun and moon; and Wen Tianxiang 文天祥, who had no regrets even facing death nine times over and whose single Song of Righteous Qi (Zhengqi ge) endures as long as the cosmos itself—how flourishing indeed were the notable figures of Ji'an 吉安! Yet the beauty of customs in the present day is no different from that of antiquity; how could the flourishing of notable figures in antiquity be separated from the present? Thus, the moral conduct and literary writings of today's men stand in dense array gazing upon one another, and their achievements, fame, and enterprises blaze forth with renowned reputations; in my ignorance, I truly lack the leisure to enumerate them one by one. Only regarding the intention of unifying customs and taking the former worthies as teachers do I privately harbor an aspiration as well, and dare not remain silent. Now, if one wishes to unify customs, nothing comes before clarifying ritual and righteousness and nurturing a sense of honor and shame, guarding against superficial extravagance and esteeming frugality. As for the means of transforming and guiding them…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
者固當造端乎民牧所以鼓舞而倡率之則又
在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳若夫靖節之介
得其正文忠公之文本於德文安文正之學
根乎道此道德文章之可師也澹菴憂中興
之社稷信國決萬世之綱常此功名節義之
可師也爲士者誠能師先哲以脩己寄民社
者又能師先哲以化民則民風之所以淳者
在是士風之所以正者在是人物之所以盛
者亦在是愚也不敏倘蒙與進俾得以行其
言敢不景行先哲以副執事之望謹對
punctuated: 者，固當造端乎民牧；所以鼓舞而倡率之，則又在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳。若夫靖節之介得其正，文忠公之文本於德，文安、文正之學根乎道，此道德文章之可師也；澹菴憂中興之社稷，信國決萬世之綱常，此功名節義之可師也。爲士者誠能師先哲以脩己，寄民社者又能師先哲以化民，則民風之所以淳者在是，士風之所以正者在是，人物之所以盛者亦在是。愚也不敏，倘蒙與進，俾得以行其言，敢不景行先哲，以副執事之望！謹對。
translation_en: … [The means by which to transform and guide] them must indeed originate with the shepherds of the people [local officials]; yet the means to inspire and lead them lies in turn with how the scholar-officials and gentlemen apply their minds. As for the incorruptibility of Jingjie [Tao Yuanming 陶淵明] attaining rectitude, the literary writings of Duke Wenzhong [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修] being rooted in virtue, and the learning of Wen'an [Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵] and Wenzheng [Zeng Gong 曾鞏 /謝枋得?] being grounded in the Way—these are the exemplars of moral virtue and literary composition worthy of emulation. Dan'an [Hu Quan 胡銓] worrying over the altars of state during thedynastic restoration, and the Duke of Xinguo [Wen Tianxiang 文天祥] upholding the cardinal principles and constant virtues for ten thousand generations—these are the exemplars of merit, fame, and righteous integrity worthy of emulation. If those who are scholars can truly take the former sages as their teachers in cultivating themselves, and those entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil can likewise take the former sages as their teachers in transforming the people, then that by which popular customs become pure lies right here, that by which the ethos of the literati becomes upright lies right here, and that by which men of talent flourish also lies right here. Ignorant as I am, should I be favored with advancement and enabled to put my words into practice, how could I dare not emulate the illustrious conduct of the former sages so as to fulfill the expectations of Your Excellency the Examiner! I respectfully reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西蔚爲東南鉅服英賢之
生萃焉發于漢唐盛于有宋
而尤盛于我
朝我以文學鳴或以政事顯或
以忠烈震撼轟天地煥爛簡
冊海宇之廣人材之夥率推
===
先焉況自我
朝迨今踵大拜者垂百數年連
大魁者踰十數人雖其所樹
立有隆有庳然至於大貽詒
於時者尠矣於戲誠盛矣哉
乃今成化十三年實維大比
之秋合列郡之士幾三千人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西蔚爲東南鉅服，英賢之生萃焉。發于漢、唐，盛于有宋，而尤盛于我朝。我以文學鳴，或以政事顯，或以忠烈震，撼轟天地，煥爛簡冊。海宇之廣，人材之夥，率推先焉。況自我朝迨今，踵大拜者垂百數年，連大魁者踰十數人。雖其所樹立有隆有庳，然至於大貽詒於時者尠矣。於戲！誠盛矣哉！乃今成化十三年，實維大比之秋，合列郡之士幾三千人，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Jiangxi flourishes as a great domain of the southeast, where the birth of heroes and worthies is concentrated. Having begun to emerge in the Han and Tang dynasties, they flourished during the Song dynasty, and have flourished especially in our dynasty. Some [?; transcription has 我 "we/I" for 或 "some"] have won renown through literature and learning, some have gained prominence through administrative affairs, and some have stirred the world through loyalty and heroism—shaking heaven and earth and shining brilliantly in the historical records. Across the vastness of the realm and the multitude of its men of talent, Jiangxi is generally ranked first. Moreover, from the founding of our dynasty down to the present, those who have succeeded one another in appointments to the Grand Secretariat have spanned nearly a hundred years, and those who have successively taken first place in the examinations have exceeded a dozen men. Although their achievements have been some lofty and some modest, those who have brought great disgrace [?; 貽詒, likely for 貽誚] upon their times have been few indeed. Alas, how truly flourishing this is!

Now, in the thirteenth year of the Chenghua reign (1477), it is truly the autumn of the triennial examination. Bringing together nearly three thousand scholars from the various prefectures, …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
三試之自監臨以曁內外諸
執事旣皆殫力防範周
詳㝵等濫竽考官敢不精白
一心以公去取於是擇其文
之中式者遵
制得九十五人登之賢書獻之
□拜手稽首爲
===
□人賀復僭序諸小錄爲
登名諸君子告焉夫江右人
材於今固盛矣而其所以盛
諸君子容不知所勉哉勉之
唯無負
天之所以命我者之大而遜其第
一等者於人以文學鳴必爲
punctuated: 三試之。自監臨以曁內外諸執事，旣皆殫力防範周詳，㝵等濫竽考官，敢不精白一心，以公去取？於是擇其文之中式者，遵制得九十五人，登之賢書，獻之□，拜手稽首，爲□人賀；復僭序諸小錄，爲登名諸君子告焉。夫江右人材於今固盛矣，而其所以盛，諸君子容不知所勉哉？勉之唯無負天之所以命我者之大，而遜其第一等者於人。以文學鳴，必爲
translation_en: …and tested them in three sessions. Since everyone from the Supervising Official down to the various functionaries of the inner and outer wards exhausted their efforts to make the precautions and regulations thorough and detailed, how could I, Ai [? 㝵], and my colleagues, though unworthy to serve as Examiners, dare not keep our minds pure and single-hearted so as to be impartial in rejecting and selecting? Thereupon, we chose those whose essays met the standard, obtaining ninety-five men in accordance with the imperial regulations. Recording them in the Register of Worthies and presenting it to the [Court / Throne ?], we bow with hands clasped and heads to the ground to offer congratulations on finding men [for the state ?]; and we further presume to write this preface to the minor record to address the gentlemen whose names have been inscribed on the list. Now, men of talent in Jiangxi are certainly flourishing today; yet as to the reason why they flourish, how could you gentlemen not know how to exert yourselves? In exerting yourselves, simply do not fail the greatness of what Heaven has endowed in us, nor yield the first-rank achievement to others. If one wins renown through literature and learning, one must…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
往聖繼絕學爲萬世開太平
斯第一流之文學歟以政事
顯必爲天地立心爲生民立
命斯第一流之政事歟忠烈
自文學政事中事無庸言已
若然則諸君子負挾之弘建
士豈徒爲當今人物將
===
□虞三代人物等而我
□雍熙泰和之治所以登三
□后五者亦將愈遠彌隆矣
主司深望實在于茲唯諸君
子副之
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開
化吾𣅀謹序
punctuated:
往聖繼絕學，爲萬世開太平，斯第一流之文學歟！以政事顯，必爲天地立心，爲生民立命，斯第一流之政事歟！忠烈自文學、政事中事，無庸言已。若然，則諸君子負挾之弘、建□之士，豈徒爲當今人物？將□虞、三代人物等，而我□雍熙泰和之治，所以登三□后五者，亦將愈遠彌隆矣。主司深望，實在于茲，唯諸君子副之。
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開化吾𣅀謹序。
translation_en:
…carry on the lost learning of the past sages and open up peace for ten thousand generations—is this not literature and learning of the first rank? To distinguish oneself through statecraft, one must establish a heart for Heaven and Earth and establish a destiny for the living people—is this not statecraft of the first rank? Loyalty and heroic integrity are matters that naturally arise from within literature, learning, and statecraft, so there is no need to speak of them separately. If it is so, then with the breadth of what you gentlemen bear and embrace, and as scholars of [lofty] achievements [?], how could you merely be figures of the present day? You will [stand as] equals to the figures of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and the harmonious, peaceful, and supremely concordant governance of our [Dynasty], whereby it ascends to the Three [August Ones] and leaves behind [?] the Five [Emperors], will also become ever more far-reaching and increasingly flourishing! The deep hopes of the examination officials truly lie in this; may you gentlemen live up to them.

Respectfully prefaced by Wu Hu 吾𣅀 of Kaihua 開化, Instructor (jiaoyu) of the Confucian School of Jiangpu County 江浦縣 in Yingtian Prefecture 應天府.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
敬豫定於方寸也其存養之功何如夫敬脩於已
故德著於儀殆見一舉足也必時行而行時止而
止何有失足於人耶一動容也必喜所可喜怒所
可怒何有失色於人耶口則當語而語當默而默
而口於人也又豈有所失乎惟其不失足則威儀
抑抑而貌儼然足畏也惟其不失色則容止顒顒
而色肅然足憚也口無所失則出言有章其言又
豈不足信乎是則動處中節固本於持敬之功敬
德流形實君子儀刑之本本立則行道之具在矣
===
奚必歷聘駕說而後為行道哉抑若此篇言持敬
而驗於動處中節中庸言持敬而極於篤恭天下
平何耶蓋中庸示人以進德之事故推其極此篇
發明聖人立教之故故驗諸身此所以為有異也
君子誠能此敬常存動靜交致而不已焉則篤恭
之效不亦可馴致乎
夙夜強學以待問懷忠信以待舉力行以待
取
張吉
punctuated:
敬豫定於方寸也，其存養之功何如？夫敬脩於已，故德著於儀。殆見一舉足也，必時行而行，時止而止，何有失足於人耶？一動容也，必喜所可喜，怒所可怒，何有失色於人耶？口則當語而語，當默而默，而口於人也，又豈有所失乎？惟其不失足，則威儀抑抑，而貌儼然足畏也；惟其不失色，則容止顒顒，而色肅然足憚也；口無所失，則出言有章，其言又豈不足信乎？是則動處中節，固本於持敬之功；敬德流形，實君子儀刑之本。本立，則行道之具在矣，奚必歷聘駕說而後為行道哉？抑若此篇言持敬，而驗於動處中節；《中庸》言持敬，而極於篤恭天下平，何耶？蓋《中庸》示人以進德之事，故推其極；此篇發明聖人立教之故，故驗諸身：此所以為有異也。君子誠能此敬常存，動靜交致而不已焉，則篤恭之效不亦可馴致乎？

夙夜強學以待問，懷忠信以待舉，力行以待取。
張吉
translation_en:
…reverence is settled beforehand in one's heart. How great is the effort of preserving and nourishing it! Now, when reverence is cultivated within oneself, virtue is manifested in one's demeanor. Thus it will be seen that whenever he lifts his foot, he surely advances when it is time to advance and stops when it is time to stop—how could he ever make a misstep before others? Whenever he changes his countenance, he surely rejoices at what is worthy of joy and is angered by what is worthy of anger—how could he ever lose his composure before others? As for his mouth, he speaks when he ought to speak and remains silent when he ought to remain silent—so in his speech toward others, how could there be any fault? Because he makes no misstep, his dignified demeanor is restrained and his appearance is gravely awe-inspiring. Because he does not lose his composure, his bearing is solemn and his expression is reverently daunting. Because his mouth commits no fault, hisuttered words have pattern and order—how then could his words fail to be trustworthy? Thus, hitting the proper measure in every movement is assuredly rooted in the effort of maintaining reverence, and the outward manifestation of reverent virtue is truly the foundation of the gentleman's exemplary model. Once the foundation is established, the means for practicing the Way are present; why must one travel from state to state offering counsel before it can be called practicing the Way? Yet why is it that while this chapter speaks of maintaining reverence and verifies it through hitting the proper measure in movement, the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of maintaining reverence and carries it to the ultimate point of devout reverence bringing peace to the world? It is because the Doctrine of the Mean instructs people in the work of advancing in virtue, and therefore pushes it to its ultimate realization, whereas this chapter elucidates the reason the sage established his teaching, and therefore verifies it in one's own person. This is why they differ. If the gentleman can truly preserve this reverence constantly, applying it mutually in both activity and stillness without ceasing, then may not the efficacy of devout reverence also be gradually attained?

"Day and night he strenuously studies to await questioning, cherishes loyalty and trustworthiness to await recommendation, and vigorously practices to await selection."
Zhang Ji 張吉

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔此題方氏已有明訓作者往往蹈襲陳言混無分別而此篇體認切當文有發〕
〔揮從葉健〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔說儒者自立之行詞理俱優〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔積學脩德自立有待是作得之〕
〔一薦何悉〕
積學以聽人之求脩德以聽人之用此儒者然也
蓋學不積則無可求德不脩則無可用儒者積學
脩德皆有所待其自立之行何如哉且夫以道得
===
名爲儒有儒者之名必有儒者之行如詩書以紀
聖賢之成法儒者朝夕孳孳學之不已至於熟而
渰貫則自然可以及人故人必從之取正焉禮樂
以寓事理所當然儒者夙夜勉勉習之不倦至於
積而充周則自然可以成物故人必就之講明焉
而曰待問必叩之以大則大鳴不叩之以小則小鳴不聞往教也自非積學有素安能然
以小則小鳴不聞往教也自非積學有素安能然
乎至若忠信乃固有之理今則懷盡已之忠而所
學皆實必抱以實之信而所習皆實事故忠信可
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭，批〔此題方氏已有明訓，作者往往蹈襲陳言，混無分別，而此篇體認切當，文有發揮，從葉健。〕
考試官教諭吾，批〔說儒者自立之行，詞理俱優。〕
考試官教諭趙，批〔積學脩德，自立有待，是作得之。〕〔一薦何悉。〕
積學以聽人之求，脩德以聽人之用，此儒者然也。蓋學不積則無可求，德不脩則無可用。儒者積學脩德，皆有所待，其自立之行何如哉？且夫以道得名爲儒，有儒者之名，必有儒者之行。如詩書以紀聖賢之成法，儒者朝夕孳孳，學之不已，至於熟而渰貫，則自然可以及人，故人必從之取正焉。禮樂以寓事理所當然，儒者夙夜勉勉，習之不倦，至於積而充周，則自然可以成物，故人必就之講明焉。而曰待問，必叩之以大則大鳴，不叩之以小則小鳴，不聞往教也。自非積學有素，安能然？以小則小鳴，不聞往教也。自非積學有素，安能然乎？至若忠信，乃固有之理。今則懷盡已之忠，而所學皆實，必抱以實之信，而所習皆實事，故忠信可
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: 〔Master Fang has already provided a clear explanation of this topic. Writers often tread over familiar ground, repeating established phrases without making distinctions. This essay, however, grasps the meaning accurately and develops it in its prose. The concluding words, 從葉健, are unclear [?].〕
Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: 〔It explains the conduct by which a Confucian scholar establishes himself; both its wording and its reasoning are excellent.〕
Examiner Zhao, an Instructor, comments: 〔Accumulating learning and cultivating virtue, establishing oneself and awaiting an opportunity: this composition captures these points.〕〔First recommendation, He Xi [?].〕
To accumulate learning and await others’ requests, to cultivate virtue and await others’ employment of him—such is the way of the Confucian scholar. Without accumulated learning, he has nothing others can seek; without cultivated virtue, he has nothing others can employ. The scholar accumulates learning and cultivates virtue, in each case awaiting something. What, then, is the conduct by which he establishes himself?
Now, one earns the name of Confucian scholar through the Way. Whoever bears that name must possess the corresponding conduct. For example, the Odes and the Documents record the established models of the sages and worthies. The scholar applies himself diligently morning and evening, studying them without cease until he knows them thoroughly and comprehends them throughout [?]. He can then naturally extend their benefits to others, who will therefore follow him and seek a correct understanding from him. Rites and music embody what is proper in affairs and their underlying principles. The scholar exerts himself early and late, practicing them tirelessly until his accumulated practice becomes full and comprehensive. He can then naturally bring others to fulfillment, and people will therefore approach him for discussion and elucidation.
As for the phrase ‘await questions’: strike him with a great question, and he gives a great response; ‘do not strike him with a small question, and he gives a small response’ [?]. One does not hear of going out to teach others unsolicited. Without a longstanding accumulation of learning, how could he be like this? ‘With a small question, he gives a small response; one does not hear of going out to teach others unsolicited. Without a longstanding accumulation of learning, how could he be like this?’ [The transcription repeats this passage.]
As for loyalty and trustworthiness, these are principles inherently possessed. Now, if he cherishes the loyalty that consists in giving fully of himself, all that he learns will be grounded in reality; he must also embrace trustworthiness grounded in sincerity [?], so that everything he practices concerns real affairs. Thus loyalty and trustworthiness can …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
任人必舉之自有用世之道存焉力行乃體履之
功今而學不徒學必允蹈之惟勤習不徒習必實
踐之匪懈故力行可使人必取之自有應世之具
在焉而曰待舉待取必舉而後進未嘗輕進也微
而後出未嘗苟出也自非脩德有待安致是乎夫
儒者自立之行不求於人如此聖人以之而告哀
公得無意歟抑考孔子因哀公始問儒服則對以
不知及問儒行則悉數其事此言儒者自貴以待
天下之用而強學忠信力行皆自立有待之事也
===
古之儒者如此夫何後世末流抱空學惟慮人之
不知懷片善惟恐世之不用寧不深愧于孔子之
論儒耶噫業儒者於儒行此篇宜詳致意焉
論
聖人至公至神之化
同考試官學正陳　批　議論切實句法蒼健有操縱
有規矩誠作手也置之魁選允愜輿論
張約
考試官教諭吾　批　議論縱出非有學之士不能當
punctuated:
任，人必舉之，自有用世之道存焉。力行乃體履之功，今而學不徒學，必允蹈之惟勤；習不徒習，必實踐之匪懈。故力行可使，人必取之，自有應世之具在焉。而曰待舉待取，必舉而後進，未嘗輕進也；微而後出，未嘗苟出也。自非脩德有待，安致是乎？夫儒者自立之行，不求於人如此，聖人以之而告哀公，得無意歟？抑考孔子因哀公始問儒服，則對以不知；及問儒行，則悉數其事。此言儒者自貴，以待天下之用，而強學、忠信、力行，皆自立有待之事也。古之儒者如此，夫何後世末流，抱空學，惟慮人之不知；懷片善，惟恐世之不用？寧不深愧于孔子之論儒耶？噫！業儒者於《儒行》此篇，宜詳致意焉。

論
聖人至公至神之化

同考試官學正陳　批：議論切實，句法蒼健，有操縱，有規矩，誠作手也。置之魁選，允愜輿論。

張約

考試官教諭吾　批：議論縱出，非有學之士不能。當
translation_en:
…trusted, others will certainly recommend him: he inherently possesses the Way by which to serve the world. Earnest practice is the work of personally embodying and carrying out what one has learned. His learning is thus no mere learning: he must diligently put it into effect. His repeated study is no mere repetition: he must put it into practice without slackening. Thus his earnest practice makes him fit for employment, and others will certainly select him: he inherently possesses the equipment for responding to the world’s needs. As for saying that he awaits recommendation and selection, he advances only after being recommended, never advancing rashly; he comes forth only after being summoned [?], never coming forth heedlessly. Without cultivating virtue and awaiting his opportunity, how could he attain this?

Such is the conduct by which a Confucian scholar establishes himself without seeking favors from others. Could the Sage have been without a purpose in explaining it to Duke Ai? Consider, moreover, that when Duke Ai first asked Confucius about Confucian dress, he replied that he did not know; but when asked about Confucian conduct, he enumerated its particulars in full. This says that a Confucian scholar values himself and awaits employment by the world. Diligent learning, loyalty and trustworthiness, and earnest practice are all matters of establishing oneself and awaiting one’s opportunity. Such were the Confucian scholars of antiquity. Why, then, do their latter-day, degenerate successors, cherishing empty learning, worry only that others do not know them, and, possessing some small virtue, fear only that the world will not employ them? Should they not feel profound shame before Confucius’s discussion of the Confucian scholar? Alas! Those who pursue Confucian learning ought to give careful attention to this chapter, “The Conduct of the Confucian Scholar” (Ruxing).

Discourse
“The Sage’s Supremely Impartial and Numinous Transforming Influence”
