title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
放子出一頭地
考試官教諭趙　批議論疊出筆力雄健佳作也
論曰寂然之中而有感通者寓聖人之心大
造之心也聖人之於天地蓋並立而爲三也
其好惡賞罰一無私至眞與天地上下相爲
流通者矣天地無私物聖人無私民天地無
心而成化聖人有心而無爲至寂之中而妙
乎至感之機至靜至隱而貫乎至動至著之
理聖人之心不私已之心也私則人人則滯
===
滯於此而不達於彼局於己而不通於人拘
拘於一隅而不普徧於天下國家若然則與
天地不相似矣聖人之心不如是之固也不
如是之滯也不如是之局且拘也其至公
至神之化即天地之公之神之化乎朱子
以是爲言其知聖人之所以爲聖人者歟愚
敢繹其說天位乎上職乎覆也而其所以覆
者公而已地位乎下職乎載也而其所以載
者亦公而已公則神神則化天地之無心也
punctuated:
放子出一頭地。
考試官教諭趙　批：議論疊出，筆力雄健，佳作也。
論曰：寂然之中而有感通者寓，聖人之心，大造之心也。聖人之於天地，蓋並立而爲三也。其好惡賞罰，一無私至，眞與天地上下相爲流通者矣。天地無私物，聖人無私民；天地無心而成化，聖人有心而無爲。至寂之中而妙乎至感之機，至靜至隱而貫乎至動至著之理。聖人之心，不私已之心也。私則人，人則滯；滯於此而不達於彼，局於己而不通於人，拘拘於一隅而不普徧於天下國家，若然，則與天地不相似矣。聖人之心，不如是之固也，不如是之滯也，不如是之局且拘也。其至公至神之化，即天地之公之神之化乎！朱子以是爲言，其知聖人之所以爲聖人者歟！愚敢繹其說。天位乎上，職乎覆也，而其所以覆者，公而已；地位乎下，職乎載也，而其所以載者，亦公而已。公則神，神則化，天地之無心也。
translation_en:
…let this gentleman stand a head above the rest.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhao comments: Arguments emerge one after another, and the brushwork is vigorous and robust; it is a fine piece of work.
The discourse reads: Within absolute stillness there resides that which responds and penetrates; the mind of the sage is the mind of the Great Creator. In relation to Heaven and Earth, the sage indeed stands alongside them to form a triad. In his likes and dislikes, rewards and punishments, no partiality ever arrives; he truly flows in mutual harmony above and below with Heaven and Earth. Heaven and Earth have no favored things, and the sage has no favored people; Heaven and Earth have no deliberate mind yet accomplish transformation, while the sage has a mind yet acts without deliberation. Within utmost stillness he wondrously masters the mechanism of utmost responsiveness; in what is most tranquil and most hidden, he threads through the principle of what is most active and most manifest. The mind of the sage is a mind not partial to itself [reading 已 as 己]. To be partial is to be merely human, and to be merely human is to be obstructed—obstructed here and unable to reach there, confined to oneself and unable to connect with others, cramped in a single corner and unable to extend universally throughout the realm, the state, and the family. If it were so, then he would not resemble Heaven and Earth. The mind of the sage is not so obstinate as this, not so obstructed as this, not so confined and cramped as this. Is not his supremely impartial and supremely numinous transformation none other than the impartial and numinous transformation of Heaven and Earth! When Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) spoke in these terms, did he not understand that whereby a sage is a sage! I venture to unfold his explanation. Heaven is positioned above, its office being to shelter, and that whereby it shelters is nothing other than impartiality; Earth is positioned below, its office being to support, and that whereby it supports is likewise nothing other than impartiality. Being impartial, it is numinous; being numinous, it transforms—such is the non-deliberate mind of Heaven and Earth.…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
一或有心則涉於私矣私則不足以言公況
謂至公之化乎非公不足以言神況謂至神
之化乎聖人中天地以有生合天地以爲德
體天地以致治法天地之公妙天地之神普
天地之化寂然不動感而遂通生者自生殺
者自殺天何爲也殊不知無爲而無所不爲
天之神化何如哉聖人之神化亦猶是也成
者自成悴者自悴地何在也殊不知無在而
無乎不在地之神化何若哉聖人之神化亦
===
若此也周子曰一故神兩故化張子曰合一
不測爲神推行有漸爲化是盖化生於神非
神何以能化神生於公非公何以能神公而
神神而化天地聖人極其至矣善者好之
聖人無私好也如天地之暑則徧天下皆
暑而不知所以暑者伊誰之使歟惡者惡之
聖人無私惡也如天地之寒則徧天下皆寒
而不知所以寒者伊誰之致歟賞天慶也聖
人不以私心遽喜而行賞罰天誅也聖人不
punctuated: 一或有心，則涉於私矣。私則不足以言公，況謂至公之化乎？非公不足以言神，況謂至神之化乎？聖人中天地以有生，合天地以爲德，體天地以致治，法天地之公，妙天地之神，普天地之化，寂然不動，感而遂通。生者自生，殺者自殺，天何爲也？殊不知無爲而無所不爲，天之神化何如哉！聖人之神化亦猶是也。成者自成，悴者自悴，地何在也？殊不知無在而無乎不在，地之神化何若哉！聖人之神化亦若此也。周子曰：「一故神，兩故化。」張子曰：「合一不測爲神，推行有漸爲化。」是盖化生於神，非神何以能化？神生於公，非公何以能神？公而神，神而化，天地聖人極其至矣。善者好之，聖人無私好也。如天地之暑，則徧天下皆暑，而不知所以暑者，伊誰之使歟？惡者惡之，聖人無私惡也。如天地之寒，則徧天下皆寒，而不知所以寒者，伊誰之致歟？賞，天慶也，聖人不以私心遽喜而行賞；罰，天誅也，聖人不
translation_en:
…If there is the slightest deliberate intention, selfish partiality enters in. With partiality, one cannot speak even of impartiality, much less of the transforming power of utmost impartiality. Without impartiality, one cannot speak even of spiritual efficacy, much less of the transforming power of utmost spiritual efficacy. The sage is born amid Heaven and Earth, accords with Heaven and Earth in his virtue, and embodies Heaven and Earth in bringing about good government. He models himself on their impartiality, gives subtle expression to their spiritual efficacy, and extends their transforming influence everywhere. Quiescent and unmoving, he responds to stimulation and thereby penetrates all things. What lives lives of itself; what is killed is killed of itself. What does Heaven do? People fail to understand that it does nothing yet leaves nothing undone. How wondrous is Heaven’s spiritually efficacious transformation! The sage’s spiritually efficacious transformation is just like this. What flourishes flourishes of itself; what withers withers of itself. Where is Earth in this? People fail to understand that it is nowhere in particular yet nowhere absent. How wondrous is Earth’s spiritually efficacious transformation! The sage’s spiritually efficacious transformation is likewise so.

Master Zhou said, “Because it is one, it is spiritually efficacious; because it is two, it transforms.” Master Zhang said, “Uniting as one and being unfathomable constitutes spiritual efficacy; proceeding by gradual stages constitutes transformation.” Thus transformation arises from spiritual efficacy: without spiritual efficacy, how could there be transformation? Spiritual efficacy arises from impartiality: without impartiality, how could there be spiritual efficacy? Impartiality leads to spiritual efficacy, and spiritual efficacy to transformation. Heaven, Earth, and the sage bring these to their utmost perfection.

The sage loves those who are good, yet has no partiality in his love. It is like the heat of Heaven and Earth: everywhere under Heaven is hot, yet no one knows who makes it so. The sage hates those who are evil, yet has no partiality in his hatred. It is like the cold of Heaven and Earth: everywhere under Heaven is cold, yet no one knows who brings it about. Rewards are Heaven’s blessings: the sage does not bestow rewards in a sudden burst of delight arising from selfish feelings. Punishments are Heaven’s chastisements: the sage does not…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以私心遷怒而行罰聖人之心至公之心也
惟其至公故能以至寡而服天下之衆以一
心而通億兆之心此感彼應蓋有不疾而速
者存焉上行下效蓋有不行而至者在焉動
而無動天之動也靜而無靜地之靜也用一
君子而天下蒙其福其大虛之清明也去一
小人而天下除其害其雷霆之鼓舞也好一
人而千萬人皆勉於爲善殆湯和之宣暢乎
惡一人而千萬人皆懲於爲惡殆窮陰之摧
===
剥乎承天慶以行賞也而民莫不知勸其與
天地之雨露萬物者同一揆奉天誅以行罰
也而民莫不知戒其與天地之霜雪萬物者
無二致聖人之化至神之化也聖人之化出
於至神聖人之神由於至公無彼此無小大
無衆寡無以地之遠近無以勢之强弱無隔
形骸而分爾汝無隔樊墻而分比鄰天下好
惡之心不約而自同聖人賞罰之公不言而
自信所謂立之斯立道之斯行而神化莫能
punctuated:
以私心遷怒而行罰。聖人之心，至公之心也。惟其至公，故能以至寡而服天下之衆，以一心而通億兆之心。此感彼應，蓋有不疾而速者存焉；上行下效，蓋有不行而至者在焉。動而無動，天之動也；靜而無靜，地之靜也。用一君子而天下蒙其福，其大虛之清明也；去一小人而天下除其害，其雷霆之鼓舞也。好一人而千萬人皆勉於爲善，殆湯和之宣暢乎？惡一人而千萬人皆懲於爲惡，殆窮陰之摧剥乎？承天慶以行賞也，而民莫不知勸，其與天地之雨露萬物者同一揆；奉天誅以行罰也，而民莫不知戒，其與天地之霜雪萬物者無二致。
聖人之化，至神之化也。聖人之化出於至神，聖人之神由於至公。無彼此，無小大，無衆寡，無以地之遠近，無以勢之强弱，無隔形骸而分爾汝，無隔樊墻而分比鄰。天下好惡之心，不約而自同；聖人賞罰之公，不言而自信。所謂「立之斯立，道之斯行」，而神化莫能
translation_en:
…inflict punishment by venting anger out of private feeling. The sage’s mind is utterly impartial. Only through this utter impartiality can he, though one among so many, win the allegiance of all under Heaven and, with his single mind, communicate with the minds of countless millions. A stimulus here elicits a response there: something is at work that is swift without haste. Those below emulate what those above practice: something reaches them without traveling. Moving without deliberate movement is the movement of Heaven; resting without deliberate stillness is the stillness of Earth. Employ one exemplary man, and all under Heaven receive his blessings: this is like the clarity and brightness of the great void. Remove one petty man, and all under Heaven are freed of his harm: this is like the stirring power of thunder. Favor one man, and millions exert themselves to do good: is this not like the spreading of genial warmth [?]? Disfavor one man, and millions are deterred from doing evil: is this not like the destructive force of deepest winter? In bestowing rewards, the sage carries out Heaven’s blessings, and everyone knows to strive: this follows the same principle as Heaven and Earth nourishing all things with rain and dew. In administering punishments, he carries out Heaven’s chastisement, and everyone knows to take warning: this is no different from Heaven and Earth subjecting all things to frost and snow.
The sage’s transforming influence is supremely numinous. His transforming influence springs from his supreme numinous efficacy, and his numinous efficacy arises from his utter impartiality. There is no distinction between this and that, small and great, many and few; none based on geographical distance or proximity, or on strength or weakness of power. Bodily separation creates no division between persons, nor do enclosing walls create divisions between neighbors. The likes and dislikes of all under Heaven agree spontaneously, without prior arrangement; the impartiality of the sage’s rewards and punishments commands trust without explanation. As the saying goes, “When he establishes them, they stand firm; when he guides them, they advance,” and his numinous transforming influence none can …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
測其機也緩之斯來動之斯和而神化莫能
窺其涯也吁聖人之好惡賞罰一天地之公
心其神化豈不與天地上下相爲流通者乎
此愚所以謂寂然之中而有感通者寓聖人
之心大造之心也嗟夫堯仁如天而黎民於
變舜德好生而萬邦咸寧此堯舜至公至神
之化也禹克勤克儉而聲教四訖湯克寬克
仁而萬民允懷此禹湯至公至神之化也世
不三代人非三王不拔爲茂之毛者忍而不
===
公其如神化何不殺㲉觫之牛者愛而不公
其如神化何漢削秦令以寬爲治似也然而
𠛬中人氶不免加於骨肉況能運神化於天
下乎唐除肉刑以恕爲治近也然而禁門喋
血不免傷於同氣況能運神化於國家乎迄
宋及元寥寥千載
皇明
天啓
聖祖龍飛德以出治裕乎乾剛而坤厚刑以輔治
punctuated:
測其機也；緩之斯來，動之斯和，而神化莫能窺其涯也。吁！聖人之好惡賞罰，一天地之公心，其神化豈不與天地上下相爲流通者乎？此愚所以謂寂然之中而有感通者寓，聖人之心，大造之心也。

嗟夫！堯仁如天，而黎民於變；舜德好生，而萬邦咸寧：此堯舜至公至神之化也。禹克勤克儉，而聲教四訖；湯克寬克仁，而萬民允懷：此禹湯至公至神之化也。世不三代，人非三王，不拔爲茂之毛者，忍而不公，其如神化何？不殺㲉觫之牛者，愛而不公，其如神化何？漢削秦令，以寬爲治，似也；然而𠛬中人氶，不免加於骨肉，況能運神化於天下乎？唐除肉刑，以恕爲治，近也；然而禁門喋血，不免傷於同氣，況能運神化於國家乎？迄宋及元，寥寥千載。

皇明，天啓聖祖龍飛，德以出治，裕乎乾剛而坤厚；刑以輔治，
translation_en:
…fathom its workings. When he eases them, they come; when he sets them in motion, they become harmonious; yet none can discern the bounds of his wondrous transforming influence. Ah! In his likes and dislikes, rewards and punishments, the sage shares the impartial heart of Heaven and Earth. How could his wondrous transforming influence fail to flow in mutual communion with Heaven above and Earth below? This is why I say that within stillness resides the capacity to respond and communicate: the sage’s heart is the heart of the great creative power.

Alas! Yao’s benevolence was like Heaven, and the common people were transformed. Shun’s virtue cherished life, and the myriad states were all at peace. Such was the utterly impartial and wondrous transforming influence of Yao and Shun. Yu was diligent and frugal, and his renown and teaching reached the four quarters. Tang was magnanimous and benevolent, and the myriad people sincerely cherished him. Such was the utterly impartial and wondrous transforming influence of Yu and Tang. But the age was no longer that of the Three Dynasties, nor were its men the Three Kings. One who would not pluck out a single hair for benefit [?] was hardhearted and lacked impartiality: how could he exercise wondrous transforming influence? One who would not slaughter a trembling ox [?] was loving but lacked impartiality: how could he exercise wondrous transforming influence? The Han reduced the ordinances of Qin and governed through leniency, seemingly resembling this ideal. Yet punishments [?] were still inflicted upon their own flesh and blood; how, then, could they extend wondrous transforming influence throughout the realm? The Tang abolished mutilating punishments and governed through forbearance, coming close to this ideal. Yet blood was shed at the palace gates, and even brothers suffered injury; how, then, could they extend wondrous transforming influence throughout the state? Down through the Song and Yuan, a thousand years passed with scarcely anyone to exemplify it.

Under our august Ming, Heaven brought forth the sagely founder, who rose like a dragon. Through virtue he established his government, abundantly embodying the strength of Qian, Heaven, and the generosity of Kun, Earth; through punishment he supported his government…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
廓乎天涵而地育
列聖相承益隆丕緒則至公至神之化端有在於
我
朝矣愚何容喙謹論
表
擬宋以蘇轍爲尚書右丞謝表
方輿
同考試官學正陳　批〔得體非出入歐蘇者筆力詎〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔擬宋表得宋人語可嘉〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔得體〕
===
伏以
廟堂寀分班聯三省之崇
禁闥論思職重六卿之選顧茲要秩宜畀宏
材伏念臣轍西蜀鄙夫彫蟲小技竊眉山之
秀氣名忝兄齊涉洙泗之餘波學由父授早
冐制科之舉中叨條例之司性本不回才無
適用言干宮禁荷
punctuated:
廓乎天涵而地育。列聖相承，益隆丕緒，則至公至神之化，端有在於我朝矣。愚何容喙？謹論。

表

擬宋以蘇轍爲尚書右丞謝表
方輿
同考試官學正陳　批〔得體，非出入歐蘇者，筆力詎〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔擬宋表，得宋人語，可嘉。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔得體。〕

伏以：廟堂寀分，班聯三省之崇；禁闥論思，職重六卿之選。顧茲要秩，宜畀宏材。伏念臣轍，西蜀鄙夫，彫蟲小技。竊眉山之秀氣，名忝兄齊；涉洙泗之餘波，學由父授。早冐制科之舉，中叨條例之司。性本不回，才無適用。言干宮禁，荷
translation_en:
…expansive as Heaven in its encompassing embrace and Earth in its nurture. Successive sage sovereigns have carried on the succession, further magnifying the great enterprise. Thus the transforming influence of utmost impartiality and spiritual efficacy assuredly resides in our dynasty. What room is there for an ignorant man like me to add anything? Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial

A Memorial of Thanks Written in the Voice of Su Zhe upon His Appointment as Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs under the Song
By Fang Yu

I humbly consider: among the colleagues allotted duties in the council of state, this rank stands within the exalted Three Departments; in deliberating and reflecting within the palace precincts, its responsibilities give it weight among those chosen for the Six Ministries. Such an important office should indeed be entrusted to a man of great ability.

I humbly reflect that I, your servant Zhe, am an uncultivated man from western Shu, possessing only the petty skill of carving insects—literary ornament. Having undeservedly partaken of Meishan's finest vital spirit, I am unworthily ranked beside my elder brother in reputation; having entered the lingering currents of the Zhu and Si rivers—the Confucian tradition—I received my learning from my father. Early on, I presumptuously undertook the special examination; later, I undeservedly served in the bureau for drafting regulations. My nature has always been unbending, but my talents have proved unsuited to practical use. My words encroached upon matters within the palace, yet I received…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
先朝之曲賜登庸力溫青瑣致大臣之隂加排斥
身雖外補心無內慚千里賜環重依光於
日月內臺執法何有肅乎風霜惟邪正難以並居
似薰蕕不可同器章蔡之奸既去君子方為
舒眉調亭之論不行小人因之切齒自分竄
身之無地豈擬獎擢之自
天有覥心顏益增悚懼斯蓋伏遇
○○○○道參堯舜治邁成康奉
膺聖之慈顏懋循大孝紹
===
耿光之烈祖丕顯鴻謨鑒情偽於離照之中察賢
否於晉明之下用人不殊用藥兼收溲勃參
苓取士有若取材何間楩楠居楔以茲厚
寵俯及凡庸德薄才涼任重恐譏於負乘血誠
心赤攄忠效報於銜環敢不仰三事之餘光
裁六聯之滯論亮天工熙帝載誓祭國論之
餘補袞闕輯黎元用副鼎鉉之寄伏願
聖學緝熙
聖德廣運龍出河而龜出洛照一代之人文乾為
punctuated: 先朝之曲賜登庸，力溫青瑣，致大臣之隂加排斥。身雖外補，心無內慚。千里賜環，重依光於日月；內臺執法，何有肅乎風霜？惟邪正難以並居，似薰蕕不可同器。章蔡之奸既去，君子方為舒眉；調亭之論不行，小人因之切齒。自分竄身之無地，豈擬獎擢之自天？有覥心顏，益增悚懼。斯蓋伏遇○○○○，道參堯舜，治邁成康，奉膺聖之慈顏，懋循大孝；紹耿光之烈祖，丕顯鴻謨。鑒情偽於離照之中，察賢否於晉明之下。用人不殊用藥，兼收溲勃參苓；取士有若取材，何間楩楠居楔？以茲厚寵，俯及凡庸。德薄才涼，任重恐譏於負乘；血誠心赤，攄忠效報於銜環。敢不仰三事之餘光，裁六聯之滯論，亮天工，熙帝載，誓祭國論之餘，補袞闕，輯黎元，用副鼎鉉之寄？伏願聖學緝熙，聖德廣運，龍出河而龜出洛，照一代之人文；乾為
translation_en:
…the late sovereign’s exceptional favor in raising me to office. My efforts at the palace gates [?] brought covert exclusion at the hands of high ministers. Though assigned to a post outside the capital, I felt no shame within. A ring bestowed upon me a thousand li away summoned me back, once more to bask in the light of sun and moon. Enforcing the law in the Censorate, how could I possess the sternness of wind and frost? Yet the crooked and upright cannot dwell together, just as fragrant and foul herbs cannot share one vessel. Once the treacherous Zhang and Cai had departed, gentlemen could at last relax their brows; when proposals for compromise failed to prevail, petty men consequently gnashed their teeth. I expected to find nowhere even to hide myself; how could I have imagined that reward and promotion would descend from Heaven? Ashamed in heart and countenance, I am all the more apprehensive.

This is surely because I have humbly encountered ○○○○, whose Way equals those of Yao and Shun and whose government surpasses those of Kings Cheng and Kang. Reverently attending upon the kindly countenance of Yingsheng [?], you diligently practice the highest filial devotion; succeeding your illustrious ancestors of radiant virtue, you magnificently manifest their grand designs. With the penetrating illumination of Li, you distinguish sincerity from falsehood; beneath the advancing brightness of Jin, you discern the worthy and unworthy. Employing people is no different from using medicines: humble remedies such as soubo [?] are accepted alongside ginseng and poria. Selecting scholars resembles selecting timber: why distinguish fine hardwoods such as pian and nan from ju and xie [?]? Through this abundant favor, your grace has reached even an ordinary man like me. My virtue is slight and my talent meager; with so weighty a charge, I fear the reproach of one who bears a porter’s load yet rides in a carriage. With utter sincerity and a loyal heart, I shall express my devotion and repay your kindness, like the creature that carried a ring in its beak.

How could I fail to look up to the reflected glory of the Three Dukes, resolve stalled deliberations concerning the six forms of administrative cooperation, assist Heaven’s work, and advance the emperor’s undertakings? I pledge to contribute to deliberations on state affairs [?], remedy shortcomings in imperial government, and bring harmony to the common people, thereby fulfilling the trust placed in me to assist the chief ministers. I humbly wish that Your Majesty’s sacred learning may continually shine brighter and your sacred virtue spread far and wide; that a dragon may emerge from the Yellow River and a tortoise from the Luo River, illuminating the cultural achievements of your age; and that Qian may serve as…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
綱而坤爲維綿萬年之國祚臣𣽂無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
策
第一問
===
同考試官學正陳　批〔古今事實條答詳明必博學之士也是用錄出〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔考據不遺非欽誦制書之熟者能之乎〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔條答無遺必熟於聖訓者〕
對聖人出而致治之道本諸身聖經作而致
治之道垂於世是道莫大於人倫也聖人之
身斯道之本聖經之經斯道之迹二帝之所
punctuated:
綱而坤爲維，綿萬年之國祚。臣𣽂無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
策
第一問
同考試官學正陳批〔古今事實條答詳明，必博學之士也，是用錄出。〕
考試官教諭吾批〔考據不遺，非欽誦制書之熟者能之乎？〕
考試官教諭趙批〔條答無遺，必熟於聖訓者。〕
對：聖人出而致治之道本諸身，聖經作而致治之道垂於世。是道莫大於人倫也。聖人之身，斯道之本；聖經之經，斯道之迹。二帝之所
translation_en:
…the guiding cord, while Earth forms the binding strands, prolonging the dynasty’s good fortune for ten thousand years. Your servant, whose name is transcribed as 𣽂 [?], looks up to Heaven and reveres Your Sagely Majesty with boundless fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude and make it known to Your Majesty.

Policy Essay
First Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor: 〔The historical facts, ancient and modern, are set out in detailed and lucid answers, point by point. He must be a man of broad learning; hence this essay has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Wu, School Instructor: 〔His examination of the evidence omits nothing. Could anyone accomplish this without thorough familiarity gained by reverently reciting the imperial writings?〕

Comment by Examiner Zhao, School Instructor: 〔His answers omit no point. He must be thoroughly familiar with the imperial teachings.〕

Response: When a sage arises, the Way by which he brings about good government is rooted in his own person; when the sages’ classics are composed, the Way by which good government is achieved is handed down to the world. Nothing in this Way is more important than human relationships. The sage’s person is the foundation of this Way; the texts of the sages’ classics are its traces. That by which the Two Emperors…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
以帝天下者此也三王之所以王天下者此
也其載諸經傳如典謨訓誥之文何莫非斯
道之所寓也肆惟我
太祖高皇帝
太宗文皇帝
宣宗章皇帝
聖聖相承繼天立極心帝王之心體帝王之道既
躬行以化導乎民必立言以垂教于世故於
萬幾之暇條成
===
大誥□□繇爲善陰隲孝順事實五倫書頒示中外
宸翰奎章輝暎天地玉軸瑶編昭回日月浩乎其
無涯際茫乎其無畔岸考其要歸無非欲人
明五倫以惇道化而已夫五倫一書其載古
今能盡人倫之道者星分昈列雖更僕未能
悉數姑以明問所及者言之君道莫大乎敬
天法祖也莫大乎節儉剛明也若堯之欽若
昊天敬授民時舜之在璇璣以齊七政盤庚
punctuated: 以帝天下者，此也；三王之所以王天下者，此也。其載諸經傳，如典謨訓誥之文，何莫非斯道之所寓也？肆惟我太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝、宣宗章皇帝，聖聖相承，繼天立極，心帝王之心，體帝王之道。既躬行以化導乎民，必立言以垂教于世，故於萬幾之暇，條成《大誥》、□□繇、《爲善陰隲》、《孝順事實》、《五倫書》，頒示中外。宸翰奎章，輝暎天地；玉軸瑶編，昭回日月。浩乎其無涯際，茫乎其無畔岸。考其要歸，無非欲人明五倫，以惇道化而已。夫《五倫》一書，其載古今能盡人倫之道者，星分昈列，雖更僕未能悉數。姑以明問所及者言之：君道莫大乎敬天法祖也，莫大乎節儉剛明也。若堯之欽若昊天，敬授民時；舜之在璇璣，以齊七政；盤庚
translation_en:
…thereby ruled All under Heaven as emperors: it was through this Way. It was likewise through this Way that the Three Kings ruled All under Heaven as kings. Among the writings preserved in the classics and their commentaries, such as the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements, which does not embody this Way?

Thus our Emperor Gao of the Taizu reign, Emperor Wen of the Taizong reign, and Emperor Zhang of the Xuanzong reign succeeded one another as sages, continuing Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard. They took the minds of the ancient emperors and kings as their own and embodied their Way. Having personally practiced it to transform and guide the people, they necessarily also set down teachings to instruct the world. Accordingly, in the intervals between their myriad affairs of state, they compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), [an unclear title: □□繇, ?], Good Deeds and Hidden Merit (Weishan Yinzhi), Accounts of Filial Piety and Obedience (Xiaoshun Shishi), and the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun Shu), and promulgated them within and beyond the capital. These imperial writings and resplendent compositions illuminate Heaven and Earth; their jade rollers and precious volumes shine with the sun and moon. Vast, they have no limit; boundless, they have no shore. Examining their essential purpose, one finds nothing other than the desire that people understand the five human relationships and thereby strengthen moral transformation through the Way.

The Book of the Five Relationships records people of ancient and recent times who fully fulfilled the Way of human relationships, arranging them distinctly like stars. Even with attendants taking turns, one could not enumerate them all. Let me speak provisionally of those addressed in your discerning question. In the Way of the ruler, nothing is greater than revering Heaven and emulating the ancestors; nothing is greater than frugality, firmness, and discernment. Thus Yao reverently followed August Heaven and respectfully imparted the seasons to the people; Shun examined the astronomical instrument to bring the seven celestial regulators into harmony; Pan Geng…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
行湯之政成王繼序不忘此其敬天法祖盖
與我
太祖之遇旱憂農徒步請禱
太宗之繼承天位恪遵成憲者同一道焉禹之菲
食惡衣周文之卑服即功武帝斥田蚡之請
孝宣辨燕王之誣此其節儉剛明盖與我
太祖之不作苑臺以費民財
太宗之辨民交通特釋其罪者同一揆焉以臣道
言之莫先於守法持正也莫先於忠義蕭介
===
也如犯蹕之止於罰金不肯順旨故人必正
以贓罪不徇私恩非張釋之蘇章之守法乎
龍鬪洧淵力拒禳祟之請帝欲廢立廷爭而
不奉詔非子產周昌之持正乎至如我
朝宋濂文爲天策知事守將欲擅殺人而力爭
其不可卒蒙賚予之榮較諸張釋之蘇章之
輩何讓拒蘇峻之逆賊而父死於忠子死於
孝當禄山之不道而兄死於前弟死於後此
卞壼顏杲卿之忠義也以不貪爲寶而不寶
punctuated:
行湯之政，成王繼序不忘，此其敬天法祖，盖與我太祖之遇旱憂農、徒步請禱，太宗之繼承天位、恪遵成憲者，同一道焉。禹之菲食惡衣，周文之卑服即功，武帝斥田蚡之請，孝宣辨燕王之誣，此其節儉剛明，盖與我太祖之不作苑臺以費民財，太宗之辨民交通、特釋其罪者，同一揆焉。
以臣道言之，莫先於守法持正也，莫先於忠義蕭介也。如犯蹕之止於罰金，不肯順旨；故人必正以贓罪，不徇私恩：非張釋之、蘇章之守法乎？龍鬪洧淵，力拒禳祟之請；帝欲廢立，廷爭而不奉詔：非子產、周昌之持正乎？至如我朝宋濂文爲天策知事，守將欲擅殺人，而力爭其不可，卒蒙賚予之榮，較諸張釋之、蘇章之輩何讓？拒蘇峻之逆賊，而父死於忠、子死於孝；當禄山之不道，而兄死於前、弟死於後：此卞壼、顏杲卿之忠義也。以不貪爲寶，而不寶
translation_en:
…carried out Tang’s policies, and King Cheng continued the succession without forgetting his predecessors. Their reverence for Heaven and emulation of their ancestors followed the same Way as our Taizu, who, distressed for the farmers during drought, went on foot to offer prayers, and our Taizong, who succeeded to the heavenly throne and scrupulously observed established institutions. Yu ate sparingly and wore poor clothing; King Wen of Zhou wore humble garments and devoted himself to work; Emperor Wu rejected Tian Fen’s request; and Emperor Xiaoxuan discerned the falsehood of the Prince of Yan’s accusation. Their frugality, firmness, and discernment followed the same standard as our Taizu, who refrained from building parks and terraces at the people’s expense, and our Taizong, who investigated commoners’ alleged collusion [?] and specially pardoned their offenses.
As for the Way of a minister, nothing takes precedence over upholding the law and maintaining what is right; nothing takes precedence over loyalty, righteousness, and incorruptible integrity [?]. In the case of someone who violated the restrictions surrounding the imperial procession, the punishment was limited to a fine, despite the emperor’s wishes; an old friend was duly punished for corruption, without indulgence on account of personal ties. Were these not examples of Zhang Shizhi and Su Zhang upholding the law? When dragons fought in a deep pool of the Wei River, a request to perform rites to avert evil was firmly rejected; when the emperor wished to depose the heir apparent and install another, the proposal was contested at court and the command was not obeyed. Were these not examples of Zichan and Zhou Chang maintaining what was right? Likewise, Song Lian [?] of our dynasty, while serving as Office Manager in the Tiance office, firmly argued against a garrison commander’s intention to execute someone without authorization, and was ultimately honored with rewards. In what respect was he inferior to men such as Zhang Shizhi and Su Zhang? In resisting the rebel Su Jun, the father died for loyalty and the sons for filial devotion; in confronting Lushan’s lawlessness, the elder brother died first and the younger brother afterward. Such was the loyalty and righteousness of Bian Kun and Yan Gaoqing. To regard freedom from greed as a treasure, rather than to treasure…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
金玉以清白遺子孫而不計產業此司城子
罕司徒楊震之廉介也至若我
朝孫炎爲處州總制禁黠之徒欲脅以降而罵
賊以死終獲爵土之封較諸卞壼顏杲卿之
儔何亞古者百里負米之仲由名有家法之
公綽與今之母病不愈吮疽嘗糞之李英親
沒哀慟蔬食廬墓之張翼同一父子之盡道
也可知古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺不忘糟
糠之宋弘與今之夫溺水而自投二屍並出
===
之袁氏夫死不嫁雙節並稱之俞氏同一夫
婦之盡道也可見若趙孝趙禮之爭死不懼
莚式張元之雖死不易以至不肯分財異居
隨所欲取之李貞非古今能盡兄弟朋友之
倫者乎然以五倫一書質之於
大誥孝順事實爲善陰隲三書之旨則
大誥所載君臣同游者非五倫書所謂盡君臣之
道者乎孝順事實所載武王之達孝非五倫
書所謂盡父子之倫者乎爲善陰隲所載馮
punctuated:
金玉，以清白遺子孫而不計產業，此司城子罕、司徒楊震之廉介也。至若我朝孫炎爲處州總制，禁黠之徒欲脅以降，而罵賊以死，終獲爵土之封，較諸卞壼、顏杲卿之儔何亞？古者百里負米之仲由、名有家法之公綽，與今之母病不愈、吮疽嘗糞之李英，親沒哀慟、蔬食廬墓之張翼，同一父子之盡道也，可知。古者夫婦相敬如賓之冀缺、不忘糟糠之宋弘，與今之夫溺水而自投、二屍並出之袁氏，夫死不嫁、雙節並稱之俞氏，同一夫婦之盡道也，可見。若趙孝、趙禮之爭死不懼，莚式、張元之雖死不易，以至不肯分財異居、隨所欲取之李貞，非古今能盡兄弟朋友之倫者乎？
然以《五倫》一書質之於《大誥》《孝順事實》《爲善陰隲》三書之旨，則《大誥》所載君臣同游者，非《五倫》書所謂盡君臣之道者乎？《孝順事實》所載武王之達孝，非《五倫》書所謂盡父子之倫者乎？《爲善陰隲》所載馮
translation_en:
…gold and jade, and leaving an unblemished reputation to one’s descendants without concern for property: such was the incorruptible integrity of Zihan, Minister of Works, and Yang Zhen, Minister of Education. As for Sun Yan of our dynasty, when he served as Regional Commander at Chuzhou, a band of cunning men [?] sought to force him to surrender, but he died cursing the rebels and ultimately received a grant of noble rank and lands. How was he inferior to the likes of Bian Kun and Yan Gaoqing? Zhong You of antiquity, who carried rice a hundred li, and Gongchuo, renowned for his household discipline, may be recognized as having fulfilled the way of father and son just as did Li Ying of our own times, who sucked his mother’s abscess and tasted her excrement when her illness would not heal, and Zhang Yi, who mourned bitterly when his parent died, ate only vegetables, and lived in a hut beside the grave. Ji Que of antiquity, who treated his wife with the respect due a guest, and Song Hong, who did not forget the wife who had shared his poverty, may be seen as having fulfilled the way of husband and wife just as did Lady Yuan of our own times, who threw herself into the water when her husband drowned, their two bodies being recovered together, and Lady Yu, who refused to remarry after her husband’s death and whose chastity was celebrated jointly with another’s. As for Zhao Xiao and Zhao Li, who each fearlessly sought to die in the other’s place, and Yan Shi and Zhang Yuan [?], who remained steadfast even in death, down to Li Zhen, who refused to divide the family property and establish a separate household, allowing others to take whatever they wished—were these not people, ancient and modern, who fully upheld the relationships between brothers and between friends?
Yet if we compare the single book Five Relationships (Wulun) with the purport of the three books Grand Pronouncements (Dagao), Accounts of Filial Obedience (Xiaoshun shishi), and Hidden Recompense for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), is not the account in Grand Pronouncements of ruler and ministers traveling together an instance of what Five Relationships calls fully observing the way of ruler and minister? Is not the account in Accounts of Filial Obedience of King Wu’s consummate filial piety an instance of what Five Relationships calls fully upholding the relationship between father and son? As for Feng, recorded in Hidden Recompense for Doing Good…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
式燮贊叔通堅不與五倫書所謂盡夫婦
之道者同一意歟是則五倫之理包天括地
而是書足以該之三書之旨殊塗異轍而是
書足以會之溥天率土不賓烏號之弓而寶
此書四方萬國不蔵曲阜之履而蔵此書斯
世斯民得以盡彛倫惇道化熙熙然於光天
化日之下可以匹休唐虞三代之治者豈無
所自
第二問
===
同考試官學正陳　批〔欵對詳明必熟於大學衍義者也兼學如此場屋幾人〕
揚應
考試官教諭吾　批〔條答無遺且忠愛之意溢於言表蓋久學而有志者歟歎羡歎羨〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔答問詳悉非熟於衍義者不能〕
對甚矣天下不可一日無大學之書而衍義
一書亦不可以一日不講也脩己治人之道
於焉而存化民成俗之本於焉而在涵養君
punctuated:
式燮贊叔通堅，不與五倫書所謂盡夫婦之道者同一意歟？是則五倫之理，包天括地，而是書足以該之；三書之旨，殊塗異轍，而是書足以會之。溥天率土，不賓烏號之弓而寶此書；四方萬國，不蔵曲阜之履而蔵此書。斯世斯民，得以盡彛倫，惇道化，熙熙然於光天化日之下，可以匹休唐虞三代之治者，豈無所自？

第二問

同考試官學正陳，批〔欵對詳明，必熟於大學衍義者也。兼學如此，場屋幾人？〕

揚應

考試官教諭吾，批〔條答無遺，且忠愛之意溢於言表，蓋久學而有志者歟？歎羡歎羨！〕

考試官教諭趙，批〔答問詳悉，非熟於衍義者不能。〕

對：甚矣！天下不可一日無《大學》之書，而《衍義》一書亦不可以一日不講也。脩己治人之道，於焉而存；化民成俗之本，於焉而在。涵養君
translation_en:
… Shi, Xie Zan, and Shu Tongjian [?]: do these not express the same idea as what the Book of the Five Relationships calls fully fulfilling the way of husband and wife? Thus, the principles of the five relationships encompass heaven and earth, and this book suffices to comprehend them all. The purport of the three books follows different paths and courses, yet this book suffices to bring them together. Throughout all beneath heaven, people honor not the Wuhao bow but treasure this book; in every quarter and every realm, they preserve not the shoes of Qufu but preserve this book. That the people of this age can fully fulfill the constant human relationships, strengthen moral transformation, and live in harmony beneath the radiant light of enlightened rule, matching the glorious governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—surely this has its source!

Second Question

Associate Examiner Chen, School Instructor, comments: 〔The response is detailed and clear; he must be thoroughly familiar with the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning. How many in the examination halls possess such breadth of learning?〕

Yang Ying

Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔He answers each point without omission, and his loyal devotion overflows beyond his words. Surely he is someone of long study and firm aspiration! Admirable, admirable!〕

Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔His answers are detailed and thorough; only someone well acquainted with the Extended Meaning could achieve this.〕

Response: How vital it is! The world cannot go a single day without the Great Learning, nor can the Extended Meaning go a single day without being expounded. Herein resides the way of cultivating oneself and governing others; herein lies the foundation for transforming the people and establishing good customs. Nurturing the ruler’s …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
德緝熙聖學亦莫不於是而基學者一日不
由乎此則流於異端惑於邪說無以開發聰
明而措諸事業君天下者一日不由於此則
身有不脩化有不行而天下不得蒙至治之
澤此西山真文忠公衍義之所以作而執事
之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟愚雖不敏敢不
紬繹舊聞以答明問之萬一乎夫大學一書
其經出於孔氏其傳出於曾子二程爲之表
章朱子爲之章句綱領條目畢備無遺誠聖
===
賢進德之閫奥君天下者之律例格令後世
莫能尚已至宋真文忠公當理宗之朝圖致
治之道以爲治道莫大於大學於是首劉聖
賢性命道德之言旁采古今治亂安危之迹
推本帝王爲治之序探求帝王爲學之本詳
著格物致知誠意正心脩身齊家之要而及
其目以爲衍義一書其所以闡義理之淵微
發聖賢之未發爲帝王之監戒豈小補哉觀
其述帝堯克明峻德而致黎民於變皐謨身
punctuated: 德、緝熙聖學，亦莫不於是而基。學者一日不由乎此，則流於異端，惑於邪說，無以開發聰明而措諸事業；君天下者一日不由於此，則身有不脩，化有不行，而天下不得蒙至治之澤。此西山真文忠公衍義之所以作，而執事之所以惓惓詢之承學也歟？愚雖不敏，敢不紬繹舊聞，以答明問之萬一乎？夫《大學》一書，其經出於孔氏，其傳出於曾子，二程爲之表章，朱子爲之章句，綱領條目畢備無遺，誠聖賢進德之閫奥、君天下者之律例格令，後世莫能尚已。至宋真文忠公，當理宗之朝，圖致治之道，以爲治道莫大於《大學》。於是首劉聖賢性命道德之言，旁采古今治亂安危之迹，推本帝王爲治之序，探求帝王爲學之本，詳著格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家之要，而及其目，以爲《衍義》一書。其所以闡義理之淵微，發聖賢之未發，爲帝王之監戒，豈小補哉？觀其述帝堯克明峻德而致黎民於變，《皐謨》身
translation_en:
…the ruler’s virtue and the continued illumination of sagely learning likewise all find their foundation here. If scholars depart from this for even a single day, they stray into heterodox teachings and become deluded by pernicious doctrines, with no means of developing their understanding and applying it to practical affairs. If one who rules all under Heaven departs from this for even a single day, his personal cultivation will be deficient and his transforming influence will fail to reach the people, so that the realm cannot receive the blessings of consummate governance. Is this not why Master Zhen of Xishan, posthumously titled Wenzhong, composed the Extended Meaning, and why you so earnestly question us students about it? Though I am slow of understanding, how could I dare not draw out what I have previously learned, to answer even a fraction of your discerning question?

As for the Great Learning, its canonical text derives from Confucius and its commentary from Zengzi. The two Cheng masters brought it to prominence, and Master Zhu supplied its chapter-and-sentence commentary. Its guiding principles and particular articles are fully provided, with nothing omitted. It is truly the inner sanctuary in which sages and worthies advance in virtue, and the statutes, substatutes, regulations, and ordinances for those who rule all under Heaven. Later ages have been unable to surpass it.

In the Song dynasty, Master Zhen Wenzhong, during the reign of Lizong, considered the means of achieving good governance and judged that nothing was more important to the Way of governing than the Great Learning. He therefore first assembled [?] the sayings of sages and worthies concerning human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and virtue, and gathered widely the historical traces of order and disorder, security and peril, past and present. He traced to its source the sequence by which emperors and kings governed, and explored the foundations of their learning. He set out in detail the essentials of investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, and regulating the family, together with their particular subdivisions, thereby composing the Extended Meaning. In elucidating the profound subtleties of moral principle, bringing forth what the sages and worthies had left unexpressed, and providing a mirror and admonition for emperors and kings, could its contribution be called small?

Consider how it recounts Emperor Yao’s ability to manifest his lofty virtue and thereby bring about the transformation of the common people, and, in the Counsels of Gao Yao, the words concerning personal…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
脩思永而邇可遠在茲與夫四海雖遠致治
在心之語則帝王爲治之序可知矣述伊訓
太甲立愛惟親立敬惟長以終於四海詩美
文王刑于寡妻至于兄弟以御于家邦與夫
治天下有本身之謂也之言又豈不可見其
序哉其述堯舜禹湯文武或執中懋德或宅
心建極以至勉彊學問行道之辭則帝王為
學之本可知矣述漢唐魏陳諸君或以王霸
雜治或以音律爲高以至或專文賦游宴之
===
樂夫豈得其本哉其格物致知之要曰明道
術其目則天理人心之正吾道源流之正異
端之差王霸之異也而審治體非在分德刑
先後別義利輕重乎曰辨人材其目則聖賢
觀人之法帝王知人之事姦雄之術憸邪之
情也而察民情非在生靈嚮背田里休戚乎
若夫誠意正心之要曰崇畏敬則崇脩己事
天之敬崇遇災臨民之敬及夫操存省察之
功規警箴戒之助並曰戒逸欲則戒沈湎于
punctuated:
脩思永，而邇可遠在茲，與夫「四海雖遠，致治在心」之語，則帝王爲治之序可知矣。述《伊訓》《太甲》「立愛惟親，立敬惟長，以終於四海」，《詩》美文王「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦」，與夫「治天下有本，身之謂也」之言，又豈不可見其序哉？其述堯舜禹湯文武，或執中懋德，或宅心建極，以至勉彊學問行道之辭，則帝王為學之本可知矣。述漢唐魏陳諸君，或以王霸雜治，或以音律爲高，以至或專文賦游宴之樂，夫豈得其本哉？

其格物致知之要，曰明道術，其目則天理人心之正、吾道源流之正、異端之差、王霸之異也。而審治體，非在分德刑先後、別義利輕重乎？曰辨人材，其目則聖賢觀人之法、帝王知人之事、姦雄之術、憸邪之情也。而察民情，非在生靈嚮背、田里休戚乎？

若夫誠意正心之要，曰崇畏敬，則崇脩己事天之敬，崇遇災臨民之敬，及夫操存省察之功、規警箴戒之助。並曰戒逸欲，則戒沈湎于
translation_en:
…cultivating oneself and thinking of what endures, with the extension from what is near to what is distant depending on this, together with the statement, “Though the lands within the Four Seas are distant, bringing them to good order depends on the heart”—from these, the sequence by which emperors and kings establish good government can be understood. The work recounts the teachings of the “Instructions of Yi” (Yi xun) and “Tai Jia”: “Establish love toward one’s parents and reverence toward one’s elders, extending these ultimately throughout the Four Seas”; the praise of King Wen in the Odes: “He set an example for his wife, extended it to his brothers, and thereby governed his household and state”; and the saying, “Governing the world has a root: this means one’s own person.” Can the sequence not also be seen in these?

It recounts how Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu held fast to the Mean and exerted themselves in virtue, or settled their hearts and established the supreme standard, together with statements about diligently pursuing learning and practicing the Way. From these, the foundation of imperial and royal learning can be understood. It recounts how various rulers of Han, Tang, Wei, and Chen mingled the methods of true kings and hegemons in government, or esteemed musical theory as the highest attainment, or even devoted themselves exclusively to literary compositions and rhapsodies and the pleasures of excursions and banquets. How could they have grasped that foundation?

Among its essentials for investigating things and extending knowledge, it names “clarifying the Way and its methods.” The particular topics are the correctness of Heaven’s principles and the human heart, the orthodox origins and transmission of our Way, the errors of heterodox teachings, and the distinction between true kingship and hegemony. As for examining the principles of government, does this not consist in distinguishing the precedence of virtue over punishment and the greater weight of righteousness over profit? It also names “discerning human talent.” The particular topics are the sages’ and worthies’ methods of judging people, emperors’ and kings’ acts of recognizing people’s abilities, the techniques of unscrupulous men of ambition, and the dispositions of the crafty and wicked. As for investigating the people’s circumstances, does this not concern whether the populace gives or withdraws its allegiance, and whether rural communities prosper or suffer?

As for the essentials of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the heart, it names “exalting awe and reverence”: fostering reverence in cultivating oneself and serving Heaven, and in confronting calamities and governing the people, together with the work of preserving and examining the heart and the assistance afforded by admonitions, warnings, and injunctions. It also names “guarding against indolence and desire,” which means guarding against becoming immersed in…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
酒戒荒淫於色及夫盤逸游田之戒窮奢極
侈之戒也謹言行為脩身之要則發號施令
之際其可以不慎正威儀為脩身之要則在
宮在廷之容不可以不謹若夫齊家之要不
外乎重妃匹嚴內治也謹選立之道賴規警
之益以至內臣忠謹之禍非其目而何又不
外乎定國本教戚屬建立之計宜蚤諭教之
法宜豫以至外家驕溢之禍非其目而何夫
大學之綱目如彼其大而詳衍義之具載又
===
如此其備而切信矣哉聖賢進德之方帝王
致治之道不可一日無者也雖然明大學之
道在致知推大學之道在力行而所以致知
力行之方則又在一敬而已愚生於此實踐
之功固有所未盡而探討之功則未嘗不力
倘蒙執事與而進之使得立
玉階寸地續
翠幄一貂敢不以平生所學竭涓埃以助
海嶽之萬一乎謹對
punctuated:
酒，戒荒淫於色，及夫盤逸游田之戒、窮奢極侈之戒也。謹言行為脩身之要，則發號施令之際，其可以不慎？正威儀為脩身之要，則在宮在廷之容，不可以不謹。若夫齊家之要，不外乎重妃匹、嚴內治也。謹選立之道，賴規警之益，以至內臣忠謹之禍，非其目而何？又不外乎定國本、教戚屬。建立之計宜蚤，諭教之法宜豫，以至外家驕溢之禍，非其目而何？夫《大學》之綱目，如彼其大而詳；《衍義》之具載，又如此其備而切。信矣哉，聖賢進德之方、帝王致治之道，不可一日無者也！

雖然，明《大學》之道在致知，推《大學》之道在力行，而所以致知力行之方，則又在一敬而已。愚生於此，實踐之功固有所未盡，而探討之功則未嘗不力。倘蒙執事與而進之，使得立玉階寸地，續翠幄一貂，敢不以平生所學，竭涓埃以助海嶽之萬一乎？謹對。
translation_en:
…wine; guard against debauchery in sexual pleasures, as well as against idle indulgence in excursions and hunting, and against extravagance and luxury carried to extremes. If care in speech and conduct is essential to cultivating oneself, how could one fail to exercise caution when issuing commands and promulgating orders? If rectifying one’s dignified bearing is essential to cultivating oneself, one must be scrupulous about one’s demeanor both within the palace and at court. As for the essentials of regulating the family, these consist simply in attaching importance to the imperial consort and strictly ordering the inner palace. Exercising care in selecting and installing a consort, benefiting from admonitions and warnings, and even the calamities arising from palace attendants’ loyalty and circumspection [?]—what are these if not its subsidiary topics? They also consist simply in securing the foundation of the state through the succession and instructing imperial relatives. Plans for establishing an heir should be made early, and methods of instruction prepared beforehand; even the calamities arising from the arrogance and excesses of consorts’ families—what are these if not its subsidiary topics? The guiding principles and subsidiary topics of the Great Learning are thus extensive and detailed, while their full exposition in the Amplified Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) is so comprehensive and pertinent. Truly, these are the means by which sages and worthies advance in virtue and the Way by which emperors and kings achieve good government: they cannot be dispensed with for even a single day!

Nevertheless, understanding the Way of the Great Learning lies in extending knowledge, and putting that Way into practice lies in earnest action. The means of extending knowledge and acting earnestly, in turn, lie solely in reverent attentiveness. In this regard, my own efforts at practice admittedly remain incomplete, but I have never failed to exert myself in study and inquiry. Should you gentlemen favor me with your approval and advancement, allowing me a mere inch of standing room upon the jade steps and a place as one more sable-capped attendant beneath the emerald canopy, would I dare fail to devote all that I have learned throughout my life, exhausting my contributions, slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust, to add even the smallest fraction to the imperial seas and mountains? Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第三問
王佐
同考試官學正張　批　治教一策關涉甚大此作識
人情善措置而又不失治教之本用世之士也高薦
何忝
考試官教諭吾　批　策有處置非識義理達時務
者不能録出允當
考試官教諭趙　批　究政教之本酌時措之宜可
謂達於治體者表而出之
君天下者莫先於脩政而立教成政教者必
本於制禮以作樂蓋政教不舉固不足以言
治禮樂不脩又何以為政教之本君天下者
可不知所本乎執事以此為問其期待愚生
以用世之意非淺淺也敢不援古據今以對
夫禮以辨上下樂以和民情虞之禮樂本於
帝舜之德而典以夷夔三禮脩而五禮明六
律和而八音諧後世固莫能尚矣然禮緣人
情樂隨風氣而損益先王之舊以備一代之
punctuated:
第三問

王佐

同考試官學正張　批：治教一策，關涉甚大。此作識人情，善措置，而又不失治教之本，用世之士也。高薦何忝？

考試官教諭吾　批：策有處置，非識義理、達時務者不能。録出允當。

考試官教諭趙　批：究政教之本，酌時措之宜，可謂達於治體者，表而出之。

君天下者，莫先於脩政而立教；成政教者，必本於制禮以作樂。蓋政教不舉，固不足以言治；禮樂不脩，又何以為政教之本？君天下者，可不知所本乎？執事以此為問，其期待愚生以用世之意，非淺淺也。敢不援古據今以對？

夫禮以辨上下，樂以和民情。虞之禮樂，本於帝舜之德，而典以夷夔。三禮脩而五禮明，六律和而八音諧，後世固莫能尚矣。然禮緣人情，樂隨風氣，而損益先王之舊，以備一代之
translation_en:
Third Question

Wang Zuo

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: This policy essay on governance and education concerns matters of great importance. The author understands human feelings and handles affairs well, without losing sight of the foundations of governance and education. He is a man fit for public service. What cause for shame could there be in recommending him highly?

Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: The policy essay offers practical measures, something only a person who understands moral principles and comprehends the affairs of the time could accomplish. Its selection is entirely appropriate.

Comment by Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He investigates the foundations of government and education and weighs what measures suit the circumstances. He may be said to understand the essentials of governance. Let him be singled out and selected.

For one who rules All under Heaven, nothing takes precedence over putting government in order and establishing education. Bringing government and education to fruition must rest upon instituting rites and creating music. For if government and education are not carried out, there can certainly be no talk of good order; yet if rites and music are not cultivated, what can provide the foundation for government and education? Can one who rules All under Heaven fail to understand what he must take as his foundation? In posing this question, you show that your expectations of this humble student’s usefulness in public service are far from slight. How could I fail to reply by drawing upon antiquity and taking the present as evidence?

Rites distinguish higher from lower, while music harmonizes the feelings of the people. The rites and music of Yu were rooted in the virtue of Emperor Shun, with Yi and Kui placed in charge. The three rites were cultivated and the five rites made clear; the six pitch standards were brought into accord and the eight classes of musical instruments harmonized. Later ages could certainly not surpass this. Yet rites accord with human feelings, and music follows prevailing customs; thus, adapting the inherited practices of the former kings by subtraction and addition, to complete the institutions of an age…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
制者不能不有待於周公也周之禮樂成於
周公之手而典以宗伯有五禮以親邦民六
樂以和神人後世固莫能加矣然聖王不作
禮樂廢壞而斟酌先王之制以爲萬世之法
者不能不有假於孔子也厥後嬴秦無道典
籍煨燼禮之亡也著者非一家若曾褒之漢
禮韋公肅之新儀王彥威之曲臺惟陳太常
之禮書辯論精博雖識者所愛然較之文公
家禮謹名分崇愛敬以爲之本畧浮文務本實
===
以爲之用者則不及焉今禮司於春官行於
朝廷之上者郁郁乎其盛可以匹休於虞周矣
而冠昏喪祭之典頒在有司燦然備具然民
間行之有未周者特以承亖者有未至而勢
未能革其因襲之弊也樂之亡也論者非一
葉若聶冠卿之樂圖胡瑗之樂記房庶之補
亡惟陳正字之樂書綱羅綜貫雖識者所許
然比之蔡氏新書本原器數之咸備辭約理
明之易曉者則未若焉今樂司於太常奏於
punctuated:
制者，不能不有待於周公也。周之禮樂成於周公之手，而典以宗伯，有五禮以親邦民，六樂以和神人，後世固莫能加矣。然聖王不作，禮樂廢壞，而斟酌先王之制以爲萬世之法者，不能不有假於孔子也。厥後嬴秦無道，典籍煨燼。禮之亡也，著者非一家，若曾褒之《漢禮》、韋公肅之《新儀》、王彥威之《曲臺》，惟陳太常之《禮書》，辯論精博，雖識者所愛，然較之文公《家禮》，謹名分、崇愛敬以爲之本，畧浮文、務本實以爲之用者，則不及焉。今禮司於春官，行於朝廷之上者，郁郁乎其盛，可以匹休於虞周矣。而冠昏喪祭之典，頒在有司，燦然備具。然民間行之有未周者，特以承亖者有未至，而勢未能革其因襲之弊也。

樂之亡也，論者非一葉，若聶冠卿之《樂圖》、胡瑗之《樂記》、房庶之《補亡》，惟陳正字之《樂書》，綱羅綜貫，雖識者所許，然比之蔡氏《新書》，本原器數之咸備、辭約理明之易曉者，則未若焉。今樂司於太常，奏於
translation_en:
…institutions necessarily had to await the Duke of Zhou. Zhou ritual and music were completed at his hands and placed under the Minister of Rites: the five rites brought the people of the realm into close relations, and the six musical performances harmonized spirits and human beings. Later ages certainly could not surpass them. Yet when sage kings no longer arose and ritual and music fell into decay, the task of weighing the institutions of the former kings and making them a standard for all ages necessarily required Confucius. Thereafter, the Qin of the Ying clan lacked the Way, and the canonical writings were reduced to ashes. After ritual learning was lost, more than one writer addressed it: examples include Zeng Bao’s Han Rites, Wei Gongsu’s New Ceremonies, and Wang Yanwei’s Terrace of Rites. Among these, Minister Chen of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices stood out for his Book of Rites, with its precise and wide-ranging discussions. Although discerning readers cherished it, it falls short of the Family Rituals of Lord Wen. That work takes scrupulous observance of status distinctions and the honoring of affection and reverence as its foundation, and makes its practical method the reduction of superficial ornament and attention to what is fundamental and substantial. Today, ritual is administered by the Ministry of Rites, and its observance at court is so splendid and flourishing that it can rival the glory of Yu and Zhou. The prescriptions for capping, marriage, funerals, and sacrifices have been promulgated to the responsible officials and are splendidly complete. Yet their practice among the people remains incomplete, simply because those charged with carrying them out [?] have not fully discharged their duties, and circumstances have not permitted the reform of abuses perpetuated by inherited practice.

After musical learning was lost, discussions of it extended over more than a single page [?]: examples include Nie Guanqing’s Diagrams of Music, Hu Yuan’s Record of Music, and Fang Shu’s Supplement to What Was Lost. Among these, Orthographer Chen’s Book of Music stood out for its comprehensive organization and synthesis. Although discerning readers commended it, it does not equal Master Cai’s New Book, which fully covers fundamental principles, instruments, and numerical relationships, and is readily understood because its language is concise and its reasoning clear. Today, music is administered by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and performed at…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之上一者洋洋乎其盛可以追美於韶武矣
而聲音器數之制布在有司井然有條然民
間之音律有未協者特以奉行者有未盡而
力亦未能振其諴和之俗也夫國以民為本
而民之師帥川守令也古之守令若龔遂之
化盜黃霸之寬和卓茂之愛民魯恭之三異
其見稱於世也尚矣今守令之選多出賢科
其於牧民之道視四子宜不多讓槩以才質
有高下民俗有淳漓況其間非棘而棼則寬而
===
漫其民力尚疲而卒戍之績未著者職此故
也國以兵為衛而兵之統御則將師也古之
將師若吳起之治兵王翦之善戰廉頗之勇
氣李牧之備邊其見稱於人也久矣今將師
之選類出世胄其於治兵之道視四子當有
所加槩以綺紈叙蔭之徒御夫游逸不練之
兵又加之以非貪而刻則縱而弛其智勇尚
少而決勝之策猶有未見者職此由也方今
聖天子在上而於禮樂兵民四者惓惓注意然而
punctuated:
朝廷之上一者，洋洋乎其盛，可以追美於韶武矣。而聲音器數之制，布在有司，井然有條。然民間之音律有未協者，特以奉行者有未盡，而力亦未能振其諴和之俗也。
夫國以民為本，而民之師帥川守令也。古之守令，若龔遂之化盜、黃霸之寬和、卓茂之愛民、魯恭之三異，其見稱於世也尚矣。今守令之選，多出賢科，其於牧民之道，視四子宜不多讓。槩以才質有高下，民俗有淳漓，況其間非棘而棼，則寬而漫。其民力尚疲，而卒戍之績未著者，職此故也。
國以兵為衛，而兵之統御則將師也。古之將師，若吳起之治兵、王翦之善戰、廉頗之勇氣、李牧之備邊，其見稱於人也久矣。今將師之選，類出世胄，其於治兵之道，視四子當有所加。槩以綺紈叙蔭之徒，御夫游逸不練之兵，又加之以非貪而刻，則縱而弛。其智勇尚少，而決勝之策猶有未見者，職此由也。
方今聖天子在上，而於禮樂兵民四者惓惓注意，然而
translation_en:
…at the imperial court [?], its abundant magnificence can rival the beauty of the Shao and Wu music. Regulations governing musical sounds, instruments, and numerical proportions have been distributed to the responsible offices and are systematically ordered. Yet musical pitches among the people remain imperfectly harmonized, simply because those charged with implementation have not fully carried out their duties, and their efforts have likewise failed to foster harmonious customs.
The state takes the people as its foundation, and the people's teachers and leaders are prefects and magistrates [?]. Among prefects and magistrates of antiquity were Gong Sui, who reformed bandits; Huang Ba, known for leniency and harmony; Zhuo Mao, who cherished the people; and Lu Gong, whose administration produced three extraordinary signs. Their acclaim in the world dates from long ago. Today, those selected as prefects and magistrates mostly come through the examinations for worthy men. In the art of governing the people, they should scarcely yield to these four masters. Yet their abilities and dispositions vary, and popular customs range from honest to corrupt. Moreover, some administer affairs with harsh urgency and confusion, while others are lenient and careless. This is precisely why the people's resources remain exhausted and achievements in garrison service have not become apparent [?].
The state takes soldiers as its protection, and generals command those soldiers. Among generals of antiquity were Wu Qi, skilled in managing troops; Wang Jian, adept in battle; Lian Po, renowned for courage; and Li Mu, accomplished in frontier defense. Their acclaim among men has endured for a long time. Today, those selected as generals mostly come from hereditary military families. In the art of managing troops, they ought to surpass these four masters in some respects. Yet these men, raised amid silks and appointed through hereditary privilege, command idle and untrained soldiers. Added to this, they are either grasping and harsh or indulgent and lax. This is precisely why wisdom and courage remain scarce among them and strategies for securing victory have yet to appear.
At present, the sagely Son of Heaven reigns above and devotes his earnest attention to these four matters: rites, music, soldiers, and the people. Yet …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
禮樂之用未盡周治民兵者未盡得人誠有
如執事之所慮者茲欲教民以禮當以文公
家禮申而明之使庠序日加講習而推及閭
閻之下薰陶日久自然成俗禮豈有不行者
乎茲欲教民以樂當以元定新書嚴而教之
俾學校詳加考究而達於鄉黨之間涵泳日
深自然成風樂豈有不用者乎至於治民也
惟在乎慎選守令使布列郡縣者能若程顥
之令晉城朱熹之知漳州則教化乎而黎元
===
自安何龔黄之徒難及乎治兵也惟在乎謹
擇將帥使統御中外者能如韓琦之宣撫陝
西仲淹之經畧環慶則武備脩而兵威自振
何頗牧之輩足數乎然爲政固莫先於教化
而禮樂又教化之本也禮樂有本有文本諸
敬以爲禮則禮得其體而當然之禮行本諸
和以爲樂則樂得其本而自然之和生矣夫
然則本末兼該禮樂畢舉政無不立俗無不
美而治化之隆何虞周之不可及哉謹對
punctuated: 禮樂之用未盡周，治民兵者未盡得人，誠有如執事之所慮者。茲欲教民以禮，當以文公家禮申而明之，使庠序日加講習，而推及閭閻之下，薰陶日久，自然成俗，禮豈有不行者乎？茲欲教民以樂，當以元定新書嚴而教之，俾學校詳加考究，而達於鄉黨之間，涵泳日深，自然成風，樂豈有不用者乎？至於治民也，惟在乎慎選守令，使布列郡縣者能若程顥之令晉城、朱熹之知漳州，則教化乎，而黎元自安，何龔黄之徒難及乎？治兵也，惟在乎謹擇將帥，使統御中外者能如韓琦之宣撫陝西、仲淹之經畧環慶，則武備脩，而兵威自振，何頗牧之輩足數乎？然爲政固莫先於教化，而禮樂又教化之本也。禮樂有本有文，本諸敬以爲禮，則禮得其體，而當然之禮行；本諸和以爲樂，則樂得其本，而自然之和生矣。夫然則本末兼該，禮樂畢舉，政無不立，俗無不美，而治化之隆，何虞周之不可及哉？謹對。
translation_en:
…the application of rites and music is not yet fully comprehensive, and those who govern the people and the troops are not all suitable men. Matters are indeed as you, honored examiners, fear. If we now wish to instruct the people in rites, we should expound and clarify them through Master Wengong’s Family Rituals, ensuring that local schools lecture on and practice them daily and extend this instruction to the common people in their neighborhoods. Through prolonged cultivation, these practices will naturally become customary. How could rites fail to be observed? If we now wish to instruct the people in music, we should teach it rigorously through Yuanding’s New Book, having the schools investigate it thoroughly and extend it throughout the local communities. As immersion in it deepens daily, it will naturally become established practice. How could music fail to be employed?

As for governing the people, the essential point is to select prefects and magistrates carefully. If those stationed throughout the prefectures and counties could emulate Cheng Hao as magistrate of Jincheng and Zhu Xi as prefect of Zhangzhou, moral instruction would [flourish?], and the common people would naturally live in peace. Why should men like Gong and Huang be difficult to equal? As for governing the troops, the essential point is to choose commanders carefully. If those commanding forces at court and in the provinces could emulate Han Qi as pacification commissioner in Shaanxi and Zhongyan as military commissioner in Huanqing, military preparations would be put in order and the army’s might would naturally be invigorated. Why would men like Lian Po and Li Mu even merit mention?

Yet in governing, nothing takes precedence over moral instruction, and rites and music are themselves its foundation. Rites and music have both a foundation and an outward expression. When rites are grounded in reverence, they attain their proper substance, and the observances that ought to be practiced are carried out. When music is grounded in harmony, it attains its foundation, and spontaneous harmony arises. In this way, root and branches would both be encompassed, and rites and music would be fully implemented. Every measure of government would be established, and every custom would become good. With governance and moral transformation thus flourishing, why should the achievements of Yu and Zhou be beyond our reach? Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
第四問
魯煥
同考試官訓道李批質諸經傳斷以義理有學之
士也
同考試官教諭韓批此策有考據而斷以理宜錄
考試官教諭吾批能答所問
考試官教諭趙批决未决之疑有識之士
道無往而不在雖聖人無不師理有疑而不
决在學者所當辨夫道之所存師之所在也
===
聖人之生不資於師而亦未嘗不取諸人以
為善賢人之學不能不資於師而亦未嘗無
自得之妙然而議論紛紜莫知所定學者其
可不稽之經傳斷之義理以求一定之說哉
請因明問而言之黃帝生而神靈長而聰
慧仰觀俯察作則垂憲顓頊淵與靜淵有
謀疏通達事帝嚳繼之聰以知逺明以察微
既執厥中民罔弗從以至堯舜禹湯文武皆
生知之聖而謂其學於大填録圖赤松子君

punctuated:
第四問
魯煥
同考試官訓道李批：「質諸經傳，斷以義理，有學之士也。」
同考試官教諭韓批：「此策有考據而斷以理，宜錄。」
