道無往而不在，雖聖人無不師；理有疑而不决，在學者所當辨。夫道之所存，師之所在也。聖人之生，不資於師，而亦未嘗不取諸人以為善；賢人之學，不能不資於師，而亦未嘗無自得之妙。然而議論紛紜，莫知所定，學者其可不稽之經傳，斷之義理，以求一定之說哉？請因明問而言之。黃帝生而神靈，長而聰慧，仰觀俯察，作則垂憲。顓頊淵與靜淵有謀，疏通達事。帝嚳繼之，聰以知逺，明以察微，既執厥中，民罔弗從。以至堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武，皆生知之聖，而謂其學於大填、録圖、赤松子、君
translation_en:
Fourth Question
Lu Huan

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, an Instructor [?]: “He tests his claims against the classics and their commentaries and judges them by moral principles. He is a man of learning.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, a School Instructor: “This policy essay draws on textual evidence and reaches judgments through principle. It merits acceptance.”

Comment by Examiner Wu, a School Instructor: “He can answer what was asked.”

Comment by Examiner Zhao, a School Instructor: “He resolves unresolved doubts: a man of discernment.”

The Way is present everywhere; even sages invariably learn from others. Where doubts about principle remain unresolved, it falls to students to distinguish what is correct. For wherever the Way resides, there resides a teacher. Sages, by birth, do not depend upon teachers, yet they have always drawn upon others to practice goodness. Worthy men, in their learning, cannot dispense with teachers, yet they too have the subtle capacity to attain understanding for themselves. Nevertheless, opinions proliferate, and no one knows what conclusion to adopt. How, then, could students fail to examine the classics and their commentaries and judge by moral principles, seeking a settled account? Allow me to address your illuminating question.

Huangdi was divinely perceptive from birth and intelligent as he grew. Looking upward and examining below, he established standards and handed down models. Zhuanxu was profound and tranquil, profound and resourceful [?], discerning and conversant with affairs. Di Ku succeeded him, perceptive enough to know what was distant and discerning enough to detect what was subtle. Once he upheld the Mean, none among the people failed to follow him. Down to Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and Kings Wen and Wu, all were sages who possessed knowledge from birth. Yet it is claimed that they studied under Da Tian, Lu Tu, Chisongzi, Jun…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
疇務成昭之輩西王國伯成子時子思郭叔
之徒雖曰載之傳記其果然耶夫自黃帝至
於武王皆以聖人之德居君師之位所以繼
天而立極者也其道統之傳心法之妙見諸
經傳者若帝嚳帝堯舜禹之執中成湯文武
之建中建極昭如日星矣今乃謂數聖人反
師於大填郭叔之徒蓋道之至也聖人有所
不知謂其師一端之善容或有之謂其學於
其門親授其業豈足信哉雖其說之出於孔
===
門高弟意好事者為之託子夏之名以取信
於人不然何其授受之旨經傳無一語以及
之耶此其不足信也明矣自是之後若孔子
之於老聃左丘明之於孔子公羊高穀梁赤
之於子夏孟子之於子思二程之於周子皆
謂之師弟子也或又謂其不然學者不能無
疑夫孔子之聖天理之純人道之極其於古
今名物制度沿革蓋亦於彼或有所詢如適
周問禮於老聃是孔子之無常師也而謂孔
punctuated:
疇、務成昭之輩，西王國、伯成子、時子思、郭叔之徒，雖曰載之傳記，其果然耶？夫自黃帝至於武王，皆以聖人之德居君師之位，所以繼天而立極者也。其道統之傳、心法之妙，見諸經傳者，若帝嚳、帝堯、舜、禹之執中，成湯、文武之建中建極，昭如日星矣。今乃謂數聖人反師於大填、郭叔之徒。蓋道之至也，聖人有所不知，謂其師一端之善，容或有之；謂其學於其門，親授其業，豈足信哉？雖其說之出於孔門高弟，意好事者為之，託子夏之名以取信於人。不然，何其授受之旨，經傳無一語以及之耶？此其不足信也明矣。

自是之後，若孔子之於老聃，左丘明之於孔子，公羊高、穀梁赤之於子夏，孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，皆謂之師弟子也。或又謂其不然，學者不能無疑。夫孔子之聖，天理之純，人道之極，其於古今名物制度沿革，蓋亦於彼或有所詢。如適周問禮於老聃，是孔子之無常師也，而謂孔
translation_en:
…Chou [the end of Jun Chou’s name], Wucheng Zhao, and their like, and such men as Xi Wangguo, Bocheng Zi, Shi Zisi, and Guo Shu—although these claims are said to be recorded in transmitted accounts, were they really so? From Huangdi to King Wu, all occupied the position of ruler and teacher by virtue of their sagely character, thereby carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the supreme standard. The transmission of their succession to the Way and the subtleties of their teachings of the mind, as manifested in the Classics and their commentaries—for example, Di Ku, Di Yao, Shun, and Yu holding fast to the mean, and Cheng Tang and Kings Wen and Wu establishing the mean and the supreme standard—are as bright as the sun and stars. Yet now it is claimed that these sages instead took men such as Da Tian and Guo Shu as their teachers. At the utmost reaches of the Way, even sages have things they do not know. To say that they learned some particular excellence from these men might perhaps be admissible; but to say that they studied under them and personally received their instruction—how could this be credible? Although the account is attributed to an eminent disciple of Confucius, I suspect that someone fond of fabricating stories composed it and borrowed Zixia’s name to win people’s trust. Otherwise, why do the Classics and their commentaries contain not a single word touching upon the substance of this transmission of teaching? Clearly, this account is unworthy of belief.

Thereafter, such relationships as those of Confucius to Lao Dan, Zuo Qiuming to Confucius, Gongyang Gao and Guliang Chi to Zixia, Mencius to Zisi, and the two Cheng brothers to Master Zhou have all been called relationships between disciple and teacher. Others deny that this was so, and students cannot help harboring doubts. The sagehood of Confucius embodied the purity of Heaven’s principle and the highest perfection of the human Way. As for the names and particulars of things, institutions, and their changes through ancient and recent times, he too presumably had occasion to make inquiries of others. His journey to Zhou to ask Lao Dan about ritual, for example, illustrates that Confucius had no fixed teacher. Yet to say that Confucius…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
子爲老聃弟子豈不妄哉至若左氏公穀之
所傳受實得孔子子夏而爲宗師然春秋一
書褒貶是非撥亂反正人道之大綱王法之
所寓以卜氏之賢當筆削之際尚無一辭之
可賛彼左氏之傳果能得其奥旨而不失之
誣哉以親炙之丘明而尚有所失況公穀去
聖既遠顧欲立傳以明乎經是亦不免有所
失也又何名家之有哉使二子能知子夏所
以不敢賛經□□亦未敢輕爲立傳以取
===
謬妄之譏是又□□即其所學而遂疑其師
授也他如孟子之於子思二程之於周子是
皆亞聖大賢之資而又難以左氏公穀例也
且孟子以命世亞聖之才受業子思之門故
思誠之語與中庸同符而合轍也二程負特
立之材學於周子之門實始尊信庸學爲之
表章斥二家似是之非續千載不傳之緒俾
吾道之明如日麗天其學雖出周子而得於
經者爲多其與孟子息邪說正人心之功同
punctuated: 子爲老聃弟子，豈不妄哉？至若左氏、公穀之所傳受，實得孔子、子夏而爲宗師。然《春秋》一書，褒貶是非，撥亂反正，人道之大綱，王法之所寓。以卜氏之賢，當筆削之際，尚無一辭之可賛。彼左氏之傳，果能得其奥旨而不失之誣哉？以親炙之丘明而尚有所失，況公穀去聖既遠，顧欲立傳以明乎經，是亦不免有所失也。又何名家之有哉？使二子能知子夏所以不敢賛經，□□亦未敢輕爲立傳，以取謬妄之譏。是又□□即其所學而遂疑其師授也。他如孟子之於子思，二程之於周子，是皆亞聖大賢之資，而又難以左氏、公穀例也。且孟子以命世亞聖之才，受業子思之門，故思誠之語與《中庸》同符而合轍也。二程負特立之材，學於周子之門，實始尊信《庸》《學》，爲之表章，斥二家似是之非，續千載不傳之緒，俾吾道之明如日麗天。其學雖出周子，而得於經者爲多，其與孟子息邪說、正人心之功同
translation_en:
…to call Kongzi a disciple of Lao Dan—is this not absurd? As for the teachings transmitted to Zuo and to Gongyang and Guliang, they did indeed take Kongzi and Zixia as their authoritative teachers. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals, in its praise and censure of right and wrong and its restoration of order amid disorder, contains the great guiding principles of human conduct and embodies the laws of true kingship. Even someone as worthy as Master Bu [Zixia], when the text was being revised, could not contribute a single word. Could Zuo’s commentary really have grasped its profound meaning without lapsing into misrepresentation? If even Qiuming, who received instruction in person, still made mistakes, how much more must Gongyang and Guliang, already far removed from the sage, have done so when they undertook to establish commentaries to elucidate the classic? They too could not avoid errors. What claim, then, could they have to standing as authoritative interpreters? Had these two understood why Zixia did not dare contribute to the classic, [two illegible characters; connection uncertain] they too would not have dared rashly to compose commentaries and thus incur criticism for error and absurdity. Here again, [two illegible characters; connection uncertain] to examine what they learned and thereupon doubt their transmission from their teachers [?].

Other cases, such as Mengzi’s relationship to Zisi and the two Cheng brothers’ relationship to Master Zhou, involve men endowed with the qualities of a second sage or great worthies; it is difficult to judge them by the precedent of Zuo, Gongyang, and Guliang. Mengzi, with the talents of a second sage destined to appear in his age, received instruction in Zisi’s school. Thus his words on striving for sincerity tally exactly with the Doctrine of the Mean. The two Cheng brothers, endowed with exceptional abilities, studied in Master Zhou’s school. They were indeed the first to revere and trust the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning and to bring them to prominence. They rejected the specious errors of the two schools [Buddhism and Daoism] and renewed the line of transmission that had been broken for a thousand years, making our Way shine as brightly as the sun in the heavens. Although their learning originated with Master Zhou, they derived more of it from the classics. Their achievement accorded with Mengzi’s in putting an end to pernicious teachings and rectifying people’s hearts…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
一揆也此伊川所以謂其得不傳之學於遺
經孟子之後一人而已故朱子之序庸學亦
直以程子而繼孟子也耶管見區區未能究
其源流以袪古今之疑惟進而教之
第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃　批〔敘江西之風俗人物歷歷指　掌末復以師先哲爲言非博學有志者不能得〕
〔士如斯其難養之效歟〕
===
同考試官教諭屠　批〔此策有事實有發揚有歸宿　博洽之士也〕
同考試官教諭桂　批〔答者徒知誇美風俗人物之　盛而不知以名節道德爲尚此作能景行先哲其　有志者歟〕
同考試官學正張　批〔此策乃究實跡者易而居德　善俗者難多見出衆見無如此作故錄之〕
考試官教諭吾　批〔風俗人物鋪敘殆盡且師古　善俗之志藹然言表可嘉可嘉〕
punctuated:
一揆也。此伊川所以謂其得不傳之學於遺經，孟子之後一人而已。故朱子之序《庸》《學》，亦直以程子而繼孟子也耶？管見區區，未能究其源流，以袪古今之疑，惟進而教之。
第五問
蕭昇
同考試官教諭黃批〔敘江西之風俗人物，歷歷指掌，末復以師先哲爲言，非博學有志者不能得。〕〔士如斯，其難養之效歟？〕
同考試官教諭屠批〔此策有事實，有發揚，有歸宿，博洽之士也。〕
同考試官教諭桂批〔答者徒知誇美風俗人物之盛，而不知以名節道德爲尚。此作能景行先哲，其有志者歟？〕
同考試官學正張批〔此策乃究實跡者易，而居德善俗者難。多見出衆，見無如此作，故錄之。〕
考試官教諭吾批〔風俗人物鋪敘殆盡，且師古善俗之志，藹然言表，可嘉！可嘉！〕
translation_en:
…are of the same order. This is why Yichuan said that he had recovered the learning whose transmission had been lost from the surviving classics, and was the sole person to have done so since Mengzi. Is this also why Master Zhu, in his prefaces to the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning, placed Master Cheng directly in succession to Mengzi? My limited understanding has not enabled me to trace their origins and development and thereby dispel doubts ancient and modern. I ask only that you come forward and instruct me.
Fifth Question
Xiao Sheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔He describes Jiangxi’s customs and notable figures with the clarity of something displayed in the palm of his hand. At the end he also speaks of taking earlier worthies as his teachers. Only someone broadly learned and possessed of resolve could achieve this.〕〔A scholar such as this—is he the fruit of painstaking cultivation?〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Tu, Instructor: 〔This policy essay contains factual substance, develops its themes, and reaches a definite conclusion. Its author is a scholar of extensive learning.〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Gui, Instructor: 〔Those answering merely know how to extol flourishing customs and abundant talent, without knowing to esteem integrity and moral virtue. This composition shows an ability to emulate earlier worthies. Surely its author is a man of resolve!〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, School Instructor: 〔The point of this policy essay is that investigating actual deeds is easy, whereas abiding in virtue and improving customs is difficult. I have seen many outstanding works, but none like this composition [?]; therefore I have selected it for inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔His exposition of customs and notable figures is nearly exhaustive. Moreover, his aspiration to learn from antiquity and improve customs is abundantly evident in his words. Commendable! Commendable!〕

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭趙　批〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上〕
〔抱奇器之士也士風不爲之倚重乎〕
橐籥之中以倡以化而天下之風俗所由美
陶冶之內以感以興而天下之人物所由盛
此
國家氣運之隆治化之美超越於往古也尚矣
然輿圖之廣在在皆然而江西特一大方也
為郡一十有三統邑六十有九在禹貢隷揚
州之域在天文屬斗牛之墟山有匡廬之秀
===
特水有彭蠡之環匯其間風俗之異人物之
盛誠有關於
國家之氣化者安得不爽執事之問哉愚也
生長是地得之父師考之圖志竊有所知
敢不為執事陳之以言其風俗也南昌在
藩省之中而饒州與之相屬一則講誦為
業而衣冠萃止一則忠孝繼出而文物相
續廣信居藩省之東而南康為其接壤一
則矜謹節義而士風貧薄一則淳固慤實有
punctuated:
考試官教諭趙批〔生斯邦而尚友於千古之上〕〔抱奇器之士也，士風不爲之倚重乎？〕

橐籥之中，以倡以化，而天下之風俗所由美；陶冶之內，以感以興，而天下之人物所由盛。此國家氣運之隆、治化之美，超越於往古也，尚矣！然輿圖之廣，在在皆然，而江西特一大方也。為郡一十有三，統邑六十有九。在禹貢隷揚州之域，在天文屬斗牛之墟。山有匡廬之秀特，水有彭蠡之環匯。其間風俗之異、人物之盛，誠有關於國家之氣化者，安得不爽執事之問哉？愚也生長是地，得之父師，考之圖志，竊有所知，敢不為執事陳之？以言其風俗也，南昌在藩省之中，而饒州與之相屬，一則講誦為業而衣冠萃止，一則忠孝繼出而文物相續。廣信居藩省之東，而南康為其接壤，一則矜謹節義而士風貧薄，一則淳固慤實，有
translation_en:
Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔Born in this land, he seeks fellowship with worthy men across the ages.〕〔He is a scholar endowed with exceptional capacities. Does not the ethos of scholars gain standing through him?〕

Within the bellows of transformation, guidance and moral instruction make the customs of the realm admirable; within its molding and refining, inspiration and encouragement bring forth an abundance of outstanding men throughout the realm. Such is the flourishing vital fortune of the state and the excellence of its transformative governance: they surpass antiquity. How exalted! Throughout the vast territory of the realm, this is everywhere so; Jiangxi is but one great region within it. It comprises thirteen prefectures, administering sixty-nine counties. In the Tribute of Yu, it falls within the territory of Yangzhou; in celestial geography, it belongs to the region of the Dipper and Ox lodges. Among its mountains is the singular beauty of Kuanglu; among its waters, the encircling confluence of Pengli. The distinctive customs and abundance of outstanding men here are indeed bound up with the transforming vital forces of the state. How could I fail to answer your question [?]?

I, in my ignorance, was born and raised in this land. Through what I have learned from my father and teachers and investigated in maps and gazetteers, I have acquired some knowledge. How could I presume not to set it before you? To speak of its customs: Nanchang lies in the center of the province, and Raozhou adjoins it. In the former, lecturing and recitation are pursued as a vocation, and men of scholarly standing congregate; in the latter, loyal and filial men emerge in succession, and cultural accomplishments continue unbroken. Guangxin lies in the east of the province, and Nankang borders it. In the former, integrity and righteousness are carefully upheld, yet the ethos of its scholars is impoverished and meager [?]; in the latter, the people are steadfastly simple, sincere, and honest, possessing …

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
先儒遺風至於士習詩書而農不勤稼穡風□
和平而人物秀麗者非九江與建昌乎風流
儒雅而民樂耕桑崇德尚禮而勤力知分者
非撫州與臨江乎瑞之吏民朴野而不嚚於
訟袁之廉恥愈嚴而事不煩此二郡之風俗
不同也贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節南安
則民習淳古而士果於義此又二郡之風俗各
異也至於人尨淳而多壽考家詩書而口庠
塾其吉安之風俗何厚哉以言乎人物也徐
===
樨非其力不食陳蕃稱為南州高士黃庭堅
為江西詩宗蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表致力中
原陶侃之運甓以自勵克定大計趙汝愚之謀
國不顧身此南昌饒州之人物也可知矣身
歸國棄大用受金牌之賜□□□□□□得
獲全婦之安保衛鄉閭鄒元靖有□□□才
請救襄樊江萬里以峭直見忌此廣信南康
之人物也可見九江建昌則有周訪之沉
毅果斷陶潛之恥身後代與夫曾鞏齊名
punctuated:
先儒遺風。至於士習詩書而農不勤稼穡，風□和平而人物秀麗者，非九江與建昌乎？風流儒雅而民樂耕桑，崇德尚禮而勤力知分者，非撫州與臨江乎？瑞之吏民朴野而不嚚於訟，袁之廉恥愈嚴而事不煩，此二郡之風俗不同也。贛州則伉健工巧而抗志勵節，南安則民習淳古而士果於義，此又二郡之風俗各異也。至於人尨淳而多壽考，家詩書而口庠塾，其吉安之風俗何厚哉！
以言乎人物也，徐樨非其力不食，陳蕃稱為南州高士；黃庭堅為江西詩宗，蘇軾嘆其獨立於物表。致力中原，陶侃之運甓以自勵；克定大計，趙汝愚之謀國不顧身。此南昌、饒州之人物也，可知矣。身歸國，棄大用，受金牌之賜，□□□□□□得獲全婦之安；保衛鄉閭，鄒元靖有□□□才；請救襄樊，江萬里以峭直見忌。此廣信、南康之人物也，可見。九江、建昌則有周訪之沉毅果斷，陶潛之恥身後代，與夫曾鞏齊名
translation_en:
…the legacy of earlier Confucian masters. As for places where scholars study the Odes and Documents but farmers are not diligent in cultivating their crops, where the customs [illegible] are peaceable and the people outstanding and refined—are these not Jiujiang and Jianchang? Where cultivated elegance and Confucian refinement prevail and the people delight in farming and sericulture, where virtue is revered and ritual esteemed, and people work diligently and know their station—are these not Fuzhou and Linjiang? In Rui, officials and commoners are plain and rustic, without contentiousness in litigation; in Yuan, standards of integrity and shame are still stricter, and affairs are uncomplicated. These are the differences in the customs of those two prefectures. In Ganzhou, people are vigorous and skilled in craftsmanship, lofty in aspiration and resolute in integrity. In Nan’an, the people’s habits retain an ancient simplicity, and scholars act decisively for righteousness. Here again, the customs of the two prefectures differ. As for people being simple and honest [?] and often reaching a venerable age, every household studying the Odes and Documents and every mouth speaking of schools [?]—how substantial are the customs of Ji’an!
Turning to notable people: Xu Xi [?] would eat nothing that he had not earned through his own labor, and Chen Fan called him an eminent scholar of the southern region. Huang Tingjian was the patriarch of Jiangxi poetry, and Su Shi marveled at how he stood alone above worldly things. Devoting his efforts to the Central Plain, Tao Kan carried bricks to discipline himself; settling the great affairs of state, Zhao Ruyu planned for the realm without regard for his own safety. From these examples, the notable people of Nanchang and Raozhou may be known. He returned in person to the state, relinquished high employment, and received the gift of a gold tablet; [six illegible characters] secured the safety of preserving a woman [?]. Defending the villages, Zou Yuanjing possessed [three illegible characters] talent. Jiang Wanli urged that Xiangyang and Fancheng be relieved, but incurred resentment for his uncompromising uprightness. From these examples, the notable people of Guangxin and Nankang may be seen. Jiujiang and Jianchang have Zhou Fang, with his composure, fortitude, and decisiveness; Tao Qian, who considered it shameful to live under a succeeding dynasty; and Zeng Gong, who shared equal renown with…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
於歐陽陳宗禮之直言清節者焉撫州臨江則
有陸九淵之講明道學吳澂之力學聖賢與
夫陳喬以社稷爲己任劉清之之博極群書者
焉他如劉恕篤好史學陳仲微涵飫六經廖
洪之孝築墳塋陳重之友堅膠漆非瑞袁之
人物乎李朴之操履勁特曾開之大節不奪
盧汝舟之廉約守正田闢之嗜學不倦非贛
南之人物乎以至盡心匡直文章與韓愈並
稱歐陽脩一代之宗也死不屈節而父子相
===
繼楊邦乂名世之人也胡銓之力排和議劾
奸一疏與日月以爭光文天祥之九死不悔
正氣一歌與宇宙相爲悠久其吉安之人物
何盛哉然風俗之美於今者無以異乎古人
物之盛乎古者何有間於今故今之節行文
章濟濟相望功名事業燁燁馳聲愚固未暇
以縷數惟於一風俗師先哲之意竊亦有志
不敢無言夫欲一風俗莫先於明禮義而
養廉恥戒浮靡而崇節儉其所以化導之
punctuated:
於歐陽、陳宗禮之直言清節者焉。撫州、臨江則有陸九淵之講明道學、吳澂之力學聖賢，與夫陳喬以社稷爲己任、劉清之之博極群書者焉。他如劉恕篤好史學，陳仲微涵飫六經，廖洪之孝築墳塋，陳重之友堅膠漆，非瑞、袁之人物乎？李朴之操履勁特，曾開之大節不奪，盧汝舟之廉約守正，田闢之嗜學不倦，非贛、南之人物乎？以至盡心匡直，文章與韓愈並稱，歐陽脩一代之宗也；死不屈節，而父子相繼，楊邦乂名世之人也。胡銓之力排和議，劾奸一疏與日月以爭光；文天祥之九死不悔，《正氣》一歌與宇宙相爲悠久。其吉安之人物何盛哉！
然風俗之美於今者，無以異乎古；人物之盛乎古者，何有間於今？故今之節行文章，濟濟相望；功名事業，燁燁馳聲。愚固未暇以縷數，惟於一風俗、師先哲之意，竊亦有志，不敢無言。夫欲一風俗，莫先於明禮義而養廉恥，戒浮靡而崇節儉。其所以化導之
translation_en:
…with Ouyang, and Chen Zongli, with his forthright speech and unsullied integrity. In Fuzhou and Linjiang there were Lu Jiuyuan, who expounded the Learning of the Way; Wu Cheng, who diligently studied the teachings of the sages and worthies; Chen Qiao, who took responsibility for the altars of soil and grain; and Liu Qingzhi, whose extensive learning encompassed the whole range of books. Others included Liu Shu, deeply devoted to historical scholarship; Chen Zhongwei, thoroughly steeped in the Six Classics; Liao Hong, whose filial devotion found expression in building a tomb; and Chen Zhong, whose friendship was as firm as glue and lacquer. Were these not men of Ruizhou and Yuanzhou? Li Pu was resolute and distinctive in his conduct; Zeng Kai could not be shaken in his integrity on great matters; Lu Ruzhou was incorruptible, frugal, and steadfast in rectitude; and Tian Pi was tireless in his love of learning. Were these not men of Ganzhou and Nan’an? Then there was Ouyang Xiu, who devoted himself wholeheartedly to correction and remonstrance, and whose writings were ranked alongside those of Han Yu: he was the literary master of his age. Yang Bangyi, who died without compromising his integrity, father and son following one another in this, was a man renowned in his time. Hu Quan vigorously opposed peace negotiations; his single memorial impeaching the treacherous rivaled the sun and moon in brilliance. Wen Tianxiang remained unrepentant even in the face of repeated mortal peril; his Song of Righteous Qi endures as long as the universe. How abundant were the outstanding men of Ji’an!
Yet the excellence of customs today is no different from that of antiquity; how could antiquity’s abundance of outstanding men surpass that of today? Thus today, men distinguished for integrity, conduct, and literary achievement appear in impressive succession, while their meritorious accomplishments and undertakings spread their brilliant renown. I have certainly had no leisure to enumerate them individually. Yet I, too, privately aspire to the purpose of unifying customs and taking former worthies as teachers, and dare not remain silent. To unify customs, nothing takes precedence over clarifying ritual propriety and righteousness, nurturing incorruptibility and a sense of shame, guarding against frivolous extravagance, and honoring frugality. As for the means by which the people are transformed and guided…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
者固當造端乎民牧所以鼓舞而倡率之則又
在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳若夫靖節之介
得其正文忠公之文本於德文安文正之學
根乎道此道德文章之可師也澹菴憂中興
之社稷信國決萬世之綱常此功名節義之
可師也為士者誠能師先哲以脩己寄民社
者又能師先哲以化民則民風之所以淳者
在是士風之所以正者在是人物之所以盛
者亦在是愚也不敏倘蒙與進俾得以行其
言敢不景行先哲以副執事之望謹對
punctuated: 者，固當造端乎民牧；所以鼓舞而倡率之，則又在乎士夫君子之用心何如耳。若夫靖節之介，得其正；文忠公之文，本於德；文安、文正之學，根乎道：此道德文章之可師也。澹菴憂中興之社稷，信國決萬世之綱常：此功名節義之可師也。為士者誠能師先哲以脩己，寄民社者又能師先哲以化民，則民風之所以淳者在是，士風之所以正者在是，人物之所以盛者亦在是。愚也不敏，倘蒙與進，俾得以行其言，敢不景行先哲，以副執事之望？謹對。
translation_en: …such moral guidance should certainly begin with the local magistrates; how the people are encouraged and led by example depends, in turn, on how scholar-officials and gentlemen apply themselves. Jingjie’s integrity accorded with what was right; Lord Wenzhong’s writing was founded on virtue; and the learning of Wen’an and Wenzheng was rooted in the Way. These are examples to emulate in morality and literary accomplishment. Dan’an concerned himself with the altars of soil and grain during the dynastic restoration; the Duke of Xinguo made his decisive stand for the cardinal bonds and enduring moral norms of all ages. These are examples to emulate in achievement, integrity, and righteousness. If scholars can truly emulate these earlier worthies in cultivating themselves, and those entrusted with the people and their communities can likewise emulate them in transforming the people, herein lies the means to make popular customs wholesome, the conduct of scholars upright, and outstanding men abundant. Unworthy and slow of understanding though I am, should I be granted advancement and thereby enabled to put my words into practice, how could I fail to follow the lofty example of these earlier worthies and fulfill your expectations? Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
江西蔚爲東南鉅服英賢之
生萃焉發于漢唐盛于有宋
而尤盛于我
朝我以文學鳴我以政事顯或
以忠烈震撼轟天地煥爛簡
冊海宇之廣人材之彬彬推
===
先焉況自我
朝追今踵大拜者垂百數年連
大魁者踰十數人雖其所樹
立有隆有庳然至於大貽謂
於時者尠矣於戲誠盛矣哉
乃今成化十三年實維大比
之秋合列郡之士幾三千人
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

江西蔚爲東南鉅服，英賢之生萃焉，發于漢唐，盛于有宋，而尤盛于我朝。我以文學鳴，我以政事顯，或以忠烈震撼轟天地，煥爛簡冊。海宇之廣，人材之彬彬，推先焉。況自我朝追今，踵大拜者垂百數，年連大魁者踰十數人。雖其所樹立有隆有庳，然至於大貽謂於時者尠矣。於戲，誠盛矣哉！

乃今成化十三年，實維大比之秋，合列郡之士幾三千人。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Jiangxi has flourished as a great region of the southeast, where outstanding and worthy men are born in abundance. Their emergence began under the Han and Tang, flourished under the Song, and has flourished still more under our dynasty. Some have won renown through literary learning, others distinction through government service [?]; still others, through loyalty and heroic sacrifice, have shaken heaven and earth and shone brilliantly in the historical records. Across the vast empire, amid its abundance of cultivated talent, Jiangxi is accorded foremost place. Moreover, from the beginning of our dynasty down to the present [?], those who have successively received high appointments number nearly a hundred, while more than ten men have taken first place in the examinations in successive years [?]. Although their achievements have varied in stature, few have incurred grave reproach from their contemporaries [?]. Ah, how truly flourishing!

Now, in the thirteenth year of Chenghua [1477], the autumn of the triennial examination, nearly three thousand candidates from the various prefectures have assembled…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
三試之自監臨以暨內外諸
執事既皆殫力防範周
詳昇等濫竽考官敢不精白
一心以公去取於是擇其文
之中式者遵
□制得九十五人登之賢書獻之
□□□□手稽首爲
===
□人賀復僭序諸小錄爲
登名諸君子告焉夫江右人
材於今固盛矣而其所以盛
諸君子容不知所勉哉勉之
唯無負
天之所以命我者之大而遜其第
一等者於人以文學鳴必爲
punctuated:
三試之。自監臨以暨內外諸執事，既皆殫力，防範周詳，昇等濫竽，考官敢不精白一心，以公去取？於是擇其文之中式者，遵□制，得九十五人，登之賢書，獻之□□□□手稽首，爲□人賀。復僭序諸小錄，爲登名諸君子告焉。
夫江右人材於今固盛矣，而其所以盛，諸君子容不知所勉哉？勉之，唯無負天之所以命我者之大，而遜其第一等者於人。以文學鳴，必爲
translation_en:
…They were examined in three sessions. From the Supervising Official to all functionaries serving within and outside the examination compound, everyone exerted himself fully, taking thorough precautions. The passage concerning advancement in rank and unqualified candidates is unclear [?]. How could the Examiners dare not purify their minds and devote themselves single-heartedly to impartial selection and rejection? Accordingly, we selected those whose compositions met the prescribed standard and, in accordance with the □ regulations, obtained ninety-five men. We entered them in the register of worthies and presented them to [illegible]. With hands [unclear] and heads bowed to the ground, we offered congratulations to □ persons [?]. I have further presumed to write a preface to this modest record, addressing these remarks to the gentlemen whose names appear in it.
Talent in Jiangyou is indeed abundant today. Yet can you gentlemen fail to understand what you must strive for if that abundance is to be sustained? Strive, then: do not fail the greatness of the charge Heaven has entrusted to you, or yield the foremost rank to others. If you win renown through literary learning, you must…

title: 成化十三年江西鄉試錄
text:
往聖繼絕學爲萬世開太平
斯第一流之文學歟以政事
顯必爲天地立心爲生民立
命斯第一流之政事歟忠烈
自文學政事中事無庸言已
若然則諸君子負挾之弘建
千豈徒爲當今人物將
===
□虞三代人物等而我
□雍熙泰和之治所以登三
□后五者亦將愈遠彌隆矣
主司深望實在于茲唯諸君
子副之
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開
化吾昇謹序
punctuated:
往聖繼絕學，爲萬世開太平，斯第一流之文學歟？以政事顯，必爲天地立心，爲生民立命，斯第一流之政事歟？忠烈，自文學政事中事，無庸言已。若然，則諸君子負挾之弘、建千，豈徒爲當今人物？將□虞三代人物等，而我□雍熙泰和之治，所以登三□后五者，亦將愈遠彌隆矣。主司深望，實在于茲，唯諸君子副之。
應天府江浦縣儒學教諭開化吾昇謹序。
translation_en:
…to carry on the interrupted learning of the sages of old and inaugurate lasting peace for ten thousand generations: would this not be scholarship of the highest order? If you attain distinction in government service, you must establish a heart for Heaven and Earth and secure a life’s mandate for the people: would this not be government service of the highest order? Loyalty and heroic devotion are themselves integral to scholarship and government service; there is no need to discuss them separately. If this is so, then, through the breadth of what you gentlemen possess and the achievements you establish [?], how could you merely become distinguished figures of the present age? You will rank alongside the figures of [Tang?] and Yu and the Three Dynasties. And our [illegible] reign of radiant concord and supreme harmony, by which we rise to the Three and surpass the Five [?], will extend ever farther and grow ever more exalted. Here, indeed, lie the earnest hopes of those presiding over the examination. May you gentlemen fulfill them.
Preface respectfully composed by Wu Sheng 吾昇 of Kaihua, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture.
